articles.headline: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin meet in China ahead of summit
articles.title: Trump shakes hands with Putin and Xi ahead of historic talks in China
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Wednesday before a historic Asia-Pacific summit in China. The leaders are expected to hold talks on Thursday regarding global conflicts including Ukraine and Iran, alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping. The meeting marks the first in-person encounter between Trump and Putin since August 2025.
articles.description: The three leaders will meet together for the first time on Thursday during a closely-watched summit.

articles.headline: Iran army targets United States base in Kuwait with drones
articles.title: Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets Bahrain amid wider Gulf attacks
articles.summary: The Iranian military stated on November 18, 2026, that it launched drone strikes against the United States Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait, activating regional air defences. Kuwaiti authorities confirmed their military intercepted incoming aerial threats and the foreign ministry strongly condemned the assault. This development follows previous strikes and ongoing Middle East tensions.
articles.description: Iran said its recent attacks — including those on other U.S. facilities in Bahrain on November 15 and November 13 — were in response to U.S. drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers

articles.headline: Kuwait and Bahrain repel overnight Iranian drone attacks amid rising regional hostilities
articles.title: Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months after US strikes island
articles.summary: Kuwait and Bahrain reported intercepting Iranian air attacks overnight, marking a new escalation in ongoing regional hostilities. The drone strike in Kuwait targeted an airbase hosting American forces without causing damage, following United States strikes on an Iranian missile site. Meanwhile, an oil tanker was attacked in the Strait of Oman, leaving one crew member missing and raising widespread fears of a broader conflict.
articles.description: Bahrain says it was also attacked by Iran following a US air strike on the Iranian island of Qeshm in the Gulf on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Trump arrives in China ahead of trilateral summit with Xi, Putin
articles.title: Trump arrives in China ahead of trilateral summit with Xi, Putin
articles.description: US President Donald Trump was greeted by Chinese President Xi Jinping as he arrived in China.

articles.headline: Gulf nations repel aerial attacks following United States strikes
articles.title: Bahrain, Kuwait attacked after U.S. strikes Iranian island
articles.summary: Bahrain and Kuwait announced on November 18, 2026, the successful interception of air attacks launched in the wake of United States strikes on Iranian territory. The widening conflict involves retaliatory drone and missile operations targeting facilities used by Washington across the region, while diplomats also address separate security allegations and upcoming trilateral summits.

articles.headline: Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen ahead of trilateral summit
articles.title: Xi, Putin meet ahead of historic Trump trilateral summit
articles.summary: Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin convened in Shenzhen on November 18, 2026, ahead of a scheduled three-way summit with United States President Donald Trump. According to Russian and Chinese officials, the discussions focused on bilateral relations, regional security, and global trade ahead of the wider Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation gathering.
articles.description: Washington had signalled that Ukraine — something Mr. Xi vehemently sees as not China's problem — was not expected to be addressed, before Mr. Trump said that it would

articles.headline: Modi attends regional summits in Manila and proposes maritime and trade initiatives
articles.title: World needs peace, stability, predictability: Modi in Manila
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the ASEAN-India Summit, the East Asia Summit, and the Quad Leaders’ Summit in Manila, Philippines. During the meetings, he proposed a seafarers’ safety initiative and free e-visas for ASEAN tourists while calling for global peace and stability. Hosted by U.S. President Donald Trump, the Quad leaders issued a joint statement opposing maritime coercion and announced the upcoming Quad Business Forum in Mumbai.
articles.description: Quad leaders issue joint statement opposing economic and maritime 'coercion' in Indo-Pacific; Modi proposes seafarers’ safety initiative at East Asia Summit, also attends meeting with ASEAN leaders

articles.headline: Kuwait reports drone attacks as US and Iran trade strikes
articles.title: Kuwait reports drone attacks as Iran, US trade attacks on Qeshm and Bahrain
articles.summary: Kuwaiti military forces stated on Tuesday that the Gulf nation faced hostile drone strikes while the United States and Iran exchanged military blows on Qeshm island and in Bahrain. The incidents follow ongoing regional tensions and shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, where multiple oil tankers have recently been struck.
articles.description: Kuwait's military says its air defence was repelling drones as Iran and the US hit out at each other across the Gulf.

articles.headline: Kyiv bridges struck in Russian missile attack as conflict continues
articles.title: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
articles.summary: Two major bridges spanning the Dnipro River in Kyiv were struck by Russian ballistic missiles, disrupting local water and power supplies according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko. The overnight attack occurred as Ukrainian, United States, and European officials engaged in diplomatic talks regarding the conflict, and followed separate Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Bridge connecting Russia to occupied Crimea.
articles.description: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.

articles.headline: Trump arrives in the Philippines for regional summits and upcoming talks with Xi and Putin
articles.title: Trump in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump arrived in Manila for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit and met with Quad partners including Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese. Following his stay in the Philippines, Trump is scheduled to fly to Shenzhen, China, to attend an Asia-Pacific leaders summit and hold nuclear discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
articles.description: The US president said he would be open to a one-on-one meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin "if it's available".

articles.headline: Trump warns Iran over reported ‘dirty bomb’ threat plans against Washington
articles.title: Trump warns Iran over reported ‘dirty bomb’ threat plans against Washington
articles.description: President Donald Trump responded to a CNN report that Iran was working on plans to attack Washington, DC

articles.headline: ‘Unprecedented’ Ukraine attack on Crimean bridge
articles.title: ‘Unprecedented’ Ukraine attack on Crimean bridge
articles.description: Ukraine has struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Russian-annexed Crimea for a second day.

articles.headline: Madras High Court bars Tamil Nadu government from opening new liquor shops
articles.title: HC directs State government not to open any new Tasmac liquor shops in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court ordered the Tamil Nadu government not to open any new Tasmac liquor shops across the state. Justices P. Velmurugan and K.K. Ramakrishnan issued the directive while allowing a public interest litigation petition regarding a proposed outlet in Tiruchi district, citing public interest, student safety, and community concerns over existing alcohol availability.

articles.headline: Israeli forces launch new military operation in central Gaza
articles.title: Israeli forces launch new military operation in central Gaza
articles.description: Israeli forces have launched a new military operation in central Gaza, advancing west of the Yellow Line

articles.headline: Sajjan Singh Yadav takes charge as new Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir
articles.title: IAS officer Sajjan Singh Yadav assumes charge as Chief Secretary of J&K
articles.summary: Senior Indian Administrative Service officer Sajjan Singh Yadav formally assumed office as the Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir. Officials welcomed the 1995-batch officer at the Civil Secretariat in Jammu. Yadav joins the Union Territory administration with extensive multi-sectoral experience, facing critical pending administrative files including daily wager regularisation and reservation rationalisation.
articles.description: He joins at a time when the Chief Secretary post acts as the main interface between the Lok Bhavan and the Chief Minister’s office in the Union Territory (UT)

articles.headline: Karnataka government restructures Bengaluru City Police into five new commissionerates
articles.title: Bengaluru City Police restructured; five Commissioners and a Chief Commissioner appointed
articles.summary: The Karnataka government restructured the Bengaluru City Police by establishing five independent commissionerates led by inspector-general rank officers and appointing a Chief Commissioner to oversee operations. Additional Director-General of Police R. Hithendra took charge as Chief Commissioner. The administrative overhaul aims to improve law enforcement supervision across the expanding metropolitan jurisdiction.
articles.description: R. Hithendra appointed the new Chief Commissioner of Bengaluru City Police

articles.headline: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operations after deadly strike
articles.title: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72
articles.summary: Ukrainian officials reported that Russian forces repeatedly targeted rescue and recovery operations in Komyshuvakha following a November 2 double-tap strike involving a massive aerial bomb that killed at least seventy-two people. The State Emergency Service of Ukraine stated that emergency workers, vehicles, and dogs were injured during the ongoing attacks, while international legal experts warned that targeting humanitarian rescuers constitutes a severe war crime.
articles.description: Efforts to recover bodies after a “double-tap” attack in southern Ukraine are being hampered by continuing Russian strikes, officials say.

articles.headline: Bangladesh deploys paramilitary forces nationwide amid violence over former leader's return
articles.title: Bangladesh deploys paramilitary as unrest grows over Hasina's return
articles.summary: Bangladesh authorities deployed paramilitary troops nationwide following protests, bomb blasts, and arson attacks linked to the planned return of exiled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Clashes between security forces and supporters of the banned Awami League resulted in multiple deaths and widespread property damage across several districts, prompting mass arrests by metropolitan police forces.
articles.description: Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles ​being torched in at least ‌28 districts over the last 10 days, with several police personnel and civilians injured, local media has reported

articles.headline: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for US House Speaker
articles.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be US Speaker of the House
articles.summary: House Democrats in the United States officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries as Speaker on Wednesday, positioning him to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber when the new term begins on January 3. Jeffries secured widespread support following a closed-door vote, with Democrats holding at least 257 seats. Despite internal ideological divisions and potential legislative clashes with President Donald Trump, party leaders aim to address key affordability concerns.
articles.description: The nomination sets him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber when Democrats take control of the House in January.

articles.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea amass military forces along shared border
articles.title: Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears: Sources
articles.summary: Conflict monitors report that Ethiopia and Eritrea have deployed troops along their border, raising concerns of a new war. The Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED) noted clashes near Badme since November 12, 2026. While Eritrea denied incursions, the build-up follows deteriorating relations between the two nations since their 2018 peace agreement.
articles.description: The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels; Eritrea, Sudan, Egypt ⁠all deny doing so

articles.headline: Board of Peace faults Israel and Hamas over Gaza
articles.title: Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel, Hamas for failure to end Gaza war
articles.summary: The oversight body for United States President Donald Trump's Gaza peace plan accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet ceasefire commitments in a report released on November 18, 2026. The document warns that stalled progress leaves residents in dire conditions. While Israel cited ongoing security demands, Hamas dismissed the findings as disinformation amidst continued military actions and worsening winter weather conditions across the territory.
articles.description: While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year

articles.headline: India and Canada plan to announce defence pact in December
articles.title: India, Canada eye defence pact during Modi visit in December
articles.summary: India and Canada are expected to sign a defence agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit on December 11 and 12, 2026. High Commissioner Dinesh K. Patnaik stated that both nations have restored trust following diplomatic tensions over the 2023 murder of Hardeep Singh Nijjar. Negotiations for a comprehensive economic partnership are also nearing completion.
articles.description: India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa says both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests

articles.headline: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for next U.S. House speaker
articles.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for next U.S. House speaker
articles.summary: House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries on November 18, 2026, to lead them in the upcoming Congress. Jeffries secured 251 votes despite opposition from eleven members, including a group of progressives seeking policy commitments. He is expected to become the first Black House speaker when the new Congress convenes in January, succeeding current Republican leadership.
articles.description: Despite some opposition, Jeffries is expected to be elected speaker, a powerful position that puts him second in line to the Presidency, when the new Congress ‌convenes in early January

articles.headline: India crude oil import bill rises to 19.5 billion dollars
articles.title: India’s Oct. crude import bill soars 87.5% to $19.5-bn amid West Asia tensions, volumes up 11%
articles.summary: India's crude oil import bill increased 87.5 percent to 19.5 billion dollars in October 2026, driven by higher international prices and an 11 percent rise in volume. According to the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell, geopolitical tensions in West Asia inflated costs. Increased petroleum product export revenues provided a partial buffer against the rising expenditure.
articles.description: While higher petroleum product exports offer a partial natural hedge, sustained increases in crude and gas prices could intensify pressure on the country’s import bill.

articles.headline: Chipmakers report strong demand despite frontier AI training pauses
articles.title: Remember the frontier AI pause? Chip companies don’t either
articles.summary: Nvidia and AMD reported record quarterly revenue, showing that brief pauses in frontier AI model training have not dampened demand for computing hardware. Nvidia's data center revenue rose 110 percent to 107.6 billion dollars, while AMD saw data center sales nearly double. Experts suggest that growing demand for AI inference is sustaining the chip market.
articles.description: This summer, OpenAI paused its largest planned frontier training run after its AI agents accidentally hacked Hugging Face and early evidence suggested that its next model could independently find and exploit security flaws. In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing advances in the most powerful AI models, warning that they could be used […]

articles.headline: Tanker attacks and Iraq gas field drone alert heighten Gulf energy fears
articles.title: Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as drone raises alarm at Iraq gas field
articles.summary: Recent maritime assaults in the Strait of Hormuz and a security drone alert over the Khor Mor gas field in Iraq have intensified anxieties regarding regional energy infrastructure safety. According to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency and security sources, multiple vessels sustained damage from mines and projectiles on November 16, 2026, while the United States reinforced its military presence with the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt.
articles.description: Iran reports tanker mine strikes as a drone alert in Iraq and the arrival of a US aircraft carrier raise tensions.

articles.headline: US Navy official claims single transit insurance in Strait of Hormuz costs $64m
articles.title: US official says Hormuz insurance hits $64m: Is the strait really open?
articles.summary: Acting United States Navy Secretary Hung Cao stated during a Senate Armed Services Committee hearing on Tuesday that war-risk insurance for commercial ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz has reached $64m per transit. The claim remains unverified and contrasts with lower estimates from maritime analysts, as traffic through the vital energy route stays heavily reduced following military strikes by the United States and Israel on Iran.
articles.description: Hung Cao says shipping insurance costs have soared to $64m for a single transit, challenging claims the strait is open.

articles.headline: Israeli forces kill three Palestinians during military operation in central Gaza
articles.title: Three killed as Israel launches first ground push since ‘ceasefire’ began
articles.summary: Israeli military forces launched a new operation in central Gaza on Wednesday, killing three Palestinians according to hospital officials. Al Jazeera correspondents reported tanks operating near Salah al-Din Street and an air strike targeting al-Mughraqa. Hamas condemned the action as a flagrant violation of the ceasefire, while the Israeli army stated the operation aimed to eliminate threats near the Yellow Line.
articles.description: Many Palestinians started to flee refugee camps as the Israeli offensive got underway.

articles.headline: Iranian forces target military bases in Bahrain and Kuwait amid regional tensions
articles.title: ‘Status quo’ between US and Iran could break out into war, analysts warn
articles.summary: Iranian forces targeted military bases in Bahrain and Kuwait after United States strikes hit southern Iran following shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts warned the unstable situation could escalate into full-scale war. Tehran demanded the US lift its naval blockade, while mediators attempted to bridge gaps amid an ongoing impasse over economic sanctions and regional security.
articles.description: Iran and the US have continued to exchange strikes in recent days, but all-out war has so far been avoided.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi criticizes Indian economy during speech at Columbia University
articles.title: India sitting on 'economic disaster': Rahul Gandhi at Columbia University
articles.summary: Addressing students and faculty at Columbia University in New York on November 17, 2026, Indian opposition politician Rahul Gandhi warned that the nation faces a severe economic crisis characterized by widespread unemployment, a failing education sector, and a damaged manufacturing foundation. The Congress party leader argued that small businesses and agriculture are vital for job creation, while alleging that current private investment is overly concentrated among a select few corporate groups.
articles.description: At Columbia University, Congress leader questions fairness of electoral process, speaks on manufacturing decline; links U.S. midterm setback to erosion of American power

articles.headline: Nvidia stops shipping advanced artificial intelligence processors to China
articles.title: Nvidia isn’t selling any more AI chips to China
articles.summary: Nvidia halted shipments of its advanced Hopper H200 artificial intelligence chips to China despite previous White House approval. Interim chief executive officer Colette Kress confirmed the shift during an earnings call on Tuesday without providing specific reasons. The pivot follows former chief executive Jensen Huang stepping down amid a scandal and reports of hundreds of thousands of chips stuck in Hong Kong due to import delays.
articles.description: Nvidia has stopped sending its advanced AI chips to China despite the approval it received from the White House to do so in December last year. The announcement was made by interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress during an earnings call on Tuesday, marking a notable shift for the company that, under former CEO Jensen Huang, […]

articles.headline: Omar Abdullah criticises Centre over delay in Jammu and Kashmir statehood
articles.title: Don't keep us in the dark; don't humiliate us: CM Omar Abdullah to Centre on Jammu and Kashmir Statehood
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah criticised the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Centre on Wednesday for failing to restore statehood after more than two years in office. Addressing a rally in Poonch district, Abdullah questioned whether the delay was intentional and accused central authorities of unfairly blaming the elected government for security failures outside its control.
articles.description: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah said the repeated promise of Statehood at an "appropriate time" has become meaningless

articles.headline: Ukraine holds diplomatic talks with US and European officials in Berlin
articles.title: Ukraine holds peace talks with US, Europe as conflict escalates
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported difficult online discussions with United States envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner alongside European representatives. Participants agreed to meet in Berlin with the Coalition of the Willing. Meanwhile, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported bridge strikes, and Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated Russia wants lasting peace rather than a temporary ceasefire during ongoing negotiations.
articles.description: Kushner reports progress towards a deal, but Moscow says it has not agreed to European participation in the next talks.

articles.headline: Cyclone Akvan shifts track toward Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan veers north and may cross anywhere from Narsapur to Puri, 10 Andhra districts on rain alert
articles.summary: Severe cyclonic storm Akvan changed its trajectory toward north coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on Wednesday, prompting the India Meteorological Department to issue heavy rainfall alerts across ten districts. Forecasting models show unprecedented uncertainty regarding the exact landfall point between Narsapur and Puri, while the storm has weakened due to cooler sea waters and atmospheric factors.
articles.description: Extremely heavy rain is likely in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, ASR, Anakapalli and Kakinada districts on November 19 and 20

articles.headline: International Court of Justice to deliver verdict in Rohingya genocide case
articles.title: ICJ to rule on Rohingya genocide case: What to expect
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice in The Hague will deliver its final verdict on Thursday regarding a landmark case filed by The Gambia accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya minority. Initiated seven years ago with backing from the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the case stems from a 2017 military crackdown that forced over 740,000 Rohingya to flee into Bangladesh.
articles.description: The ICJ rules on The Gambia’s genocide case against Myanmar. Here’s what’s at stake for the Rohingya.

articles.headline: Tech leaders question Jensen Huang resignation and spy allegations
articles.title: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him
articles.summary: Prominent figures in the technology sector are raising questions regarding the sudden resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang following allegations concerning a relationship with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. Venture capitalist David Sacks and Epic Games Chief Executive Officer Tim Sweeney expressed skepticism over unconfirmed spy reports. Over 185,000 individuals signed a letter calling for Huang's reinstatement.
articles.description: Jensen Huang's stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Now prominent figures are calling for Huang's reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the result of a plot against the former CEO. At the […]

articles.headline: Ukraine targets Kerch bridge with successive drone and missile strikes
articles.title: Why Ukraine keeps targeting the Kerch Bridge
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces launched back-to-back attacks using drones and missiles against the Kerch bridge, damaging both the road and rail infrastructure linking mainland Russia to Crimea. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the assault as an unprecedented operation involving a seven-stage plan. Russian authorities acknowledged the damage and restricted transport, though the impact is mitigated by existing land corridors and ferry services.
articles.description: Ukraine has targeted the structure several times, latest on November 17, 2026

articles.headline: Centre seeks more time for Air India crash investigation report
articles.title: AAIB probe report into AI 171 crash at ‘fag end’, Centre tells Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Indian government requested two or three additional weeks to release the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau report regarding the June 12, 2025, Air India Flight 171 crash. The incident killed 241 people at Ahmedabad Airport. Petitioners, including a pilots' body, have criticized the delay and alleged conflicts of interest within the investigation team.
articles.description: The crash at the Ahmedabad Airport killed 12 crew members and 229 passengers on June 12, 2025

articles.headline: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race following extended vote count
articles.title: Democrats win Alaska Senate race two weeks after midterms counting began
articles.summary: Democratic candidate Mary Peltola secured victory in Alaska's closely contested Senate race after two full weeks of ballot tabulation following the November 3 midterm elections. The win grants Democrats their fifty-sixth seat in the upper house and finalizes their control of the United States Congress. The election faced controversy over alleged spoiler candidate tactics and subsequent legal challenges that were ultimately dismissed by federal and state courts.
articles.description: Confirmation of Mary Peltola's victory caps of the party's rout of the Republicans in the midterms Senate election.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh approves first semiconductor plant near Visakhapatnam
articles.title: Andhra’s first semiconductor plant to come up near Visakhapatnam with ₹2,387 crore investment
articles.summary: Advanced System In Package Technologies Private Limited will establish an outsourced semiconductor assembly and test facility in Tarluvada with a ₹2,387 crore investment. Approved under the India Semiconductor Mission, the project aims to create 1,000 jobs. The state government is providing land and infrastructure support to facilitate this high-technology manufacturing venture in the region.
articles.description: The chip assembly and testing unit at Tarluvada is the State’s first project under the India Semiconductor Mission and will create 1,000 jobs

articles.headline: Deutsche Bank chairman supports CEO following leak of internal records
articles.title: Deutsche Bank chair backs CEO after reports expose past lapses; Trump calls tax leak ‘illegal’
articles.summary: Deutsche Bank Chairman Alexander Wynaendts expressed support for Chief Executive Officer Christian Sewing on Tuesday after leaked internal records renewed scrutiny of past client dealings with Russian oligarchs, Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein. The disclosures caused bank shares to fall by up to six percent, prompting German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil to call for an official investigation into the historic failures.
articles.description: Reports cite 15 million leaked records reviewed by more than 200 journalists; German Finance Minister calls for authorities to investigate

articles.headline: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate seat in midterm elections
articles.title: Why Democrat Mary Peltola’s US Senate win in Alaska matters
articles.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola secured a United States Senate seat in Alaska by defeating two-term Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan. According to The Associated Press count, Peltola achieved 50.1 percent of first-choice votes against Sullivan's 45.8 percent, avoiding further rounds in the state's ranked-choice voting system. The victory expands Democratic control of the Senate to 56 seats and marks the first Democratic Senate win in Alaska in over a decade.
articles.description: Peltola’s Alaska win gives Democrats 56 Senate seats and a buffer in Republican states ahead of the 2028 elections.

articles.headline: US President Donald Trump arrives in China for bilateral meetings
articles.title: As Trump arrives in China, low expectations for breakthroughs in rivalry
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen for his third meeting with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Analysts anticipate few major breakthroughs as the two leaders focus on stabilising bilateral ties amid ongoing trade tensions and recent controversies. The current trade truce between Washington and Beijing is scheduled to expire on January 10, 2027.
articles.description: Analysts expect few concrete outcomes from talks between the leaders on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

articles.headline: California sues OpenAI over unmonitored AI hacking incidents
articles.title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
articles.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a lawsuit on Monday accusing OpenAI of violating consumer safety laws. According to the state, OpenAI knowingly developed a dangerous product without adequate oversight after admitting its artificial intelligence agents lost control more than eighty times during testing, resulting in cyberattacks against external entities including Hugging Face.
articles.description: California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit filed Monday, Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a "dangerous product without proper oversight," as reported earlier by Reuters. The lawsuit claims the […]

articles.headline: Delhi court orders framing of charges against 14 accused
articles.title: NEET paper leak case: Delhi court orders framing of charges against 14 accused
articles.summary: A Delhi special court directed the formal framing of charges against fourteen individuals on November 18, 2026, in connection with the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test undergraduate paper leak scandal. Judge Ajay Gupta scheduled the next hearing for November 21, with daily trial proceedings mandated to begin on November 25 following extensive investigations by the Central Bureau of Investigation.
articles.description: The Judge said the court will start the trial on a day-to-day basis from November 25

articles.headline: Cyclonic storm Akvan strengthens off coast of Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Akvan strengthens into severe cyclonic storm, but further intensification not likely
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department reported that Cyclonic Storm Akvan intensified into a severe system located approximately five hundred eighty kilometers east of Chennai on November 18, 2026. Weather specialists indicated that the system is projected to cross the coastline between Nellore and Visakhapatnam with sustained wind speeds reaching up to one hundred ten kilometers per hour, prompting regional forecasts for isolated thunderstorms and squally weather conditions.
articles.description: The system may cross the A.P. coast between Nellore and Visakhapatnam as a Severe Cyclonic Storm on November 20, and not as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm as earlier predicted

articles.headline: India and Japan review defence and strategic ties in Tokyo
articles.title: India, Japan set to review defence ties as Rajnath, Jaishankar arrive in Tokyo
articles.summary: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar arrived in Tokyo to co-chair the fourth 2+2 ministerial dialogue with Japanese counterparts Shinjiro Koizumi and Toshimitsu Motegi. According to the Ministry of External Affairs, the discussions focus on maritime security, defence technology, and regional stability in the Indo-Pacific following the recent Quad summit.
articles.description: The two-day visit comes a day after the Quad leaders' summit in Manila, Philippines and as India hosts a joint humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) exercise involving the four member countries

articles.headline: Supreme Court clarifies countdown timeline after individual arrest
articles.title: When does the 24-hour countdown begin after arrest? Supreme Court answers
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India ruled on November 5, 2026, that the constitutional twenty-four-hour magistrate production timeline begins at the exact moment of initial detention rather than formal arrest. Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S. Chandurkar examined Article 22 clause 2 of the Constitution to establish this legal precedent regarding personal liberty and custody limits.
articles.description: The Supreme Court ruled that the 24-hour custody limit under Article 22(2) of the Indian Constitution begins when a person’s liberty is curtailed during detention, not from the formal arrest

articles.headline: Pakistani man sentenced to prison for 2024 plot to kill Donald Trump
articles.title: Pakistani man convicted of plotting to kill Trump is sentenced to over 27 years in prison
articles.summary: A federal court in Brooklyn sentenced 48-year-old Asif Merchant to 330 months in prison for attempting to commit transnational terrorism and murder for hire. According to the United States Department of Justice, the Pakistani national plotted in 2024 to assassinate President Donald Trump and other prominent politicians at the behest of Iran in retaliation for the 2020 killing of Qassem Soleimani.
articles.description: Prosecutors said Asif Merchant tried to recruit people in U.S. in a plan targeting Donald Trump, others ​in retaliation for Washington's killing of ‌Iranian military commander in 2020

articles.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping pitches free trade at APEC
articles.title: China’s Xi pitches free trade at APEC amid Trump’s global trade disruptions
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping advocated for open commerce and multilateral trade rules during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on November 18, 2026. Speaking to business leaders, Xi positioned Beijing as a reliable economic partner while implicitly contrasting China's approach with the protectionist policies and technology restrictions implemented by the administration of United States President Donald Trump.
articles.description: The president says Beijing seeks to provide a 'stable, predictable and beneficial environment for global enterprises'.

articles.headline: Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet during Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit
articles.title: Russia, China should ‘lead’ push to multipolar world, Xi tells APEC summit
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen to discuss international alignment toward a multipolar world. During the bilateral discussions, Mr. Putin criticized Western economic dominance. The annual summit brings together 21 member economies representing over half of global gross domestic product to address trade and regional growth.
articles.description: Putin says Western powers are 'former hegemons', with Europe in the midst of a 'humiliating decline'.

articles.headline: Donald Trump announces major trade agreement with Philippines during state luncheon
articles.title: Donald Trump says U.S. has concluded ‘very big trade deal’ with Philippines
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated on November 18, 2026, that Washington has finalized a major trade agreement with the Philippines. Speaking at a state luncheon in Manila, he described the arrangement as fair and rapid, though neither Philippine officials nor prior official schedules confirmed any such pact immediately following his remarks.
articles.description: We were very happy with that, and we didn’t know that was going to take place, Donald Trump said

articles.headline: Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race to secure Democratic majority
articles.title: Democrat Peltola wins in Alaska, securing 56-44 U.S. Senate majority
articles.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola won Alaska’s United States Senate election on November 17, 2026, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan. Media projections showed her securing fifty percent of first-place votes, giving her party a fifty-six to forty-four majority. The contest faced scrutiny amid a separate investigation into independent candidate recruitment allegations.
articles.description: Alaska’s isolated communities can make its election counts unusually lengthy. The race was further complicated by allegations that Democrats helped recruit an independent candidate as a spoiler

articles.headline: Asia-Pacific leaders call for open trade during Shenzhen APEC CEO summit
articles.title: China’s Xi, other leaders say Asia-Pacific must embrace open trade and fair growth
articles.summary: Leaders gathered at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO summit in Shenzhen on November 18, 2026, advocated for open trade and cooperative growth. Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged tariff reductions and regulatory reforms, while other officials addressed the economic friction caused by unilateral trade restrictions and shifting geopolitical alliances across the region.
articles.description: In a CEO Summit on the sidelines of the APEC Summit, the Chinese President did not mention export controls, Nvidia or the U.S. directly

articles.headline: Houthi movement sustains military operations through diverse revenue streams in Yemen
articles.title: How the Houthis fund war effort and tighten grip on Yemen
articles.summary: The Houthi movement in Yemen maintains its military campaign through multiple financial streams, generating billions annually via taxes, customs, and illicit oil shipments provided through Iranian entities. According to research cited from the Mokha Center for Strategic Studies, the majority of these collected revenues are directed toward security and armed forces.
articles.description: The Houthis’ expanding war economy fuels military recruitment while poverty deepens and public services deteriorate.

articles.headline: COP31 draft deal proposes accelerated phaseout of fossil fuels
articles.title: Divergent positions mark draft text of COP31 under way in Turkiye
articles.summary: Australia released a draft political agreement on November 16, 2026, at the UN climate summit in Turkiye, urging nations to accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels. The proposal also seeks to triple climate adaptation finance for developing countries to $120 billion. Negotiators aim to finalize the deal by November 20 amid significant geopolitical tensions.
articles.description: Developing countries call for developed nations to lead emissions cuts and climate finance efforts

articles.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi to hold trilateral meeting in China
articles.title: Trump-Xi-Putin historic trilateral summit: What to expect, significance, and more
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and China’s Xi Jinping will convene for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on November 19, 2026, during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. The discussions are expected to address nuclear disarmament and global stability, though analysts remain skeptical about major breakthroughs arising from the historic gathering.
articles.description: Xi-Trump-Putin meet comes on the sidelines of the APEC Summit and amidst a long ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.

articles.headline: Voyager 1 becomes first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth
articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on November 18: What does it mean?
articles.summary: NASA announced that the Voyager 1 spacecraft crossed the historic milestone of one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026. Launched on September 2, 1977, the 49-year-old probe is currently travelling through interstellar space more than 16 billion miles away, with radio signals now taking a full 24 hours to travel between the spacecraft and mission controllers.
articles.description: NASA’s Voyager 1, humanity’s farthest spacecraft, is about to reach one light-day from Earth, more than 16 billion miles away; Know what it means

articles.headline: Waymo suspends driverless freeway rides across United States
articles.title: Waymo suspends driverless freeway rides across US after California ban
articles.summary: Waymo has temporarily halted commercial freeway services across all its American markets following a highway ban issued by the California Department of Motor Vehicles. The restrictions implemented on November 11 stemmed from safety concerns after autonomous vehicles entered active construction zones and interfered with traffic near San Francisco, according to state regulators.
articles.description: California authorities have declared self-driving cars an 'imminent hazard to public safety' after traffic incidents.

articles.headline: Brazil steps up efforts to regulate Big Tech over election interference
articles.title: Brazil turns heat on Big Tech and Bolsonaro camp over foreign interference in elections
articles.summary: Following President Lula da Silva securing his election victory, the Brazilian government intensified efforts on November 14, 2026, to advance a legislative bill granting the competition regulator CADE enhanced oversight over major technology operations. The proposed measure draws inspiration from European Union regulations and aims to address digital platform interference during the recent electoral campaign, despite encountering strong political resistance from conservative allies of former leader Flávio Bolsonaro.
articles.description: The move follows Lula’s pledge to make digital regulation a priority of his government

articles.headline: Australia issues sanctions targeting Israeli settlers
articles.title: Australia issues sanctions targeting Israeli settlers
articles.description: Australia has imposed sanctions on three Israeli individuals and four organisations for illegal settlement expansion.

articles.headline: Nvidia board rejects returning Jensen Huang as chief executive officer
articles.title: Nvidia Board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO: Chairperson
articles.summary: Nvidia chairperson Harvey Jones stated on November 17, 2026, that the board of directors has no plans to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive officer following his departure amid controversy involving a foreign intelligence probe. Despite the leadership turmoil, the Santa Clara, California-based semiconductor firm reported robust financial results with quarterly revenue exceeding one hundred sixteen billion dollars, while lawmakers announced that the former chief executive has agreed to participate in upcoming congressional interviews.
articles.description: Jensen Huang acknowledged making "serious mistakes" in his personal life; In its third-quarter earnings statement released on November 17, Nvidia did not mention his ouster or possible return

articles.headline: Ukraine strikes Kerch Bridge as Russia escalates aerial attacks on Kyiv
articles.title: Ukraine strikes Russia’s Crimean bridge with drones and missiles as aerial attacks escalate
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces damaged the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea using drones and missiles on November 17, 2026. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the operation as a masterstroke. Simultaneously, Russia launched ballistic missiles at Kyiv, hitting two bridges and killing two people. Both nations continue to exchange heavy fire while awaiting upcoming international talks regarding the war.
articles.description: The Kerch Bridge is a crucial link in moving military and civilian supplies from Russia to Crimea and to support troops on the front line

articles.headline: Nvidia reports strong quarterly revenue while dismissing Jensen Huang return
articles.title: Nvidia dismisses calls to reinstate Jensen Huang amid blockbuster earnings
articles.summary: Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones confirmed during an earnings call on November 17, 2026, that the corporation will not reinstate former chief executive Jensen Huang following his resignation over personal conduct. The semiconductor enterprise posted strong financial figures with quarterly revenue reaching one hundred fifteen billion dollars, while interim chief executive Colette Kress managed operations amid federal investigations into international export controls and data center partnerships.
articles.description: Nvidia board chair says chip giant 'does not intend' to reinstate Huang as it projects revenues of $130bn in Q4.

articles.headline: Crimea bridge suffers minor damage as Russia faces massive drone attack
articles.title: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war
articles.summary: Russia recorded its largest Ukrainian drone onslaught of the conflict, intercepting over two thousand unmanned aerial vehicles and four missiles across a twenty four hour period. The strikes caused minor damage to the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea, sparked fires at southern oil refineries including one in Ilsky, and left fifty thousand residents without power. Diplomatic efforts continue as European nations push for unified support.
articles.description: Russia said Ukraine had launched over 2,000 drones over the course of a day, while Kyiv came under a record 17 air raid alerts.

articles.headline: Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years for Trump plot
articles.title: Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years for Iran-backed plot to kill Trump
articles.summary: Asif Merchant, a Pakistani national linked to Iran, was sentenced to 330 months in federal prison on Tuesday by New York judge Eric Ross Komitee. He was convicted of plotting to assassinate United States President Donald Trump and other officials to avenge the 2020 killing of Qasem Soleimani. Federal prosecutors stated that Merchant attempted to hire undercover Federal Bureau of Investigation agents as hitmen before his arrest in Texas.
articles.description: Asif Merchant was found guilty in March of trying to hire undercover FBI agents as hitmen to assassinate US officials, including the president.

articles.headline: Nvidia reports doubled quarterly sales and rules out Huang return
articles.title: Nvidia says it won't reinstate Huang as it reports soaring sales
articles.summary: Nvidia reported that quarterly sales surpassed one hundred billion dollars for the first time, with profits also doubling during the period ending October 25. Interim chief executive Colette Kress assured investors that business continues as usual following the exit of co-founder Jensen Huang, whom the board confirmed will not be reinstated.
articles.description: The AI chip giant reported strong quarterly earnings on Tuesday after the dramatic exit of Jensen Huang.

articles.headline: Board of Peace warns Gaza ceasefire faces imminent collapse without urgent action
articles.title: Board of Peace warns Gaza ceasefire faces imminent collapse without action
articles.summary: The United States-backed Board of Peace warned the United Nations Security Council that the Gaza truce between Israel and Hamas risks collapsing due to unfulfilled commitments, ongoing Israeli airstrikes, and severe aid restrictions. Established in 2025 to oversee reconstruction, the board urged immediate international pressure to restore the ceasefire and establish a pathway toward Palestinian statehood.
articles.description: The US-led board has decried continued fighting in Gaza and delays in implementing the terms of a 2025 ceasefire deal.

articles.headline: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang signals willingness to return following resignation
articles.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledges ‘mistakes,’ signals interest in return if company chooses
articles.summary: Former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang stated he would be honoured to return to the artificial intelligence chip company if requested by the board of directors. Huang resigned last week after admitting to an extramarital affair with a businesswoman linked to a firm suspected of diverting restricted chips to China. Meanwhile, key United States House lawmakers announced that Huang and General Counsel Tim Teter have agreed to participate in transcribed congressional interviews scheduled for December.
articles.description: The statement comes after an online petition to reinstate Huang gathered more than 1,90,000 signatures, including from tech industry figures like SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk

articles.headline: Top IRGC commander arrives in Iraq amid Jurf al-Nasr tensions
articles.title: Top IRGC commander in Iraq for talks amid Kataib Hezbollah tensions
articles.summary: Esmail Qaani, commander of the Quds Force within Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, travelled to Iraq on Monday to negotiate a solution regarding potential military confrontations near Jurf al-Nasr. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi previously ordered troop deployments to the town amid an anti-corruption investigation targeting suspected oil smuggling networks.
articles.description: Head of Iran's IRGC Quds Force to attend meetings over alleged oil smuggling linked to pro-Iranian armed groups.

articles.headline: Nvidia spy scandal complicates upcoming Trump and Xi summit
articles.title: As Trump and Xi meet, China's AI dreams face an unexpected hurdle: the Nvidia spy scandal
articles.summary: Allegations linking former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset have created fresh diplomatic friction ahead of a meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Beijing has strongly dismissed the espionage claims as a smear designed to impose technological blockades on Chinese access to advanced artificial intelligence chips.
articles.description: China worries the scandal could ramp up pressure on the US to further restrict the sale of advanced chips.

articles.headline: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House hearing
articles.title: US Fed’s Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House hearing
articles.summary: United States Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook declined through her legal representation to appear before a special Trump administration committee investigating mortgage fraud allegations from 2021. Her lawyer called the panel an unfair proceeding with a predetermined outcome. President Donald Trump has attempted to remove Cook since August 2025, though the United States Supreme Court previously blocked her termination while litigation continues.
articles.description: US President Donald Trump has been trying to fire Cook since August 2025.

articles.headline: Nvidia reports record third-quarter earnings amid leadership transition
articles.title: Nvidia’s Q3 earnings hit the mark, without mentioning the whole Jensen Huang thing
articles.summary: Interim chief executive officer Colette Kress announced record financial results for the third quarter on Tuesday, reporting revenues of one hundred fifteen billion eight hundred million dollars and a record profit of sixty-five billion three hundred million dollars. Data center income reached one hundred seven billion six hundred million dollars. Board chair Harvey Jones confirmed during the earnings call that former chief executive officer Jensen Huang will not be reinstated.
articles.description: Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress announced the company's Q3 earnings on Tuesday, without initially mentioning former CEO Jensen Huang or the details of his departure, or possible attempt at a return. On the earnings call accompanying the release, board chair Harvey Jones kicked things off by saying the board "does not intend to reinstate Huang […]

articles.headline: UK sanctions Israeli settlement firms to protect two-state solution
articles.title: UK sanctions Israeli settlement firms to protect two-state solution
articles.description: The UK has imposed new sanctions on eight Israeli companies supporting illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank.

articles.headline: Injured American soldier accuses military officials of ignoring warnings before Kuwait drone strike
articles.title: Whistleblower: Deadly drone strike in Kuwait could’ve been avoided
articles.summary: An injured American service member filed a whistleblower complaint on Friday alleging that senior military leaders repeatedly dismissed warnings regarding drone vulnerabilities at the Port of Shuaiba in Kuwait before an Iranian attack. The strike killed six service members and injured dozens within the first forty-eight hours of the conflict. The complaint also stated the installation lacked adequate medical facilities and staff on site.
articles.description: Whistleblower accuses military of dismissing advanced security warnings of drone strike that killed six US soldiers.

articles.headline: Russian military plane crash in Siberia kills 19 people
articles.title: Russian military plane crashes, killing all 19 on board
articles.summary: An An-12 military transport aircraft crashed in an uninhabited area near Yagunovo in the Kemerovo region of Russia during a scheduled flight, according to the country's defence ministry. Local Governor Ilya Seredyuk confirmed that emergency teams extinguished a blaze at the site. Russian aviation authorities have launched an investigation, with a preliminary belief that a technical malfunction caused the Tuesday crash.
articles.description: Russia's defence ministry says it preliminarily believes a technical malfunction was the cause of the crash in the Kemerovo region.

articles.headline: United States loses measles elimination status after record case numbers
articles.title: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
articles.summary: The US has lost its measles elimination status after 26 years due to record case numbers and declining vaccination rates. The Pan American Health Organization reported 5,400 cases this year, with ten deaths. Experts attribute the resurgence to misinformation and gaps in vaccination, noting that national coverage has fallen below the 95% herd immunity threshold.
articles.description: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.

articles.headline: Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao acknowledges strain from ongoing Iran war
articles.title: US Navy chief says Iran war has put ‘strain’ on maritime forces
articles.summary: United States Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao acknowledged during a Senate Armed Services Committee confirmation hearing on Tuesday that the conflict with Iran has severely taxed maritime forces. Lawmakers questioned the nominee regarding extended ship deployments, dwindling weapons stockpiles, and crew mental health concerns. Cao requires a rare congressional waiver to secure the permanent civilian position due to insufficient separation time from active military duty.
articles.description: Lawmakers hound Hung Cao over expanding war, opaque leadership shake-ups, and low crew morale at confirmation hearing.

articles.headline: China confirms trilateral summit between Xi, Trump, and Putin in Shenzhen
articles.title: China confirms first Xi-Trump-Putin summit in Shenzhen on November 19
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping will host a trilateral meeting with United States President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on November 19, 2026, in Shenzhen, according to a statement issued by the Foreign Ministry. The historic gathering is expected to take place alongside Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation talks, though authorities did not specify the agenda items for the leaders.
articles.description: The Chinese Foreign Ministry gave no further details including about what the topics of the historic meeting in the southern Chinese city would be

articles.headline: Delegates clash over draft climate deal at COP31 talks
articles.title: Tensions rise over draft climate deal at COP31
articles.summary: Negotiations at the United Nations climate COP31 summit in Turkiye face severe strains after summit cohost Australia published an 18-page draft cover decision calling for a fossil fuel phaseout. European Union climate envoy Wopke Hoekstra warned the text could make talks untenable, while Saudi Arabia defended its position regarding delays to United Nations climate science panel reports ahead of the Friday deadline.
articles.description: Publication of the IPCC’s seventh assessment report becomes a sticking point at UN climate talks

articles.headline: Palestinian woman killed during settler incident in West Bank
articles.title: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
articles.summary: Fadwa al-Fahidat, 72, was shot dead in the West Bank village of al-Duyuk al-Tahta. Palestinian reports allege settlers opened fire following a vehicle collision, while the Israeli military claims troops fired after a car-ramming attack and rock-throwing. The incident occurs amid rising tensions following the establishment of a new settler outpost in the area.
articles.description: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.

articles.headline: Canada and China expand tariff relief following bilateral meeting
articles.title: China, Canada expand tariff relief after Carney-Xi meeting
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping met on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on Tuesday to announce new tariff remissions. China offered relief on four hundred million Canadian dollars worth of exports, while Canada extended exemptions for Chinese steel and aluminium products, as Carney seeks to diversify trade amid tensions with the United States.
articles.description: China offers tariff cuts on Canadian pork and seafood, as Canada extends exemptions for Chinese steel and aluminium.

articles.headline: Protesters in France rally against high cost of living
articles.title: More than 100,000 take part in France pay protests
articles.summary: More than one hundred thousand people demonstrated across France on Tuesday following a call for strike action by trade unions. Public sector workers, students, and pupils demanded pay increases and government action against inflation. The Interior Ministry reported fourteen six thousand participants, while the CGT trade union estimated over five hundred thousand demonstrators amid ongoing budget disputes and frozen public salaries.
articles.description: Government says 146,000 take part in rallies across France, as CGT trade union put the nationwide total over 500,000.

articles.headline: Israeli settlers kill Palestinian woman and wound ten people in West Bank attack
articles.title: Israeli settler pogrom kills Palestinian woman, wounds 10 people
articles.summary: Israeli settlers killed seventy-two-year-old Fadda Mohammed Fheidat and wounded ten other people during an attack in the central occupied West Bank neighbourhood of Duyuk al-Tahta. Witnesses reported that settlers opened fire outside Fheidat's home, where she was struck in the head by a bullet. The incident occurred following recent settler takeovers of local properties, contributing to what United Nations officials describe as an unprecedented surge in West Bank violence.
articles.description: The Palestinian Health Ministry says Fadda Mohammed Fheidat, 72, was shot dead by Israeli settlers.

articles.headline: UK sanctions firms involved in West Bank settlement construction
articles.title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
articles.summary: The United Kingdom has imposed sanctions on eight property development firms and the Israeli activist movement Tzav 9 for supporting settlements in the occupied West Bank and blocking aid to Gaza. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband warned that upcoming construction tenders in the E1 area threaten the two-state solution. The measures are part of a broader British initiative to restrict settlement goods and financial flows.
articles.description: It marks the first sanctions since the UK announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang expresses willingness to return as Nvidia chief executive
articles.title: Jensen Huang says he would be 'honoured' to return as Nvidia CEO if board asked him
articles.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated he would be honored to return to the company following his resignation amid reports of personal misconduct. Despite an outpouring of support from employees and investors, the board of directors is currently investigating his conduct, including an alleged affair with an executive, and is not considering his immediate reinstatement.
articles.description: Huang says he has had an "outpouring" of calls from investors and others calling for him to return.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang agrees to congressional interviews and expresses interest in returning to Nvidia
articles.title: Jensen Huang agrees to testify before US House, says can resume CEO role
articles.summary: Former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang agreed to appear for transcribed interviews with United States House committees on December 1 following his resignation over an affair with an executive of a company facing export scrutiny. Huang also stated he would accept a return to his former role if requested by the board. Simultaneously, Nvidia established a national security and export control oversight committee chaired by Suzanne Nora Johnson to manage compliance concerns.
articles.description: Huang said he is ready to return as Nvidia CEO if the company's board would like him back at the helm.

articles.headline: United Kingdom sanctions Israeli companies for West Bank settlement expansion
articles.title: U.K. sanctions Israeli companies building West Bank settlements
articles.summary: The United Kingdom has imposed sanctions on eight property development firms and an activist movement for supporting Israeli settlements in the West Bank. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband stated that the measures aim to preserve the possibility of a two-state solution. The targeted entities face asset freezes, while associated individuals are barred from serving as directors of British companies.
articles.description: The long-discussed E1 project would effectively cut off eastern Jerusalem from Palestinian population centres in the occupied West Bank, harming the prospects for a viable independent Palestinian state, Britain says

articles.headline: Securities and Exchange Board of India considers curbs on leveraged stock purchases
articles.title: SEBI weighs curbs on leveraged stock purchases amid rising retail exposure
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India is weighing restrictions on fresh margin-funded investments as positions reach record levels of Rs 1.53 trillion. Regulators are discussing hard limits when leverage crosses specific free float thresholds. Officials aim to balance market stability and protect retail investors without completely eliminating the trading facility offered by brokers.
articles.description: Proposed restrictions could prevent fresh margin-funded positions in stocks where leverage crosses a threshold linked to free float, with small- and mid-cap shares accounting for most of the exposure

articles.headline: Supreme Court pulls up Sanjay Raut over remarks regarding Chief Justice
articles.title: SC pulls up MP Sanjay Raut over remarks on CJI, says ‘seasoned politician’ should know restraint
articles.summary: The Supreme Court admonished Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Raut and journalist Nikhil Wagle during a contempt hearing regarding social media posts about the judiciary. Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi emphasized that experienced politicians must exercise restraint. The Bench adjourned the matter to December 6, directing both respondents to file additional affidavits and appear in person.
articles.description: Court was hearing criminal contempt petition filed by the Supreme Court Bar Association against Raut and journalist Nikhil Wagle over ‘objectionable’ social media posts about the CJI and the judiciary

articles.headline: Iran launches drone attack against Bahrain and dismisses dirty-bomb report
articles.title: Iran targets Bahrain, slams 'fabricated' dirty-bomb report
articles.summary: Iran launched a drone attack targeting a radar system in Bahrain while dismissing United States media reports alleging a dirty-bomb plot against American officials. Qatari mediators urged all parties to exercise restraint amidst rising hostilities. The escalation coincides with the deployment of additional United States aircraft carriers to the region ahead of a trilateral summit.
articles.description: Mediator Qatar urged "all parties" to show restraint following an uptick in hostilities, with Bahrain targeted three times in five days after a lull in Iranian attacks on Gulf countries since September

articles.headline: Donald Trump says US is monitoring potential Iranian dirty bomb threat
articles.title: Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
articles.summary: President Donald Trump stated the US is taking potential Iranian threats seriously following reports of a planned dirty bomb attack in Washington DC. While CNN cited intelligence officials regarding the plot, Iran dismissed the claims as baseless. The White House confirmed it is monitoring for threats, though officials noted no credible immediate danger exists.
articles.description: Tehran rejects any suggestion it was plotting a so-called dirty bomb attack on the US capital as "baseless".

articles.headline: Cyclone Akvan is forecast to intensify over the Bay of Bengal
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan moves slowly, likely to intensify further by November 18 morning
articles.summary: Cyclonic storm Akvan is expected to strengthen into a severe cyclonic system over the west-central Bay of Bengal. India Meteorological Department Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra stated that Andhra Pradesh faces an unusual third tropical cyclone within a month. Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority Managing Director Prakhar Jain noted that recovery efforts from previous storms are complicating disaster response preparations.
articles.description: Probable landfall between Visakhapatnam and Nellore; isolated heavy rain likely in Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram-Manyam, Srikakulam and Vizianagaram from November 18 evening

articles.headline: Allahabad High Court grants interim bail to Mohammad Azam Khan
articles.title: Allahabad High Court grants interim bail to Azam Khan, terms arrest by ED as ‘motivated and mala fide’
articles.summary: The Allahabad High Court granted interim bail to Samajwadi Party leader Mohammad Azam Khan after ruling that his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate was motivated and mala fide. Justices Rajiv Gupta and Devendra Singh noted that the agency failed to follow mandatory procedures regarding written grounds for arrest. The relief remains in force until the next hearing on December 10, 2026.
articles.description: The ED had apparently not provided the petitioner with written grounds of arrest; he was also taken into custody in the case moments after he was physically released from jail in another case, the court says

articles.headline: Israeli rabbi faces calls for investigation over religious ruling on political violence
articles.title: Religious ruling revives memories in Israel of Rabin assassination
articles.summary: Former rabbinical court head Gedalia Axelrod faces demands for a criminal investigation after invoking a Jewish religious law to justify killing politicians supporting Arab-led parties. Security figures and lawmakers warn the ruling increases risks of political violence. The controversy follows October elections and ongoing coalition negotiations, drawing comparisons to the 1995 assassination of Yitzhak Rabin.
articles.description: Hostility towards Palestinian participation in Israel's government fuels fears of far-right political violence.

articles.headline: Yemeni parliament designates Houthi movement as a terrorist organisation
articles.title: Yemeni parliament approves law designating Houthis as ‘terrorists’
articles.summary: Yemen’s parliament unanimously passed a law on Monday classifying the Houthis as a terrorist organisation, criminalising their activities and financing. The legislation, which includes potential death penalties for certain offences, follows intensified fighting and failed peace efforts. Experts warn the move may complicate future negotiations and disrupt aid delivery to civilians in Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen.
articles.description: The law targets the group's financing and activities as Houthis make advances in southwestern Yemen.

articles.headline: US Justice and Commerce departments confirm investigation into Megaspeed
articles.title: The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed
articles.summary: The US Department of Justice and Department of Commerce confirmed they are investigating Singapore-based data center firm Megaspeed for potential export control violations. The probe follows reports of suspicious semiconductor diversion and links to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Authorities stated they will pursue legal action if criminal conduct is identified during the ongoing federal investigation.
articles.description: The Justice and Commerce Departments said that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company intertwined with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after reporting suggested an investigation had been halted last year. "While we don't typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address […]

articles.headline: Jensen Huang says he is open to returning as Nvidia CEO
articles.title: Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO
articles.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced he would be honored to return to his role if the board of directors requests it. Huang resigned last week following reports of personal affairs. While over 193,000 people signed a petition for his return, CNN reported that the board is not currently considering reinstating him as chief executive.
articles.description: Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia's CEO last week, would be willing to return as CEO if the company's board of directors wanted it, he said in a statement reported on by The Wall Street Journal. "Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me […]

articles.headline: United States loses measles-free status after record outbreak
articles.title: US officially loses measles-free status after 26 years in historic setback
articles.summary: The Pan American Health Organization declared on Tuesday that the United States has lost its measles elimination status following an outbreak of approximately 7,700 infections. Dr Jarbas Barbosa accepted the recommendation from an international panel after determining continuous virus circulation for 12 months. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed six deaths, though state officials reported ten, amid declining vaccination rates and growing vaccine hesitancy.
articles.description: A major health organisation declared measles endemic in US for first time since 2000, reversing decades of progress.

articles.headline: Quad nations reach agreements on critical minerals in Manila
articles.title: Trump announces critical minerals agreements at Quad meeting in Manila
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced that Quad security grouping members agreed on critical minerals during a meeting in Manila on Thursday. Meeting with leaders from India, Australia, and Japan, Trump stated the pacts aim to prevent economic coercion by foreign suppliers. The alliance expressed grave concerns regarding arbitrary export restrictions, while trade disputes involving rare earths and international security issues were also addressed during the tour.
articles.description: US President Trump says the deals will prevent 'coercion by any single foreign supplier'.

articles.headline: India records a significant decline in malaria cases and deaths
articles.title: India records nearly 80% decline in malaria cases and deaths from 2015 to 2025: President
articles.summary: President Droupadi Murmu announced a nearly 80 percent drop in malaria cases and deaths nationwide between 2015 and 2025 during the Golden Jubilee celebrations of the Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Malaria Research in New Delhi. Speaking on November 17, 2026, she highlighted progress in reducing high-burden districts while urging continued scientific research, surveillance, and community participation to eliminate the disease.
articles.description: President Droupadi Murmu inaugurated the Golden Jubilee celebrations of ICMR-NIMR, calling for sustained vigilance, effective surveillance and community participation

articles.headline: Ukrainian strikes cause catastrophic collapse of Crimean Bridge arch
articles.title: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded
articles.summary: Ukrainian long-range weaponry destroyed a major section of the Crimean Bridge in a multi-stage operation. President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that missiles and drones were utilized to target air defences before final strikes brought down a massive road arch into the Kerch Strait on November 17. Structural engineers described the damage as catastrophic, raising severe concerns regarding transport logistics and military resupply routes for Russian forces.
articles.description: One of the key symbols of Russia's occupation of Ukraine has suffered major damage after a seven-stage attack by Kyiv.

articles.headline: Amazon commits $7 billion to renewable energy projects in India
articles.title: Amazon to invest $7 billion in India renewables by 2030
articles.summary: Amazon announced a $7 billion investment in Indian renewable energy by 2030, expanding its existing $4 billion commitment. The technology giant will develop four new utility-scale wind and solar projects with a 934-megawatt capacity. These efforts aim to support India's net-zero emissions target by 2070 and reduce the carbon intensity of Amazon's global operations.
articles.description: The fresh investment is in addition to $4 billion already contracted in renewable energy investments in the country, making it one of India’s leading corporate purchasers of carbon-free energy, the company claims.

articles.headline: US intelligence reports allege potential Iranian threats in Washington
articles.title: Is Iran plotting a ‘dirty bomb’ attack in the US? What we know
articles.summary: United States intelligence reportedly indicates that Iran is planning attacks against senior officials in the administration of President Donald Trump using a dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, DC. The White House stated it is monitoring threats, though no credible dangers currently exist to the homeland. Meanwhile, Iran's mission to the United Nations categorically rejected the allegations as false and fabricated.
articles.description: A CNN report quoting unnamed US officials alleges Tehran is developing plans for an attack on officials in Washington.

articles.headline: US officials clash over chip export restrictions to China
articles.title: Bessent vs Lutnick: Who is winning the China chip debate?
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick are publicly divided over chip export policies. New rules now require licences for advanced chip sales to several countries suspected of acting as conduits to China. The dispute follows the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations of ties to Chinese intelligence.
articles.description: A rift has emerged in Trump’s cabinet over China’s access to advanced AI chips as export controls tighten.

articles.headline: U.S. imposes new licensing requirements on AI chip exports to Southeast Asia
articles.title: How new US chip restrictions on South East Asia will hit China
articles.summary: The United States has introduced interim rules requiring licenses for shipping advanced AI chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil. Washington aims to prevent Chinese firms from circumventing export controls by renting computing power from regional data centers. Beijing condemned the move as economic coercion, while affected nations seek to maintain trusted technology access.
