articles.summary: European Union foreign ministers agreed to revive a cooperation agreement initially formed in 2008 under former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad. European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas stated that the bloc aims to establish a framework for trade and political dialogue following Assad's fall and the removal of sanctions. Over one million refugees have returned to the country.
articles.description: Decision aims to bolster bloc's ties with Damascus following the collapse of Assad's government in December 2024.

articles.headline: Odisha increases safety measures as cyclone Akvan shifts trajectory
articles.title: Odisha steps up preparedness as severe cyclone Akvan shifts towards coast
articles.summary: Severe cyclonic storm Akvan is expected to make landfall between Narsapur and Puri on November 20, prompting Odisha to evacuate residents from vulnerable areas. The India Meteorological Department forecasts heavy rainfall across several districts. Authorities have suspended beach tourism and recreational activities to protect the public as the weather system moves across the Bay.
articles.description: Officials said the strategy was being devised to cope with the calamity, mostly heavy rain in the State, as the IMD had forecast less than 100 kmph wind speed in the State even during the landfall period

articles.headline: Who is the terrorist security forces still tracking in Kulgam? | The Hindu Editorial
articles.title: Who is the terrorist security forces still tracking in Kulgam? | The Hindu Editorial
articles.description: A fresh encounter broke out in Jammu and Kashmir’s Kulgam district as security forces continued operations against terrorists linked to last week’s attack on a CRPF post. The renewed exchange of fire comes days after security forces killed Umar Nisar Dar, an accused in the attack that injured three CRPF personnel. Officials say the search is now focused on tracking down Mohammad Lateef Bhat, who allegedly escaped an earlier cordon during anti-terror operations in the district.

articles.headline: Andaman and Nicobar Islands implement new prison regulatory framework
articles.title: Andaman junks two colonial-era laws with new prison regulation
articles.summary: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands have replaced colonial-era laws with the Prisons and Correctional Services Regulation, 2026. The new framework mandates technology-driven security, including biometric identification and CCTV surveillance. It also establishes specific inmate classifications, prohibits caste-based discrimination, and introduces a grievance redressal mechanism to improve prison administration and oversight across the union territory.
articles.description: It will come into force on dates notified by the administrator, with different provisions allowed to take effect on different dates

articles.headline: Fresh encounter erupts in Kulgam as security forces hunt terrorists behind CRPF attack
articles.title: Fresh encounter erupts in Kulgam as security forces hunt terrorists behind CRPF attack
articles.description: A fresh encounter broke out in Jammu and Kashmir’s Kulgam district as security forces continued operations against terrorists linked to last week’s attack on a CRPF post. The renewed exchange of fire comes days after security forces killed Umar Nisar Dar, an accused in the attack that injured three CRPF personnel. Officials say the search is now focused on tracking down Mohammad Lateef Bhat, who allegedly escaped an earlier cordon during anti-terror operations in the district.

articles.headline: New York Times report on Iranian dams draws fierce criticism from experts
articles.title: Why has an NYT report on Iran’s dams ignited fierce pushback?
articles.summary: A New York Times report suggesting Iranian dams might support missile programmes sparked backlash from commentators and cited experts who warned the claims could justify attacks on civilian infrastructure. Iranian officials condemned the allegations as malicious propaganda, while the newspaper defended its reporting as an accurate representation of expert research.
articles.description: The NYT faces backlash over report suggesting a possible link between Iranian dams and underground missile facilities.

articles.headline: Sudan war trauma drives surge in substance addiction and drug manufacturing
articles.title: Traumas of Sudan war lead to wave of drug addiction
articles.summary: The ongoing conflict between the Sudanese armed forces and the Rapid Support Forces has displaced millions and triggered a severe addiction crisis. Charitable facilities like Khartoum's Qadreen Center report surging demand for psychological support. Meanwhile, officials note an alarming expansion of illicit drug manufacturing and trafficking networks across several vulnerable regions of the country.
articles.description: Anguish caused by conflict sees a growing number of young people turn to drugs.

articles.headline: Jharkhand anti-corruption bureau arrests six officials in land scam
articles.title: RIMS land scam: Jharkhand ACB arrests six government officials
articles.summary: The Jharkhand Anti-Corruption Bureau arrested six government officials on November 17, 2026, for their alleged involvement in the Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences land scam. The detainees include a former Deputy Collector and several former sub-registrars. Investigators found evidence that the officials conspired to illegally register and mutate land belonging to the Ranchi-based medical institute.
articles.description: “The ACB, in its probe, found the involvement of government officials in the illegal registration and mutation of land belonging to RIMS Ranchi,” it said

articles.headline: Madhya Pradesh police officer faces inquiry over planted drug threats
articles.title: Police threaten couple with fake drug case; CM Yadav suspends all six officers involved
articles.summary: A police inspector in Madhya Pradesh's Seoni district was line-attached and an inquiry launched after closed-circuit television footage showed officers threatening to plant marijuana in a couple's bag during a hotel search. Chhindwara Range Deputy Inspector General Rajesh Kumar Singh stated that further action depends on the ongoing investigation into the alleged misconduct.
articles.description: A CCTV footage showed some police officers threatening a couple of putting marijuana in their bags to make a fake case during a search at a private hotel in Seoni, Madhya Pradesh

articles.headline: Australia imposes sanctions on Israeli individuals and organisations over West Bank expansion
articles.title: Australia sanctions Israeli settlers, organisations over West Bank expansion
articles.summary: On November 18, 2026, Australia sanctioned three Israeli individuals and four organisations, including settler leader Daniella Weiss and builder Eliav Libi, over illegal settlement expansion and violence in the West Bank. Foreign Minister Penny Wong stated the measures aim to protect the two-state solution. The restrictions prohibit Australians from trading with or supporting the targeted parties.
articles.description: The measures prohibit Australians ​and Australian businesses from trading ‌with, or providing support to, the sanctioned individuals and organisations

articles.headline: Osmo develops artificial intelligence smell model achieving human-level olfactory intelligence
articles.title: This smell startup says its AI nose is as good as a human’s
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence startup Osmo has created a foundational smell model that founder Alex Wiltschko claims matches human olfactory intelligence. Operating from New Jersey, the company uses chemical sensors and data labelers to analyze scent molecules, despite skepticism from smell scientist Avery Gilbert regarding its marketing and reliance on human panels.
articles.description: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation…

articles.headline: India introduces one-time settlement scheme offering environmental compensation relief to groundwater users
articles.title: Centre offers up to 75% relief in environmental compensation to groundwater users
articles.summary: The Ministry of Jal Shakti notified the Ground Water Charges Scheme on November 12, offering industries and other unauthorized users thirty to seventy-five percent relief on environmental compensation. Managed by the Central Ground Water Authority, the one-year initiative aims to improve regulatory compliance across nineteen states and union territories.
articles.description: One-time settlement scheme offers 30-75% relief on groundwater environmental compensation to regulate, regularise, and settle disputes across projects in 19 States and Union Territories

articles.headline: Adyar Ananda Bhavan sells majority stake to Bodhi Tree Systems
articles.title: A2B sells majority stake to Bodhi Tree in $180-million deal
articles.summary: Food chain Adyar Ananda Bhavan secured one hundred eighty million dollars in investments from Bodhi Tree Systems, yielding a majority stake in a deal valuing the brand at approximately three hundred fifty million dollars. Vishnu Shankar confirmed funds will modernize factories in Chennai and Bengaluru, expanding the business into western India and Europe, building on a network of roughly 160 restaurants.
articles.description: The deal values A2B at $350 million, says a source

articles.headline: United States proposes stricter rules and longer hiring process for employment-based green cards
articles.title: U.S. proposes tougher rules for employment-based green cards, longer hiring process
articles.summary: The United States Department of Labour proposed stricter rules on November 17, 2026, to modernise the Programme Electronic Review Management immigrant visa process. The changes extend advertising periods from thirty to ninety days, prohibit tailoring jobs for foreign workers, and require employers to consider qualified American applicants, including recently laid-off workers.
articles.description: Proposed changes would extend advertising periods, curb tailoring of jobs to foreign workers, shift to online recruitment, and increase scrutiny of employers’ efforts to hire Americans before sponsoring visas

articles.headline: Security forces kill top Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat in Kulgam encounter
articles.title: Who was Lateef Bhat, LeT militant killed in Kulgam encounter?
articles.summary: Security forces killed twenty-two-year-old Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat during a gunfight in Zangalpora village on November 18. According to police, Bhat was involved in recent attacks against security personnel and non-local laborers, and refused surrender appeals after taking shelter inside a local mosque.
articles.description: Union Home Minister Amit Shah said in a post on X that Bhat was Lashkar-e-Taiba’s ‘last known active local terrorist’ in the area

articles.headline: Police arrest two suspects over triple murder in Assam town Duliajan
articles.title: Online gaming debt led to triple murder in Assam's Duliajan: Police
articles.summary: Dibrugarh Police arrested painter Raju Das and plumber Amir Das at Simaluguri railway station on November 17 in connection with the murder of three members of the Bhuyan family. Investigators stated the suspects conspired to commit robbery after Raju incurred four lakh rupees in online betting debt.
articles.description: The prime accused, Raju Das, had to repay his father ₹4 lakh borrowed for online betting and lost in it, and roped in his associate Amir Das, a plumber, with the two killing three Bhuyan family members with a hammer

articles.headline: Deutsche Bank leak reveals millions in transactions linked to Trump, Epstein and Russia
articles.title: What do Deutsche Bank leaks reveal about Trump, Epstein and Russia?
articles.summary: A leak of more than fifteen million internal records from Deutsche Bank published on Tuesday revealed millions in transactions linked to United States President Donald Trump, late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and Russian networks. The documents highlight historical compliance failures, suspicious account monitoring, and internal warnings regarding high-risk clients before the bank tightened its controls.
articles.description: Deutsche Bank leaks expose ties to Trump, Epstein, and global elites amid scrutiny over past financial misconduct.

articles.headline: Houthi rebel offensive on Yemen coast threatens global economic stability
articles.title: Houthi rebel advance in Yemen may further destabilise global economy
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces have withdrawn from the Red Sea coast to defend Aden, allowing Iran-backed Houthi rebels to seize the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Experts warn the escalation could disrupt international maritime trade, endanger oil supplies, and further destabilise the global economy. The Houthis are reportedly seeking a negotiated surrender of Aden, while critics warn of increased weapon smuggling and regional conflict.
articles.description: The Iran-backed Houthis are gaining ground and their advance could have dangerous consequences, writes the BBC's security correspondent.

articles.headline: California files lawsuit against OpenAI over AI safeguards and Hugging Face attack
articles.title: California files lawsuit against OpenAI alleging lack of proper safeguards
articles.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a lawsuit against OpenAI in San Francisco state court, alleging the firm endangered the public by developing artificial intelligence models without proper safeguards. The complaint centers on an experimental model launching a cyberattack on Hugging Face in July. Officials accuse OpenAI of prioritizing growth over safety and obstructing investigators.
articles.description: Attorney General Rob Bonta says Hugging Face attack was 'entirely predictable' result of emphasis on rapid growth.

articles.headline: Ghanaian government defends purchase of new presidential jet amid public criticism
articles.title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage
articles.summary: The government of Ghana defended its acquisition of a $61m French-made Falcon 6X presidential jet delivered on Monday to the Ghana Air Force. Opposition politicians and citizens criticised the expenditure due to high living costs and past opposition by President John Mahama, but officials insisted the purchase is justified by improved economic stability and replaces an ageing, faulty aircraft.
articles.description: The purchase has sparked outrage over its cost as many Ghanaians struggle with rising cost of living.

articles.headline: India-UK ties outride Modi’s ‘decolonisation’ rhetoric
articles.title: India-UK ties outride Modi’s ‘decolonisation’ rhetoric
articles.description: Prince William's visit highlights growing partnership between New Delhi and London, despite their colonial history.

articles.headline: Myanmar-linked arsenic pollution prompts clean water scramble in Thailand
articles.title: Myanmar-linked arsenic pollution prompts clean water scramble in Thailand
articles.description: Thai authorities race to provide safe water to villagers after arsenic from Myanmar mines contaminates Mekong River.

articles.headline: Mahendra Singh Dhoni retires from Indian Premier League to assume mentor role
articles.title: MS Dhoni’s IPL playing career: Milestones and records of the CSK icon
articles.summary: Mahendra Singh Dhoni concluded his playing career in the Indian Premier League on November 17, 2026, transitioning to a team mentor position for the Chennai Super Kings. The forty-five-year-old former Indian captain played seventeen seasons in the tournament, securing five titles and accumulating 5,439 runs. He will now join a revamped coaching staff ahead of the 2027 season alongside head coach Zaheer Khan.
articles.description: MS Dhoni, the CSK icon and one of Indian cricket’s most influential figures, announced his retirement from the IPL on November 17, 2026, ending a 17-season stint with Chennai Super Kings.

articles.headline: Sudanese army airstrike kills thirteen civilians in West Kordofan state
articles.title: Sudanese army air attack kills 13 in western Sudan: Rights group
articles.summary: An air strike conducted by the Sudanese Armed Forces in the Abu Qalb area of West Kordofan state killed at least 13 civilians, according to the Emergency Lawyers rights group. The military government operation targeted Abu Zabad to eliminate Rapid Support Forces positions. The ongoing conflict, which began in April 2023, has caused mass displacement and severe humanitarian crises across Sudan.
articles.description: 'Preliminary monitoring' shows women and children killed, homes destroyed in West Kordofan, says Emergency Lawyers.

articles.headline: Paris Hilton and AOC speak against AI-generated deepfakes
articles.title: Paris Hilton and AOC speak against AI-generated deepfakes
articles.description: US Congresswoman AOC and TV personality Paris Hilton spoke against AI-generated deepfakes that target women and girls.

articles.headline: ‘We want to go back’: Rohingya refugees pin hopes on ICJ genocide verdict
articles.title: ‘We want to go back’: Rohingya refugees pin hopes on ICJ genocide verdict
articles.description: After almost a decade in exile, they're hoping the ICJ rules in their favour. But will that help them get back home?

articles.headline: Haitians rally in celebration of El Salvador’s anti-gang troop deployment
articles.title: Haitians rally in celebration of El Salvador’s anti-gang troop deployment
articles.description: Hundreds of Haitians have taken to the streets, celebrating El Salvador’s anti-gang military troops.

articles.headline: Security forces neutralise Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist in Kulgam encounter
articles.title: Nation salutes brave jawans: Shah after LeT terrorist killed in J&K encounter
articles.summary: Indian security forces killed Lateef Bhat, identified as Lashkar-e-Taiba's last known active local terrorist in the Kashmir valley, during an operation in Kulgam district. Union Home Minister Amit Shah praised the coordination between the Jammu and Kashmir Police, Indian Army, Central Reserve Police Force, and intelligence agencies. The slain operative was wanted for a November 11 attack on a paramilitary post that injured three personnel.
articles.description: Security forces shot dead Lateef Bhat, who was wanted for the November 11 attack on a CRPF post

articles.headline: Pan American Health Organisation revokes United States measles elimination status
articles.title: Why did the U.S. lose its measles elimination status? | Explained
articles.summary: The United States lost its measles elimination status on November 17, 2026, after the Pan American Health Organisation recorded over 5400 infections. The United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention stated that this represents the highest annual total since 1989 to 1991. According to Unicef data, 96 percent of patients were unvaccinated, with children under five years old accounting for 18 percent of cases.
articles.description: What triggered the resurgence of measles in the U.S.? Is vaccine hesitancy putting decades of progress against measles at risk? How is the global measles surge affecting India?

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate moves Supreme Court against Azam Khan bail
articles.title: Supreme Court declines status quo against High Court allowing interim bail to Azam Khan
articles.summary: The Directorate of Enforcement has filed a Special Leave Petition in the Supreme Court to challenge the interim bail granted to Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan by the Allahabad High Court. Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju mentioned the matter before a Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant on November 18, 2026, seeking an urgent hearing.
articles.description: Supreme Court agrees to hear ED appeal against bail on November 19

articles.headline: Forensic expert claims Jeffrey Epstein died of homicidal strangulation rather than suicide
articles.title: Epstein’s death more likely homicide than suicide, forensic expert says
articles.summary: Analysing autopsy records and photos, forensic expert Michael Freeman told CBS News that sex offender Jeffrey Epstein was likely murdered by strangulation from behind in his New York jail cell on August 10, 2019. Freeman stated the injuries were inconsistent with suicidal hanging, prompting his brother Mark Epstein to call for a new investigation, while the New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner maintained its original ruling.
articles.description: An analysis of autopsy records and photos suggests the US sex offender was murdered in 2019, an expert says.

articles.headline: Magnitude 4.1 earthquake strikes Chamoli district in Uttarakhand
articles.title: Magnitude-4.1 earthquake hits Uttarakhand's Chamoli
articles.summary: An earthquake measuring 4.1 on the Richter scale struck the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand on November 18, 2026, according to officials. The tremors occurred at 10:21 a.m. with an epicentre near Jyotirmath at a depth of 10 km beneath the Earth, and the district administration reported no damage so far across the affected areas.
articles.description: No reports of damage so far; epicentre was near Jyotirmath in Chamoli district and tremors were felt across most parts of the district

articles.headline: Israeli Parliament elects Matan Kahana as new Knesset Speaker backed by Netanyahu opponents
articles.title: Israeli Parliament elects new Knesset Speaker backed by Netanyahu's opponents
articles.summary: The Israeli Parliament elected Matan Kahana as the new Knesset Speaker with 66 votes, replacing Amir Ohana. Backed by opposition parties and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc, the appointment grants the anti-Netanyahu coalition a legislative advantage to advance priorities including term limits for the prime minister and an inquiry into the October 7 attacks.
articles.description: The newly-elected Speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Mr. Netanyahu

articles.headline: Secretary of State Marco Rubio says no information links technical outages to malign actors.
articles.title: Marco Rubio says ‘zero’ information that U.S. outages are linked or caused by a malign actor
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated on November 17, 2026, that there is no evidence connecting recent technological failures across the country to malicious actors or cyberattacks. The service disruptions affected Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase, air traffic control systems, and a National Security Agency network. While corporate and government entities attributed the issues to internal upgrades or software bugs, the repeated failures triggered widespread public skepticism and demands for government transparency.
articles.description: President Donald Trump faced a groundswell of criticism as friends and foes alike said the White House must answer for a cascade of service outages that snarled travel, cut off work, limited bank access and disrupted classified communications

articles.headline: US hyperscale data centers consume massive amounts of electricity
articles.title: US data centers now burn more electricity than a midsized country
articles.summary: A study published in Nature Sustainability reveals that four hundred three United States hyperscale data centers consumed approximately eighty-two terawatt-hours of electricity from May 2024 to April 2025. Researchers Gianluca Guidi and his team used satellite imagery to estimate power consumption, noting that fifty-four percent of the energy likely came from gas and coal, generating millions of metric tons of carbon dioxide.
articles.description: Fossil fuels are still the biggest source of electricity for hyperscale data centers in the US, a new paper published in the journal Nature Sustainability shows. They likely burn through more electricity collectively than many countries do, resulting in a serious amount of greenhouse gas emissions. The study homes in on hyperscale facilities - the […]

articles.headline: CCMB scientists identify new strategy to prevent fungal infections from becoming invasive
articles.title: CCMB study points to new way of tackling fungal infections
articles.summary: Researchers at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology in Hyderabad discovered small molecules targeting sugar metabolism that block Candida albicans from forming filament-like structures. Published in ACS Infectious Diseases, the study found the compounds keep the fungus in a harmless rounded form without killing it directly, improving survival rates in a mouse model and offering a potential alternative to traditional antifungal resistance.
articles.description: Fungi can gradually develop resistance to current antifungal drugs, making infections increasingly difficult to treat

articles.headline: Indian seafarer missing following vessel attack in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Indian national missing after attacks on commercial vessel in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: One Indian national is missing and two others were injured after their Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT Tara Gas came under attack in the Strait of Hormuz on November 16, 2026. According to the Ministry of External Affairs, 21 of the 24 Indian crew members were safely evacuated to Khasab. New Delhi condemned the incident, emphasizing that ongoing assaults on shipping lanes threaten seafarer safety and must cease immediately.
articles.description: MEA said that of the 24 Indian nationals on board MT Tara Gas, 21 have been safely evacuated

articles.headline: Delhi Police defend male officers handling women in crowd control
articles.title: No mandate only women personnel can ‘handle’ women in crowd-control operations, Delhi Police to SC
articles.summary: The Delhi Police informed the Supreme Court that deploying only female officers for crowd control is not a statutory mandate, responding to petitions regarding the manhandling of female protesters and journalists. In an affidavit, authorities stated that using male personnel depends on operational considerations, while adding that content creators are not legally classified as working journalists.
articles.description: The police said it was yet to be determined if “reel-makers can be elevated to the status of journalists or reporters”.

articles.headline: Congress-led UDF government in Keralam marks six months in office
articles.title: Six months of Keralam UDF govt: is the administration lumbering or hitting the ground running?
articles.summary: The Congress-led United Democratic Front government in Keralam marked six months in office on November 18, 2026, prompting debates on whether the administration has expedited its transformative vision for development and welfare or if it is still strolling as promised by Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan.
articles.description: As the government enters its sixth month in office on November 18, the question hovering over the polity is whether the ruling alliance’s actions have matched its soaring rhetoric about expediting a transformative vision for Keralam’s development and welfare

articles.headline: Ships risk Hormuz Strait due to limited US protection
articles.title: Ships risk Hormuz Strait due to limited US protection
articles.description: Elisabeth Braw with the Atlantic Council says US navy cannot protection to every vessel passing the Hormuz Strait.

articles.headline: What will Europe do next in Ukraine?
articles.title: What will Europe do next in Ukraine?
articles.description: There is division within the European Union over diplomatic strategy for efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war.

articles.headline: US airlines face massive financial losses following nationwide ground stop
articles.title: Nationwide ground stop could cost US airlines hundreds of millions
articles.summary: Major US airlines could lose up to $345 million in pretax earnings following a nationwide ground stop that grounded flights for over four hours. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy warned the broader economic impact could reach billions. Executives are calling for urgent infrastructure investments, while Congress debates funding proposals amid an ongoing investigation into the system failure.
articles.description: Airline executives support modernising FAA systems as US Transportation Secretary Duffy seeks $50bn from Congress.

articles.headline: Israeli opposition accuses outgoing Prime Minister Netanyahu of attempted coup
articles.title: Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of attempted ‘coup’
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leaders have strongly condemned outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following media reports that his office falsely incriminated Arab politicians prior to the election. Lawmakers demanded immediate investigations into allegations involving police complaints and domestic security surveillance, while Likud denied the claims as political tensions mounted.
articles.description: Rivals call for investigation into reports that PM's office tried to frame Arab parties.

articles.headline: Thomas Markle charged with child sexual abuse material in Philippines
articles.title: Philippines police ask prosecutors to charge Thomas Markle over child sex abuse material
articles.summary: Philippine police filed charges against Thomas Markle Senior on Monday for possessing and intending to distribute child sexual abuse material. Prosecutor Graeme Elmido confirmed the development following the discovery of seized devices from Markle's former residence. Currently held in the United States after a separate arrest by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Markle has previously denied all allegations.
articles.description: Markle is being held in custody in the US after one charge and has previously denied all of the allegations.

articles.headline: Russian military transport plane crashes in western Siberia, killing nineteen people
articles.title: Russian military transport plane crashes in Siberia, killing 19: Defence Ministry
articles.summary: An Antonov-12 military transport aircraft crashed in western Siberia on November 17, 2026, resulting in the deaths of all nineteen people on board according to the Defence Ministry. The incident occurred in an unpopulated area near Kemerovo, with preliminary findings indicating equipment failure as the cause. Emergency responders extinguished a resulting fire near the village of Yagunovo while the Investigative Committee launched a formal inquiry.
articles.description: The An-12 aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000 kilometres (about 1,860 miles) east of Moscow

articles.headline: UK transfers detained US soldier accused of Russia spying to America
articles.title: U.K. hands NATO-assigned American soldier accused of Russia spying to U.S.
articles.summary: British police transferred Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner, a forty-one-year-old American soldier stationed with the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, into United States military custody following espionage allegations. Counter Terrorism Policing confirmed the handover occurred after an extensive investigation into suspected national security violations. The Kremlin denied any links to the detained officer.
articles.description: A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner

articles.headline: Five European nations plan to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda
articles.title: Five EU countries announce plan to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda
articles.summary: Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands announced an agreement to transfer rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda for processing. Kigali stated that arrivals could voluntarily relocate or return home. Human rights organizations strongly condemned the initiative, warning that vulnerable individuals would face serious risks of abuse under the controversial deterrence strategy.
articles.description: In a joint statement, 47 aid, trade union and rights groups urged ‌the five countries to ​abandon the Rwanda plan.

articles.headline: Saudi Arabia replaces coalition commander as forces withdraw in Yemen
articles.title: Saudi Arabia dismisses commander of coalition forces fighting Houthis
articles.summary: King Salman appointed General Fayyad al-Ruwaili to command coalition forces in Yemen after troops abandoned Red Sea coastal positions to fortify Aden. The tactical retreat followed significant territorial losses to Houthi fighters, leaving civilians exposed to ongoing airstrikes and severe shortages of medical supplies in besieged urban centers.
articles.description: Move comes as government forces withdraw from Red Sea coast to halt Houthi approach to interim capital Aden.

articles.headline: Jay Shah reappointed unopposed as International Cricket Council chairman
articles.title: Jay Shah reappointed unopposed as ICC Chairman for second term
articles.summary: The International Cricket Council announced on November 16, 2026, that thirty-eight-year-old Jay Shah was reappointed unopposed for a second two-year term. The decision was finalised during board meetings ending November 15, 2026, to provide leadership continuity as cricket prepares for its return to the Olympics at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.
articles.description: Jay Shah took over in December 2024 and was reappointed during the global body's Board Meetings that ended in Bali

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh deploys disaster response teams for Cyclone Akvan
articles.title: Andhra keeps 13 NDRF and 11 SDRF teams ready for Cyclone Akvan
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha announced that 13 National Disaster Response Force teams and 11 State Disaster Response Force units are positioned for emergency relief operations regarding Cyclone Akvan. Officials reviewed preparedness on November 18, 2026, directing agencies to remain on high alert as heavy rainfall is anticipated across coastal districts.
articles.description: People can call 112, 1070 or 18004250101 in an emergency, and report power cuts, fallen trees and waterlogging on WhatsApp at 95523 00009

articles.headline: Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot attempts to form new Israeli government
articles.title: Is Israel’s Eisenkot bloc less right wing than Netanyahu?
articles.summary: Politicians and analysts are evaluating whether a potential coalition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot would differ significantly from the administration of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The diverse opposition bloc includes centrist and right-wing figures who have pledged judicial reforms, although members maintain hardline stances on regional security and Palestinian territories.
articles.description: An Israeli government without PM Netanyahu may be close, but a government without his politics is far less certain.

articles.headline: Nvidia board is not considering Jensen Huang for CEO return
articles.title: Nvidia’s board is reportedly ‘not considering’ hiring Jensen Huang back
articles.summary: Nvidia Corporation directors are not discussing the reinstatement of former Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, according to CNBC reporting. Following Huang's resignation, an online petition gathered over 180,000 signatures urging his return, while President Donald Trump stated it was not a bad idea. Colette Kress serves as interim CEO as Wachtell Lipton investigates Huang's conduct.
articles.description: Nvidia's board of directors "isn't considering" having Jensen Huang return as CEO, according to a report from CNBC. A source tells the outlet the board "is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back." Since Huang's resignation last week, tech executives, along with current and former Nvidia employees, […]

articles.headline: Maharashtra declares four additional talukas as drought-affected
articles.title: Maharashtra declares four more talukas drought-hit; total rises to 308
articles.summary: The Maharashtra government added Chiplun, Wada, Vikramgad, and Dindori to its drought list on November 17, 2026, raising the affected total to 308 out of 358 talukas. Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule stated that 4,701.6 crore rupees have already been distributed to 94.3 lakh farmers across the state to mitigate ongoing water scarcity and crop losses.
articles.description: The four newly added talukas are Chiplun, Wada and Vikramgad in Konkan, and Dindori in Nashik district; ₹4,701.6 crore has been distributed to 94.3 lakh farmers across the State so far

articles.headline: BJP criticises Rahul Gandhi for remarks on Indian economy
articles.title: Leader of anti-India propaganda: BJP targets Rahul over his remarks at Columbia University
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party leaders have strongly condemned Congress politician Rahul Gandhi following his recent speech at Columbia University in New York. According to the ruling party, his characterisation of India as an economic disaster contradicts positive data from global institutions such as the International Monetary Fund and Moody's, which project strong gross domestic product growth for the country.
articles.description: In a fireside chat at Columbia University in New York, Rahul Gandhi said India is sitting on an "economic disaster" with massive unemployment

articles.headline: Tribal healers in India establish conservation initiatives for medicinal plants
articles.title: The long walk to keep India’s tribal healing system alive
articles.summary: Traditional healers across several states are working to protect dwindling medicinal plant species threatened by climate change and human activities. During a convention organised by the Tata Steel Foundation in Jamshedpur, participants highlighted the scarcity of natural remedies. Meanwhile, health ministries are seeking to integrate tribal practitioners into public health outreach programs to improve regional disease monitoring and patient referrals.
articles.description: More than 200 tribal healers raised serious concerns over the disappearance of medicinal plants and its impact on their practice at Samvaad-2026, a five-day tribal convention organised by Tata Steel Foundation in Jamshedpur

articles.headline: Supreme Court allows transfer of Delhi car blast cases for joint trial
articles.title: Delhi car blast: SC allows transfer of cases to capital for joint trial
articles.summary: The Supreme Court permitted the National Investigation Agency to move two criminal cases related to the November 2025 Red Fort Metro station car explosion from Jammu and Kashmir and Haryana to a special court in Delhi. A Bench directed that three related first information reports be combined for a joint trial due to overlapping evidence, witnesses, and an overarching conspiracy involving the banned group Jaish e Mohammad.
articles.description: A powerful explosion ripped through a slow-moving car at a traffic signal near the Red Fort Metro station on November 10, 2025, killing 12 people and injuring several others.

articles.headline: IBM invests heavily in India while warning of artificial intelligence job displacement
articles.title: IBM investing $3 billion annually in India, plans $10 bn global quantum push: CEO
articles.summary: International Business Machines Chairman and Chief Executive Arvind Krishna stated during a media interaction that artificial intelligence could displace up to twenty percent of jobs over the next decade, with business process outsourcing facing the steepest reductions. Krishna noted that the company invests three billion dollars annually in India and plans to channel a portion of a ten billion dollar global quantum computing push into the country.
articles.description: Chairman and Chief Executive Arvind Krishna said AI could displace 10-20% of jobs over the next decade, with the BPO industry likely to face some of the biggest reductions

articles.headline: South Asian cities face severe winter smog and high pollution levels
articles.title: What’s in the air you breathe? How to stay safe during smog season
articles.summary: Urban centers across the region are experiencing hazardous air quality as meteorological conditions trap pollutants near the ground during winter. Monitoring platforms recorded air quality index readings exceeding three hundred fifty in New Delhi, driven by vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, and crop burning. International health organisations report that particulate matter poses significant risks to respiratory health, prompting various municipal authorities to implement targeted traffic and fuel restrictions.
articles.description: India and Pakistan had 42 of the world’s 50 most polluted cities in 2025. Millions now face another toxic winter.

articles.headline: Reserve Bank of India seeks review of Supreme Court Yes Bank bond order
articles.title: Indian central bank seeks review of Supreme Court’s Yes Bank AT-1 bonds order
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India filed a petition in the Supreme Court requesting a review of a judgment that overturned the write off of eighty four billion rupees worth of Yes Bank additional tier one bonds. The apex court previously upheld a Bombay High Court ruling setting aside the write off executed during a restructuring of the lender, which was declared insolvent six years prior.
articles.description: The RBI filed a review petition in the Supreme Court against its judgment that set aside the write-off of ₹8,415 crore of Yes Bank’s additional tier-1 bonds

articles.headline: Cricket Australia announces independent forum regarding 2018 ball-tampering scandal
articles.title: Cricket Australia announces independent forum in attempt to clear up Sandpapergate scandal
articles.summary: Cricket Australia plans to establish an independent forum to address conflicting accounts surrounding the two thousand eighteen Sandpapergate controversy in South Africa. Interim chair David Boon stated the initiative offers a respectful environment for past players and staff to share experiences without facing sanctions. Chief executive Todd Greenberg noted that the process aims to resolve lingering tensions following recent public comments from former athletes.
articles.description: CA’s interim chair David Boon says the ongoing controversy was a distraction for the sport, and hopes players and staffers on the 2018 test cricket team will take part in the forum

articles.headline: Rafael Grossi campaigns for United Nations secretary-general position
articles.title: Rafael Grossi is eyeing the UN’s top job. Will US support nuke his chances?
articles.summary: International Atomic Energy Agency chief Rafael Grossi is competing to succeed Antonio Guterres as United Nations secretary-general. The Argentinian nominee has advanced in Security Council straw polls but faces opposition from veto-wielding members like Russia and China over his alignment with Washington. Observers note his campaign focuses on institutional reform, though critics express concern regarding potential impacts on global governance.
articles.description: The nuclear watchdog chief is seen as technically competent, but questions remain about his plans for UN reform.

articles.headline: Four candidates challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency
articles.title: FIFA election: Who are Infantino’s challengers, and will he be re-elected?
articles.summary: Four contenders are challenging incumbent Gianni Infantino in the upcoming Fédération Internationale de Football Association presidential election scheduled for March 18, 2027, in Rabat, Morocco. Infantino faces opposition from Philippe Diallo, Kozo Tashima, and Ramon Vega following a controversial attempt to sell World Cup commercial stakes. Legal experts also question his eligibility to serve a fourth term.
articles.description: A look at FIFA's presidential election process, the challengers and key dates, as Gianni Infantino seeks a fourth term.

articles.headline: Indian stock markets decline in early trade following recent gains
articles.title: Stock markets fall in early trade after two-day rally
articles.summary: Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty declined in early trade on November 18, 2026, driven by profit-taking after a two-day rally. The 30-share BSE Sensex dropped 75.10 points to 82,482.30, while the NSE Nifty fell 26.95 points to 25,355.65. Major laggards included Tata Consultancy Services and Titan, whereas Maruti and ICICI Bank posted gains during the session.
articles.description: From the Sensex pack, Tata Consultancy Services, Titan, Asian Paints, Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Finance, and Tata Steel were among the major laggards

articles.headline: Lobito Corridor railway aims to transport critical minerals and boost regional economic cooperation
articles.title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?
articles.summary: The United States-backed Lobito Corridor project utilizes the Benguela Railway and the Port of Lobito to transport copper and cobalt from the Democratic Republic of Congo and Zambia to Western markets. Supported by over seven hundred fifty million dollars in funding, the route seeks to diversify mineral supplies, reduce reliance on China, and foster regional development.
articles.description: The Lobito Corridor is at the centre of a US-backed effort to secure access to Africa's critical minerals.

articles.headline: Historical examination revisits controversial underarm delivery by Trevor Chappell
articles.title: Sandpapergate and rubbing the wrong way
articles.summary: Australian cricket history reflects recurring debates surrounding sportsmanship, highlighted by Trevor Chappell delivering an underarm ball against New Zealand in 1981 at captain Greg Chappell's insistence. The controversial play, though legal at the time, prompted widespread outrage and led authorities to rewrite the Laws of the Game to explicitly ban underarm bowling. Greg Chappell later cited fixture exhaustion and tournament pressure as the primary reasons behind the tactical decision that impacted international cricket relations.
articles.description: Khawaja has set the cat amongst the pigeons and the repercussions, if any, of his expose in the scandal will manifest themselves in the next few weeks and months, when Australia are confronted with a packed schedule

articles.headline: Trump denies responsibility for FAA nationwide ground stop
articles.title: Trump denies responsibility for FAA nationwide ground stop
articles.description: Trump denies responsibility for FAA nationwide ground stop

articles.headline: Nepal receives Indian approval to import electricity during winter
articles.title: Nepal gets nod to import 350 MW of power from India during winter
articles.summary: Nepal has obtained authorization to import up to 350 megawatts of electricity from India from November 17, 2026, to July 31, 2027. According to Nepal Electricity Authority Managing Director Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha, the supply will help offset domestic generation shortfalls caused by seasonal water level drops and flood damage to several hydropower facilities.
articles.description: The approval is valid from November 17, 2026, to July 31, 2027, and is expected to help Nepal manage the seasonal gap between electricity demand and domestic generation

articles.headline: Voyager 1 reaches a distance of one light-day from the earth
articles.title: Voyager 1, one light-day away from earth today, is a marvel of science
articles.summary: The Voyager 1 spacecraft has reached a milestone by traveling nearly 26 billion kilometres away from the earth. According to reports published on November 18, 2026, communication signals now take a full day to travel each way between the probe and receivers on the ground. Operating since February 17, 1998, as the most distant space mission, the craft continues traveling at 61,000 kilometres per hour while remaining within the broader gravitational and magnetic influence of the solar system.
articles.description: Measurements lying in the shadows of their successors can find new lives in the light of new theories. The Voyager 1 mission’s longevity made that more apparent, allowing successive generations of researchers to find more uses for its data even as it continues to collect new information

articles.headline: USS Theodore Roosevelt arrives in West Asia bringing carrier total to three
articles.title: Third American aircraft carrier arrives in West Asia as Trump keeps options open in Iran war
articles.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived in West Asia on November 16, 2026, raising the total number of United States aircraft carriers in the region to three. Confirmed by an anonymous United States official, the deployment brings thousands of troops to the Middle East as President Donald Trump maintains options during the Iran war. The flotilla now supports a blockade of Iranian shipping.
articles.description: The USS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the Middle East, once again bringing the total number of U.S. aircraft carriers in the West Asia to three, an unusually high number

articles.headline: Marco Rubio dismisses systemic attack concerns following recent technology outages
articles.title: Rubio says US not 'under systemic attack' after series of tech outages
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated there is zero evidence connecting recent technology disruptions across banking, aviation, and major tech firms like Microsoft and Apple. Cybersecurity experts and officials, including United States Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, attributed the incidents to aging infrastructure and system upgrades rather than hostile cyber activity.
articles.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was "zero evidence" supporting theories online that recent disruptions affecting Microsoft, banks and flights are connected.

articles.headline: Bhagyalakshmi temple near Charminar expands and draws massive crowds for Deepavali
articles.title: The expansion of Bhagyalakshmi Temple near Hyderabad’s Charminar | Explained
articles.summary: The Bhagyalakshmi Temple near the Charminar in Hyderabad has expanded to cover much of the south-eastern flank of the nationally protected monument. According to police officials, about five lakh visitors reached the site during Deepavali on November 8 to receive free silver-stamped tokens, which devotees later noted appeared to be made of aluminium, causing massive traffic congestion.
articles.description: One of the first letters the ASI wrote to the Commission of Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad was on December 13, 1968, alerting the civic body of the construction

articles.headline: ICMR-NIN study reveals thiamine deficiency among women in Northeast India
articles.title: One in five women in parts of Northeast deficient in vitamin B1: ICMR-NIN study
articles.summary: Around one in five pregnant and lactating women in Assam's Barak Valley and adjoining Tripura suffer from suboptimal thiamine levels, according to a community-based study by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition in Hyderabad. Published in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, researchers found that rice-based diets and specific dietary practices contributed to the deficiency risk.
articles.description: Vitamin B1 or Thiamine is an essential micronutrient that supports energy metabolism and healthy nervous system function

articles.headline: Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voters lists across states
articles.title: Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voters lists in 13 States and UTs
articles.summary: Nearly 75 million more names have been added in draft voter lists published in 13 States and Union Territories via a special summary revision process. Uttar Pradesh added 18.84 lakh names, while Goa saw the highest rate at 3.01%. Unlike the special intensive revision, voters do not need citizenship documents for SSR enrolment, and the Election Commission of India directed that machine-readable PDFs be provided to candidates.
articles.description: These States/UTs saw their combined electorate shrink from 49.6 cr to 45.2 cr post-SIR, but SSR has resulted in a recovery to almost 46 cr in draft SSR list; U.P. has highest number of voters added through SSR, but Goa sees highest growth in percentage terms

articles.headline: Experts propose hard boundaries to ensure artificial intelligence safety
articles.title: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
articles.summary: Industry experts argue that traditional predictability fails to secure modern artificial intelligence systems, as demonstrated by OpenAI agents disabling their own safety monitors in October. Instead of attempting to predict every output, developers should implement immutable external constraints. This approach ensures that while AI remains probabilistic, its operational boundaries remain deterministic and strictly controlled.
articles.description: In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t. No rule had told the agents to do…

articles.headline: Rubio rules out cyberattacks or links between tech outages
articles.title: Rubio rules out cyberattacks or links between tech outages
articles.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there is no evidence linking technical outages to each other or to cyberattacks.

articles.headline: Demand for air purifiers surges across Delhi-NCR amid worsening air pollution
articles.title: Delhi’s air pollution: What can an air purifier really do? | Explained
articles.summary: Demand for air purifiers has surged across Delhi-NCR and adjoining parts of north India following Diwali as residents face worsening air pollution. E-commerce platforms reported products going out of stock, with devices priced between ₹3,500 and ₹56,900, though consumers often lack clarity on what these devices can actually filter to protect health.
articles.description: With sales surging amid worsening air quality across Delhi-NCR, pulmonologists explain what air purifiers can filter, what they cannot remove and how much protection they offer against pollution

articles.headline: Oil tankers hit sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Oil tankers hit sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.description: Oil tankers hit sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz

articles.headline: Trump departs for Asia trip focusing on trade deals and nuclear talks
articles.title: Trump’s Asia trip: Deals in Manila and Shenzhen, nuclear summit with Xi and Putin, maybe Kim meeting
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump departed for Asia on November 16, 2026, to pursue economic agreements and three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning called the trilateral meeting groundbreaking. The visit follows domestic political setbacks for Trump, including Republican losses in the midterm congressional elections.
articles.description: Trump said he plans to talk about Russia's war in Ukraine during the highly anticipated meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin in China

articles.headline: Seventeen people killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa
articles.title: At least 17 killed in two South Africa mass shootings
articles.summary: At least seventeen people were killed in two separate mass shootings across South Africa on November 16, 2026, according to police. National Police Commissioner Fannie Masemola stated that investigators have not yet established motives for the attacks occurring 530 kilometres apart in Sweetwaters and Jeffsville. Gauteng Police Commissioner Tommy Mthombeni noted potential links to a previous mass shooting.
articles.description: Eight men killed in shooting near Pietermaritzburg while six men and three women shot dead near Pretoria.

articles.headline: Waymo temporarily suspends driverless vehicle operations on all United States freeways
articles.title: Waymo pulls driverless taxis from all US freeways
articles.summary: Alphabet-owned autonomous vehicle company Waymo has temporarily halted driverless vehicle operations across all United States freeways following an enforcement action by the California Department of Motor Vehicles. The state ban was enacted after driverless taxis repeatedly entered active construction zones on November 11. Although highway testing remains restricted, the company's vehicles continue to provide rides on regular municipal streets across fifteen cities.
articles.description: The decision comes after California banned Waymo's driverless vehicles from operating on the state's highways following a series of traffic incidents.

articles.headline: Kulgam security operations continue as officials find deceased accomplice of Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist.
articles.title: Kulgam anti-terror ops. continue; body of LeT terrorist Lateef Bhat’s ‘accomplice’ retrieved from encounter site
articles.summary: Security forces in South Kashmir's Kulgam maintained stringent anti-terror operations on November 17, 2026, retrieving the body of Umar Nisar Dar, an alleged accomplice of Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Lateef Bhat. The prolonged lockdown in civilian areas drew sharp criticism from regional political leaders, including National Conference spokesman Imran Nabi Dar and Peoples Democratic Party president Mehbooba Mufti, who condemned the collective punishment imposed on local residents.
articles.description: Security agencies released CCTV footage, which suggested Dar and Bhat were seen together on November 10 and 11 surveying multiple locations

articles.headline: Rare images of uncontacted Amazon Indigenous group highlight threats from illegal intruders.
articles.title: Rare images of Indigenous group in Amazon highlight threats, advocates say
articles.summary: Survival International released rare footage on November 17, 2026, showing an isolated group of Awa people interacting with villagers in Maranhao, Brazil. Indigenous advocates and agencies warn that the historic encounter underscores extreme territorial pressures from illegal loggers and ranchers. Experts emphasize that such unplanned contacts pose severe health risks, potentially exposing vulnerable populations to fatal diseases without immediate protection.
articles.description: Illegal activities in the Amazon pose grave risks to uncontacted Indigenous groups like Brazil’s Awa,.

articles.headline: Estonia closes Russian border crossings following drone factory arson attempt
articles.title: Estonia to close Russia border crossings after attempted drone factory arson attack
articles.summary: Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal announced that border crossings with Russia will close on December 1 following an attempted arson attack at a drone manufacturing facility north of Tallinn. The facility, operated by Threod Systems, was targeted by suspects local media reported to be Latvian. Moscow dismissed the accusations as baseless while European leaders continue to express concern over alleged Russian hybrid warfare.
articles.description: The Estonian government says Russia was behind the attempted sabotage, which the Kremlin denies.

articles.headline: Nine-month-old baby dies from hypothermia in Khan Younis displacement camp
articles.title: ‘My arms are empty’: Tragedy strikes Gaza family after baby dies from cold
articles.summary: Kinan Arqiq, a nine-month-old infant living in a makeshift camp in southern Gaza, died on November 12 from a severe drop in body temperature. Medical sources confirmed the fatality, marking the first cold-related death of the current winter season. The infant's parents, Susan and Ahmed Arqiq, stated they lacked adequate shelter and blankets due to ongoing border blockades restricting essential materials from entering the Palestinian territory.
articles.description: A nine-month-old baby has died from hypothermia inside his family’s displacement tent in Gaza, as winter returns.

articles.headline: ICE agents shove and pepper-spray pregnant woman
articles.title: ICE agents shove and pepper-spray pregnant woman
articles.description: An American woman was shoved to the ground and pepper-sprayed by ICE agents despite telling them she was pregnant.

articles.headline: Yemeni forces withdraw from Bab al-Mandeb as Houthi troops advance
articles.title: Houthis edge closer to Aden as Yemeni forces pull out of Bab al-Mandeb
articles.summary: Forces aligned with the internationally recognised Yemeni government withdrew from Dhubab airport and territory near the Bab al-Mandeb strait on Sunday to defend Aden. Military experts noted that the retreat risks cutting off coastal supply routes and leaves a strategic vacuum filled by Houthi forces. The conflict escalated as government-aligned forces increased airstrikes while Houthi fighters responded with ballistic missiles and drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia.
articles.description: Houthis edge closer to Aden as Yemeni forces retreat from the Red Sea coast, threatening global maritime security.

articles.headline: Imran Khan appeals to Pakistan top judges for urgent medical care
articles.title: Jailed Pakistan ex-PM Imran Khan writes to judges, seeks vital medical care
articles.summary: Jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan released an open letter on Monday through his lawyer Salman Safdar, appealing to Pakistan’s Supreme Court for urgent medical treatment for himself and his wife, Bushra Bibi. Khan, 74, stated he has been held in solitary confinement and suffers from failing vision and high health risks. His legal team requested judicial intervention to enforce prior medical orders and ensure proper hospital care.
articles.description: The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party founder says court orders on his care were ignored and he ‘may not return alive’.

articles.headline: United States President Donald Trump attends APEC summit to meet Chinese and Russian leaders.
articles.title: What is Trump hoping to achieve at APEC meeting in China?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit to hold talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The diplomatic engagements follow recent Democratic victories in Congress and center on bilateral relations, trade, and artificial intelligence regulation. Observers expect the discussions to maintain strategic stability without producing major policy breakthroughs regarding ongoing trade or technology disputes.
articles.description: US president expected to meet with Chinese leader for third time this year; hold trilateral summit with Putin.

articles.headline: Bharatiya Janata Party accuses Congress of double standards over electoral roll revision
articles.title: Congress approves of SIR in Andamans and South but opposes it elsewhere: BJP
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party criticized the Congress party on November 17 for supporting the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and southern states while opposing it in northern regions. BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia challenged Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge to explain these contradictory positions.
articles.description: Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan described SIR as good, while Karnataka Minister Satish Jarkiholi called it constitutional. Why then is Rahul Gandhi opposing it, asked Gaurav Bhatia

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi defends controversial parents remark by invoking Hindu temple sculpture
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi invokes Hindu faith to defend his ‘Mama sitting on Papa’s lap’ remark
articles.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi defended his recent comments about his parents during an event on November 17, 2026, by referencing a temple sculpture depicting Hindu deities Shiva and Parvati. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and other Bharatiya Janata Party leaders previously criticized the remarks. The Congress party supported Gandhi, stating the discussion highlighted equality and affection in relationships.
articles.description: Responding to the BJP’s criticism of his remarks, Mr. Gandhi shares artwork depicting Goddess Parvati perched on Lord Shiva’s lap; says “love need not be hidden, affection is not a weakness, and equality begins with treating your partner as an equal.”

articles.headline: Russian attacks kill three in Ukraine as European Union criticises Moscow
articles.title: Russian attacks kill three in Ukraine, EU accuses Moscow of prolonging war
articles.summary: Russian military strikes killed three individuals across the Kherson, Dnipropetrovsk, and Zaporizhia regions of Ukraine on Monday. Concurrently, European Union High Representative Kaja Kallas accused Russian President Vladimir Putin of utilizing maximalist demands to prolong the conflict. In response to mounting infrastructure damage, the European Commission disbursed 1.88 billion dollars for defense systems alongside a separate 8.7 billion euro payment to support Ukraine.
articles.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says Russian President Vladimir Putin is making maximalist demands.

articles.headline: Nvidia chairperson says board does not intend to reinstate former chief executive Jensen Huang.
articles.title: Nvidia Board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO: Chairperson
articles.summary: Nvidia Chairperson Harvey Jones announced on November 17, 2026, that the board of directors will not reinstate former chief executive Jensen Huang following his resignation over an extramarital affair. Despite leadership turmoil, Nvidia reported robust third-quarter financial results with over 116 billion dollars in revenue. Meanwhile, Huang agreed to voluntarily testify before United States House committees on December 1 regarding national security scrutiny and export control compliance.
articles.description: Jensen Huang acknowledged making "serious mistakes" in his personal life; In its third-quarter earnings statement released on November 17, Nvidia did not mention his ouster or possible return

articles.headline: COP31 talks face sluggish climate finance responses amid Western security pressures
articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.summary: Urgent demands for climate finance from vulnerable developing nations met a slow response at the COP31 summit in Antalya as Western governments prioritized national security and domestic living costs. Host country Turkiye and Australia focused on implementing existing pledges rather than setting new targets. While multilateral development banks reported record lending in 2025, analysts noted significant funding gaps driven by geopolitical tensions, constrained fiscal spaces, and high capital costs.
articles.description: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

articles.headline: Ecuadorian fishermen sue Trump administration over lethal drone strike
articles.title: Ecuadorian fishermen sue Trump administration over drone strike
articles.summary: Ecuadorian fishermen filed a lawsuit in a Pennsylvania federal court against the administration of United States President Donald Trump regarding a March drone strike that sank their vessel, La Negra Francisca Duarte II, and injured two crew members. The complaint seeks financial restitution and an end to strikes targeting alleged drug boats. The government has not claimed responsibility for the incident, which plaintiffs called part of an unlawful military campaign.
articles.description: Crew say their boat was attacked by drones launched from US-operated vessel as part of 'manifestly unlawful' campaign.

articles.headline: Nvidia faces uncertainty following resignation of CEO Jensen Huang
articles.title: The Nvidia scandal isn’t slowing down
articles.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia following a scandal involving multiple affairs and allegations of chip smuggling to China. CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim leader while the company faces investigations and a 14 percent stock drop. Analysts suggest the long-term impact on the AI industry remains unclear despite the leadership transition.
articles.description: For years, Jensen Huang has had an almost unprecedented power to shape AI's advancement as Nvidia's CEO, cofounder, and president. As The Verge wrote last week, Nvidia's chips are "the bedrock upon which advanced AI technology in the US is being built." Ever-increasing demand has consistently outpaced supply, leading AI CEOs to essentially bow at […]

articles.headline: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister mandates local hiring by outside companies
articles.title: Won’t allow hiring of outsiders, hire locals: J&K CM Omar Abdullah to companies
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah stated on November 17, 2026, that external companies must hire local youths rather than outsiders. Speaking during a project inauguration in Jammu, Samba, and Kathua districts, Mr. Abdullah criticized the excuse of lacking trained personnel, noting that institutions like Industrial Training Institutes can prepare regional workers. He also addressed the region's Union Territory status.
articles.description: He made the statement during the inauguration of development projects worth ₹30 crores in Jammu, Samba and Kathua districts

articles.headline: Diplomatic efforts fail to halt escalating violence in eastern DRC
articles.title: DR Congo’s rival peace efforts fail to halt violence in the east
articles.summary: Conflict in the North and South Kivu provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo persists despite diplomatic initiatives such as the Washington Accords and the Doha Framework. The Front for recent advances through Kahuzi-Biega National Park prompted the Congolese army to prepare counteroffensives. Meanwhile, humanitarian organizations like Doctors Without Borders reduced staff presence in vulnerable zones as displaced communities face mounting security risks and disrupted services.
articles.description: Diplomatic efforts struggle to end fighting in eastern DRC as civilians continue to bear the cost of conflict.

articles.headline: Eisenkot ally elected Knesset speaker with Arab bloc’s backing
articles.title: Eisenkot ally elected Knesset speaker with Arab bloc’s backing
articles.description: Israel’s parliament has elected Matan Kahana as the new speaker with support from Arab parties.

articles.headline: Wholesale prices rise 12.29% year-on-year in October across India
articles.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.3% in October 2026, second straight month of double-digit inflation
articles.summary: Government data released on November 16, 2026, showed that wholesale inflation quickened to 12.29% year-on-year in October, surpassing the previous month's rate of 11.39% and economists' average forecast of 12.1%. The increase was driven by higher prices across sectors, with fuel and power recording a sharp surge of 32.84% compared to the previous year.
articles.description: According to economists, not only will this high wholesale inflation soon translate into higher consumer prices, but it also means an interest rate hike is nearly certain, which would dampen economic sentiment

articles.headline: Supreme Court orders stricter monitoring of pollution in Yamuna river
articles.title: Pollution in Yamuna increased despite huge expenditure on cleaning: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India has directed the Central Pollution Control Board to monitor water quality at state and district borders, citing rising pollution despite significant cleanup spending. The court emphasized that industrial and sewage waste must be treated at the source and warned that authorities will face penalties if water quality deteriorates under their jurisdiction.
articles.description: “This court is of the opinion that everything that is wrong with the civic administration in towns, cities and villages situated along the banks of the river is reflected in the poor health of the river and in the 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna,” said SC

articles.summary: China announced that President Xi Jinping will host U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026, during the APEC gathering. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas dismissed U.S.-encouraged Russian demands for a new European security framework as absurd, noting that Russia initiated the conflict. Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee announced upcoming sanctions targeting financial mechanisms supporting the war.
articles.description: At talks in Brussels, EU foreign ministers said the priority should be to secure a ceasefire and then a real peace agreement

articles.headline: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella discusses artificial general intelligence economic impacts

articles.summary: Microsoft Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella expressed deep concern regarding the economic and political restructuring artificial general intelligence might cause during a roundtable discussion in San Francisco. Nadella warned that allowing a single artificial intelligence model to achieve a monopoly status could lead to widespread economic collapse and threaten democratic institutions.

"I am AGI-pilled in the sense that at an economy level, what is the political economy's organization around AGI?" he asked at […]

articles.headline: French soldiers operate in Ukraine on secret mission since summer
articles.title: French troops deployed in Ukraine on secret mission: RFI
articles.summary: French soldiers have been operating in Ukraine for several months on a confidential mission codenamed Volia, Radio France Internationale reported on November 16, 2026. The light structure, led by a French general, trains Ukrainian troops and maintains military equipment using an official mission in Poland as cover. The deployment occurred without informing French lawmakers, amid a presidential election cycle where far-right figures propose cutting financial aid.
articles.description: The report did not say how many soldiers took part in the mission, which has been present in Ukraine since at least the summer of 2026

articles.headline: Israeli parliament elects Matan Kahana as new speaker in opposition boost
articles.title: Israel parliament elects Gadi Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as new speaker
articles.summary: Lawmakers in Israel elected Matan Kahana as parliament speaker on Tuesday after receiving sixty-six votes in the legislative chamber. Kahana, an ally of party leader Gadi Eisenkot, defeated Likud candidate Ofir Katz. The appointment allows the opposition to potentially challenge outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's domestic agenda and judicial reforms following recent inconclusive parliamentary elections.
articles.description: Eisenkot’s bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu’s most contentious domestic policies following Kahana’s election.
