articles.headline: Yemeni forces withdraw from Bab al-Mandab Strait leaving Houthis in control
articles.title: Yemeni forces retreat to defend port city from Houthis
articles.summary: Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia withdrew from areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait on November 15, 2026, leaving the waterway under the control of the Iran-backed Houthi movement. The military redeployed troops to defend the interim capital of Aden. The seizure of the strait disrupted global oil exports and escalated a conflict that has displaced nearly 330,000 people, according to United Nations estimates cited in the report.
articles.description: Saudi-backed forces say they are moving troops from the Bab al-Mandab Strait to protect the interim capital, Aden.

articles.headline: Haitians protest in support of El Salvador military deployment
articles.title: Haitians protest in support of El Salvador’s anti-gang troop deployment
articles.summary: Demonstrators marched across multiple Haitian cities on Tuesday to back the deployment of troops from El Salvador. The military intervention followed the kidnapping of four Salvadoran aviation technicians near Port-au-Prince. Although El Salvador confirmed plans to withdraw its forces once the missing airmen are located, Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier expressed strong gratitude for the security assistance.
articles.description: El Salvador's security minister has confirmed the troops will leave once kidnapped technicians are rescued.

articles.headline: US Army officer arrested for suspected espionage is transferred to military custody
articles.title: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody
articles.summary: Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Carroll Tyner, a forty-one-year-old US Army officer arrested in the United Kingdom on suspicion of spying for Russia, was transferred to United States military custody. British counter-terrorism police arrested the serviceman last week near Gloucester, where he was based at Imjin Barracks. Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor confirmed the investigation was handed over to American partners, while the Kremlin denied involvement.
articles.description: The Metropolitan Police say he has been taken into custody by the US Military over suspected national security and espionage allegations.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh reviews cyclone preparedness as 173 fishing boats remain at sea
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan to hit Andhra on November 20; Naidu reviews preparedness, 173 fishing boats yet to return
articles.summary: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu evaluated state readiness on November 16, 2026, as the Bay of Bengal depression prepares to hit the coast as Cyclone Akvan by November 20. Agriculture officials urged farmers to secure 23.87 lakh hectares of crops. Meanwhile, authorities confirmed that 30,635 out of 30,808 fishing vessels returned safely, while search operations continue for the remaining boats.
articles.description: Andhra’s Agriculture Minister asks officials to help farmers harvest ready crops and move produce to safety before Cyclone Akvan

articles.headline: Military plane crash in western Siberia kills nineteen people
articles.title: Russian military plane crash in Siberia kills 19
articles.summary: Nineteen people died when an Antonov An-12 transport aircraft crashed near Kemerovo in western Siberia, according to the Russian Defence Ministry. Investigators suspect equipment failure caused the accident in the unpopulated area. Regional Governor Ilya Seredyuk confirmed emergency crews extinguished a fire at the site near Yagunovo, while criminal authorities launched a formal safety inquiry.
articles.description: Russia's Defence Ministry says preliminary findings for the crash point to equipment failure.

articles.headline: International Court of Justice to deliver verdict in Myanmar Rohingya genocide case
articles.title: ICJ to rule on Rohingya ‘genocide’: Refugee crisis, timeline of the case, and more
articles.summary: The United Nations court in The Hague will issue a final ruling on November 19, 2026, regarding allegations that Myanmar committed genocide against the stateless Rohingya minority. Gambia initiated the lawsuit in November 2019 under the 1948 Genocide Convention. The landmark case follows decades of sectarian violence, military crackdowns, and mass refugee exoduses into neighboring Bangladesh.
articles.description: The international community is closely watching the top UN court’s Rohingya verdict as an archetype for the case filed by South Africa against Israel over its campaign in Gaza.

articles.headline: US deploys USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier to the Middle East
articles.title: USS Roosevelt arrives in Middle East: Is the US-Iran war about to resume?
articles.summary: The United States military stationed the nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East by November 15, 2026, bringing the total regional carrier strike groups to three. The deployment occurs while diplomatic negotiations involving Pakistan and Qatar remain stalled following a collapsed memorandum of understanding between Washington and Tehran earlier this year.
articles.description: The aircraft carrier joins two others operating in the US Central Command area of responsibility.

articles.headline: Russia stalls Ukraine talks with maximalist demands to fracture European security
articles.title: ‘NATO will collapse’: Russia stalls Ukraine talks, seeks to divide Europe
articles.summary: During United States-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, Russian diplomats presented demands that go far beyond a peace settlement, seeking to dismantle Europe's post-Cold War security architecture. According to leaked documents and analysts, Moscow wants the North Atlantic Treaty Organization to withdraw troops from Central and Eastern Europe and sign individual nonaggression pacts that could undermine collective defense.
articles.description: Russia has proposed nonaggression pacts with individual nations, which could shatter collective defence against Moscow.

articles.headline: World Health Organization warns antimicrobial resistance could cause 39 million deaths
articles.title: Antimicrobial resistance could kill 39 million people over 25 years: WHO
articles.summary: The United Nations health agency stated that growing antimicrobial resistance threatens to make routine surgery and childbirth life-threatening if prevention and antibiotic use do not accelerate. Officials noted that drug-resistant infections were directly responsible for more than one million deaths in 2021 and released new diagnostic tools to help countries strengthen laboratory capabilities.
articles.description: UN's health agency says growing resistance to antibiotics and other medicines threatens 'future of modern medicine'.

articles.headline: UK police hand over US soldier accused of espionage to military

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor stated the investigation into alleged violations of the National Security Act 2023 was passed to American partners. Federal Bureau of Investigation Director Kash Patel confirmed the service member remains held following a joint espionage probe.
articles.description: UK authorities have passed the investigation to the US 'in line with existing international protocols'.

articles.headline: UK, Australia, Canada and Italy urge Israel to allow humanitarian access to Gaza
articles.title: UK and allies call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza
articles.summary: Foreign ministers from the United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and Italy issued a joint statement calling on Israel to permit immediate humanitarian access to Gaza, where recent floods have worsened conditions and thousands of tents remain held at the border. The conflict began after a Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023, resulting in tens of thousands of deaths during subsequent military operations.
articles.description: The UK, Australia, Canada and Italy say Israeli authorities are holding back vital supplies at the borders, including 150,00 tents.

articles.headline: South Africa police probe two weekend shootings that left 17 dead
articles.title: South Africa police probe two weekend shootings that left 17 dead
articles.summary: South African authorities are investigating two separate mass shootings that resulted in seventeen fatalities over the weekend. Nine victims were discovered inside a shack within an informal settlement in Pretoria, while eight others were found dead inside a vehicle near Pietermaritzburg. Police have not yet established a motive or made any arrests in connection with either incident.
articles.description: The ​motive for the shooting has not ⁠yet been established, and no arrests have been ‌made

articles.headline: African National Congress records lowest vote share in local elections
articles.title: What’s behind the ANC’s decline in South Africa?
articles.summary: The African National Congress achieved its lowest-ever vote share during local elections this month in South Africa. The governing party, led historically by Nelson Mandela, swept to power thirty-two years ago following the end of apartheid. Analysts and party members discussed the severity of this political crisis and its implications for the nation on a program hosted by presenter James Bays.
articles.description: African National Congress won its lowest-ever vote share in local elections this month.

articles.headline: Prediction market Kalshi halts presidential speech wagers following regulatory order

The regulatory action follows insider trading concerns involving a White House teleprompter operator who traded on these markets. Consequently, the operator received a three-year ban and financial penalties, while regulatory scrutiny of prediction platforms has intensified.
articles.description: Kalshi halts Trump speech bets following CFTC mandate amid concerns of insider trading in US prediction markets.

articles.headline: China resists a nuclear treaty with the US and Russia
articles.title: Why is China resisting a nuclear treaty with the US and Russia?
articles.summary: Beijing remains hesitant to join any trilateral nuclear arms control treaty with the United States and Russia due to a significant disparity in warhead numbers. While Washington and Moscow possess thousands of weapons, China maintains a smaller, rapidly growing stockpile of approximately six hundred twenty warheads. Chinese officials emphasize their minimum deterrence posture and cite previous US withdrawals from key arms pacts.
articles.description: Beijing has a smaller arsenal than Washington and Moscow and worries that a pact could limit its nuclear capabilities.

articles.headline: Global leaders gather in Mumbai to promote climate innovation

articles.headline: Hakeem Jeffries shifts strategy for US House speaker nomination

Jeffries is expected to secure the nomination ahead of the 120th Congress being sworn in on January 3.

articles.summary: The Madras High Court ordered mandatory licensing and tagging of urban cattle across Tamil Nadu to prevent motor accidents caused by stray animals. articles.headline: Odisha orders early evacuation of vulnerable areas as cyclone approaches
articles.title: Odisha orders early evacuation of vulnerable areas as cyclone threat looms

articles.headline: Russia's Andreeva defeats Ukraine's Svitolina to win WTA Finals

The match concluded without the traditional handshake, adhering to established Ukrainian policy. Andreeva earned millions and a luxury car, while Svitolina announced plans to return to Ukraine to support ongoing relief efforts.

articles.headline: Five European Union nations to unveil Rwanda migrant deportation hub deal

articles.headline: Reliance Industries plans major investment in compressed biogas plants by 2030

Satheesan praised his government's six-month performance on November 17, 2026, highlighting increased tax revenue, welfare schemes, and maritime development projects. Vijayan accused the government of enabling corruption, environmental exploitation, and questionable power agreements.
articles.description: While Satheesan sought to paint a rosy picture of good governance, development, welfare, and fulfilled promises, Pinarayi Vijayan was scathingly critical of the UDF government

articles.headline: NATO allies plan to discuss United States troop levels with Pentagon
articles.title: NATO allies to discuss U.S. troop levels with Pentagon strategy chief
articles.summary: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius stated that NATO allies will consult with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby regarding Washington's review of American troop levels in Europe. The discussions take place in Brussels alongside talks on supplying additional Patriot air defence missiles to Ukraine to counter Russian strikes and enhance European security.
articles.description: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unveiled the six-month review in June and threatened to withhold some ‌U.S. dues to NATO if “free riding” allies fell short of defence spending commitments

articles.headline: Israeli forces invade Syrian village leaving homes damaged
articles.title: Israeli forces invade Syrian village leaving homes damaged
articles.description: Video shows bullet-riddled walls and charred belongings after Israeli raids on homes in Syria’s Daraa.

articles.headline: Global powers race to replace outgoing United Nations chief Antonio Guterres
articles.title: US and rivals spar over next UN boss as race lurches towards deadline
articles.summary: The race to replace outgoing United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres is entering its final weeks ahead of a December 31 deadline. Eight candidates are competing amid geopolitical rivalries and opaque processes. Costa Rican diplomat Rebeca Grynspan leads recent straw polls, though potential vetoes from permanent Security Council members pose hurdles to securing the position.
articles.description: Costa Rica's Rebeca Grynspan is the current frontrunner, polls suggest, but the US and Russia could veto her bid.

articles.headline: Estonia to close Russian border crossings following suspected sabotage attack
articles.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after attempted arson attack
articles.summary: Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia starting December 1, 2026, according to Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna. The decision follows the detention of eight suspects over an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems, which Tallinn blamed on Russian military intelligence. Moscow dismissed the accusations as another demonstration of Russophobia.
articles.description: Estonian authorities detained ‌eight people overnight on suspicion of an attempted arson attack on ‌drone maker Threod Systems that they ‌said ⁠had been ordered by Russia’s ⁠GRU military intelligence service

articles.headline: ASHA workers in Karnataka launch indefinite protest demanding higher honorarium
articles.title: ASHA workers launch indefinite protest; refuse to withdraw despite Health Minister’s assurance
articles.summary: Members of the Karnataka Rajya Samyuktha ASHA Karyakarteyara Sangha started an indefinite day-and-night agitation at Freedom Park in Bangalore on November 17, demanding a monthly honorarium of 15,000 rupees and pending dues. The workers rejected an appeal by Health Minister U.T. Khader to withdraw the protest, vowing to continue until their demands are fulfilled.
articles.description: Mr. Khader said he would take up the demand for an increase in the monthly honorarium to ₹15,000 with the Chief Minister at the Cabinet meeting scheduled for November 19.

articles.headline: Has empire shaped today’s world?
articles.title: Has empire shaped today’s world?
articles.description: How much of today’s world is a legacy of empire?

articles.headline: India integrates artificial intelligence into official statistics architecture
articles.title: Balancing AI-driven estimates and ground-level evidence in official statistics
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence and machine learning serve as core pillars in the newly approved Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics and Research, designed to overhaul official Indian data architecture. This development follows a global warning signed by 350 technology leaders, including Sam Altman and Bill Gates, urging priority focus on mitigating societal-scale risks stemming from artificial intelligence optimization.
articles.description: While AI and Machine Learning promise to make India’s official statistics faster and comprehensive, they cannot automatically replace ground-level evidence; synthetic data with inherited limitations may lead to misallocation of public resources and distortion of economic indicators

articles.headline: Bangladesh connects first nuclear power plant at Rooppur to grid
articles.title: Bangladesh connects first nuclear power plant to national grid
articles.summary: The Rooppur nuclear power plant in Bangladesh began trial electricity supply to the national grid on November 17. Science and Technology Minister Fakir Mahbub Anam announced that the facility makes Bangladesh the 33rd country to generate nuclear power, helping offset a severe fuel crisis by eventually meeting over 10 percent of national electricity demand.
articles.description: The development comes as the South Asian nation of 170 million people grapples with a fuel crisis triggered by the conflict in West Asia

articles.headline: Karnataka plans new road grid system and infrastructure projects in Bengaluru
articles.title: Karnataka Chief Minister: State govt. plans to establish new road grid system for Bengaluru
articles.summary: The Karnataka government is developing a new road grid system and clearing stormwater drain encroachments in Bengaluru to address urban planning shortcomings. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announced the initiative during a foundation stone laying ceremony for a ₹2,000 crore flood-mitigation project funded by the World Bank. The administration is also rerouting a planned Hosakote-Nandagudi road to 45 metres to preserve thousands of buildings and reduce government compensation burdens, alongside nearly ₹20,000 crore in ongoing infrastructure works.

articles.headline: Iraqi Prime Minister visits Lebanon to discuss alternative oil export routes
articles.title: Iraqi PM heads to Lebanon amid push to explore oil routes beyond Hormuz
articles.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited Beirut for high-level meetings with Lebanese leaders, including President Joseph Aoun, to discuss strengthening bilateral trade and security coordination. A primary focus of the talks involved diversifying Iraq's crude oil export routes by potentially reviving a defunct pipeline linking Kirkuk to Tripoli in northern Lebanon, thereby bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. The proposed infrastructure project could provide vital annual revenues to Lebanon amid its ongoing economic crisis.
articles.description: Ali al-Zaidi's talks expected to include proposed project linking Tripoli in Lebanon to Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline.

articles.headline: Regional Meteorological Centre forecasts moderate rainfall for Chennai amid Cyclone Akvan
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: RMC forecasts moderate rainfall for Chennai on Wednesday
articles.summary: The Regional Meteorological Centre in Chennai forecasted moderate rainfall at isolated places in Chennai, Tiruvallur, and Chengalpattu districts on Wednesday due to Cyclone Akvan. The cyclone was located about 610 kilometres east of Chennai at 8.30 a.m. on Tuesday and is expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm. According to forecasters, the system will likely cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni on Thursday with maximum sustained winds of 120 to 130 kmph.
articles.description: The RMC has forecast moderate rainfall at isolated places in Chennai, Tiruvallur and Chengalpattu districts on Wednesday

articles.headline: R Vaishali uses tournament matches to prepare for world championship
articles.title: Hard grind a preparation for the World title match: Vaishali
articles.summary: Grandmaster R Vaishali is utilizing the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest as preparation for her upcoming world title match against reigning champion Ju Wenjun of China. Vaishali secured her challenger position by winning the Women's Candidates in Cyprus in April. During Sunday's matches, she defeated Arjun Erigaisi with the white pieces in their second Fast Classic game after capitalizing on a late error by her opponent.

articles.headline: Russian missile strikes damage bridges and disrupt transport in Kyiv
articles.title: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
articles.summary: Russian ballistic missiles struck the Pivnichnyi and Pivdennyi bridges in Kyiv late Monday, causing significant damage and large craters that forced closures and widespread travel disruptions. Recovery operations are under way as residents navigate the aftermath of the bombardment. The attacks coincided with Ukrainian missile strikes that severely damaged the bridge connecting Russia to occupied Crimea, marking a tense night of infrastructure attacks between the warring nations.
articles.description: Moscow has targeted bridges in Kyiv, while Ukraine severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.

articles.headline: NMDC plans to expand iron ore pellet production capacity
articles.title: NMDC eyes 24 million tonnes pellet capacity
articles.summary: NMDC, formerly the National Mineral Development Corporation, aims to reach 24 million tonnes of annual pellet production capacity. Chairman Amitava Mukherjee announced the expansion on November 15, noting that the company is integrating iron ore-to-pellet infrastructure. The firm is also diversifying into coal production in Jharkhand and enhancing logistics to support its long-term growth strategy.

articles.headline: Sai Parenterals acquires majority stake in Bion Therapeutics India
articles.title: Sai Parenterals acquiring majority stake in Bion
articles.summary: Sai Parenterals is acquiring a majority stake in the Hyderabad-based firm Bion Therapeutics India through its subsidiary, SP Analytics. The all-cash deal, expected to close this month, adds 16 brands and 250 staff to the company. Sai Parenterals plans to shift Bion's production to its own accredited facilities to improve quality and supply chain control.
articles.description: The acquisition will add 16 established brands and around 250 field staff, strengthening its presence in India’s prescription market, Sai Parenterals said.

articles.headline: CAIR condemns potential terrorist designation and defends civil rights work
articles.title: CAIR defends civil rights work against Trump’s ‘smear’
articles.summary: The Council on American-Islamic Relations condemned statements by United States President Donald Trump regarding a possible blanket terrorist designation against the Muslim civil liberties organisation. In a statement issued on Tuesday, CAIR asserted that the administration should focus on addressing a surge in violent hate crimes against American Muslims rather than targeting free speech and civil rights advocacy. Trump had previously told reporters outside the White House that his administration was monitoring the organisation and that a designation could happen.
articles.description: The US's largest Muslim advocacy group urges President Trump to address rising hate crimes against Muslims.

articles.headline: Congress accuses Union government of economic mismanagement amid rising household and industry inflation
articles.title: Rising prices reflect government’s economic mismanagement: Congress
articles.summary: The Congress party alleged on November 17, 2026, that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's economic policies caused severe inflation and distress for households and businesses. Citing a recent survey, party official Jairam Ramesh stated that monthly expenditures rose over twenty percent for many families, while high input costs and tariffs forced numerous garment factories to close.
articles.description: Monthly costs up by over 20% for 61% of families, according to a survey cited by Congress leader Jairam Ramesh; claims PM is more pre-occupied with politics than tackling the inflation crisis

articles.headline: England defeat Spain 3-2 to secure top spot in group A3
articles.title: England stun Spain 3-2 to end record unbeaten streak
articles.summary: England defeated world champions Spain 3-2 in Madrid on November 16, 2026, ending La Roja's record forty-four match unbeaten run in competitive games. Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White secured the victory, while Spain responded through Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams. England finished as group winners in Nations League group A3 despite playing with ten men following Elliot Anderson's second-half red card, according to the report.
articles.description: Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja's first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat

articles.headline: Congo Ebola outbreak remains out of control six months into response
articles.title: Ebola outbreak remains out of control in Congo six months into response
articles.summary: Six months after an Ebola outbreak was declared in Congo, government data shows over eleven thousand cases and nearly half of those infected have died. According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, eighty percent of new cases are detected outside health surveillance. Children and frontline workers face severe risks amid conflict and attacks in eastern provinces.
articles.description: The Ebola outbreak is the deadliest of Congo’s 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016

articles.headline: World Health Organisation warns of surging respiratory illnesses in Gaza
articles.title: Respiratory illnesses rise in Gaza with worst to come as winter floods arrive, WHO says
articles.summary: The World Health Organisation reported that acute respiratory infections in Gaza have risen by 33,000 cases compared to last year. Dr Reinhilde Van De Weerdt stated that heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians, worsening overcrowding and living conditions. The agency warned that the situation will deteriorate further during winter, while Israeli military agencies maintained that winterisation supplies and medical equipment have been facilitated into the region.
articles.description: Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher

articles.headline: India health expenditure triples as household out-of-pocket spending declines
articles.title: India’s health spending triples to ₹4.14 lakh crore, but out-of-pocket share drops to 42.7%: NHA
articles.summary: India's Union government health expenditure increased from ₹1.30 lakh crore in 2013-2014 to ₹4.14 lakh crore in 2023-2024, according to National Health Accounts estimates. The Health Ministry reported that the proportion of out-of-pocket spending by households fell from 64.2% to 42.7% over the decade. The data highlights expanded public financing, increased primary healthcare spending, and growth in government and private health insurance schemes across the country.
articles.description: The share of healthcare costs borne by households fell from 64.2% to 42.7% over a decade, while social security spending on health rose from 6% to 11%

articles.headline: Thousands protest upcoming Oxford University talk by Nathan Cofnas
articles.title: Thousands demand cancellation of Nathan Cofnas talk at Oxford University
articles.summary: Thousands of individuals signed a petition demanding the cancellation of an event featuring American academic Nathan Cofnas at Oxford University's Oriel College. Organized by the Oxford Reform student society, the Tuesday evening lecture focuses on diversity in higher education. Cofnas previously faced dismissal and suspension following plagiarism allegations and controversial statements linking race to intelligence, prompting widespread student protests and university statements regarding event hosting.
articles.description: Online petition with more than 32,000 signatures demands the university 'cancel Nathan Cofnas's invitation to speak'.

articles.headline: Wipro 3D partners with Markforged for industrial printing in India
articles.title: Wipro 3D ties up with Markforged to expand industrial 3D printing in India
articles.summary: Additive manufacturing firm Wipro 3D formed a strategic partnership with industrial printing provider Markforged to expand composite three-dimensional printing access across India. Combining engineering expertise with continuous fiber reinforcement technology, the collaboration aims to help manufacturers in aerospace, defence, and automotive sectors produce lightweight components and reduce production lead times.
articles.description: The collaboration will also focus on developing in-house composite additive manufacturing capabilities among Indian manufacturers.

articles.headline: Mirra Andreeva defeats Elina Svitolina to claim WTA Finals title
articles.title: Mirra Andreeva beats Elina Svitolina to win WTA Finals; ascends to No. 2 in rankings
articles.summary: Nineteen-year-old Russian tennis player Mirra Andreeva defeated Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 on November 15, 2026, to win the WTA Finals without dropping a set at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. Andreeva earned 3.37 million dollars and a Mercedes-Benz convertible, rising to number two in the world rankings. Svitolina collected 1.5 million dollars after finishing as the runner-up in the eight-day tournament, according to the match report.
articles.description: The WTA Finals win helped Mirra Andreeva to clinch her career-high ranking, just behing Elena Rybakina

articles.headline: Student-led movement takes seats in Serbia's new parliament
articles.title: Election-winning student movement enters Serbia’s new parliament
articles.summary: The Serbian parliament convened in Belgrade on Tuesday following an October 25 election that saw the grassroots Student List movement secure 140 of 250 seats. This shift ends the dominance of President Aleksandar Vucic and the Serbian Progressive Party. Lawmakers now face a 90-day constitutional deadline to form a new government or trigger snap elections.
articles.description: Hundreds hail Student List lawmakers as the new parliament meets for the first time.

articles.headline: Manu Bhaker joins International Shooting Sport Federation Athletes Committee
articles.title: Manu Bhaker elected to ISSF Athletes Committee for 2026-30 term
articles.summary: Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker has secured a position on the International Shooting Sport Federation Athletes Committee for the term spanning from 2026 to 2030. She aims to prioritize sustainable environments for shooters and better prize money. Former Olympic champion Abhinav Bindra previously served on this committee between 2010 and 2020.
articles.description: During her nomination earlier this month, Bhaker had outlined an athlete-centric vision, focusing on strengthening the sport and creating a more supportive, sustainable and progressive environment for shooters worldwide

articles.headline: BBC reports from Kyiv bridge hit by Russian attack
articles.title: BBC reports from Kyiv bridge hit by Russian attack
articles.description: The BBC's Sarah Rainsford spoke to residents near the site of the overnight strike.

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Deadly settler pogroms persist
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Deadly settler pogroms persist
articles.description: A Palestinian woman was killed in a settler shooting near Jericho, while Arab MPs in Israel seek Netanyahu probe.

articles.headline: Moily claims Congress leaders stalled Modi investigation
articles.title: Some Congress leaders stalled probe into Modi in Gujarat riots case, claims Veerappa Moily
articles.summary: Former Union Minister M. Veerappa Moily alleged that unidentified leaders within the United Progressive Alliance government obstructed an investigation into Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the 2002 Gujarat riots. Speaking at a book launch in Bengaluru on November 17, 2026, Moily claimed the inquiry was halted despite Supreme Court directives. He also stated that internal resistance prevented organizational reforms proposed by party chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

articles.headline: Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if U.S. trade talks fail
articles.title: Carney says Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if Trump trade talks fail
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated in Cambodia on November 16, 2026, that Canada could pursue alternative partnerships with Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with United States President Donald Trump fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry. Carney emphasized that Washington talks remain his priority following a January agreement that permitted limited Chinese electric vehicles into Canada under reduced tariffs.
articles.description: Mr. Carney said any Chinese investment would have to involve substantial manufacturing in Canada rather than simply assembling imported parts

articles.headline: Opposition questions Supreme Court decision to grant bail to Bilkis Bano convicts
articles.title: Opposition questions Supreme Court order in Bilkis Bano case
articles.summary: Opposition leaders criticized a Supreme Court bench comprising Justices M.M. Sundresh and P.B. Varale for granting bail to two convicts in the Bilkis Bano case on November 17, 2026. The Congress and CPI(M) condemned the order, stating the survivor endured fresh trauma without prior notice, while the court cited their seventeen years in prison.
articles.description: Congress says Bilkis is being put through ‘fresh humiliation and trauma’, while CPI(M) calls SC order ‘shocking and reprehensible’

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu launches HPV-DNA testing programme in five districts for cervical cancer
articles.title: HPV-DNA testing to be implemented in five high-burden districts of T.N.
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu will implement HPV-DNA testing for cervical cancer across Dharmapuri, Villupuram, Tiruvannamalai, Perambalur, and Ariyalur districts, covering 124,215 women in the first phase. Supported by central approval and funds of 869.50 lakh rupees under the National Health Mission, the initiative aims to strengthen primary screening and address high morbidity rates among women.
articles.description: Dharmapuri, Villupuram, Tiruvannamalai, Perambalur and Ariyalur will be covered in the first phase

articles.headline: Skilled worker shortage increases cyclone repair costs across coastal Andhra Pradesh districts
articles.title: Skilled-worker shortage pushes up cyclone repair costs in coastal Andhra
articles.summary: Residents in Eluru, West Godavari, and Krishna districts faced severe financial losses and high repair costs following Cyclones Arnab and Murasu. A shortage of skilled workers like masons and electricians drove daily wages up significantly, leaving many households struggling with damaged roofs and submerged water motors without full normalcy restored.
articles.description: Residents face repair bills ranging from ₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh as a shortage of technicians pushes up wages and delays restoration of damaged houses in Eluru, West Godavari and Krishna districts

articles.headline: Bangladesh adviser states India cannot dictate terms regarding Sheikh Hasina return
articles.title: India cannot dictate terms on Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: PM’s adviser
articles.summary: Bangladesh information adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated on November 17, 2026, that India cannot dictate conditions for the return of deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. While media reports suggested New Delhi sought judicial safeguards and direct army reception, Dhaka insisted any extradition and subsequent legal procedures will follow domestic laws strictly.
articles.description: Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government

articles.headline: Uttar Pradesh publishes draft electoral roll with 13.58 crore voters ahead of 2027 elections
articles.title: 13.58 crore voters in U.P. draft electoral roll; 18 lakh added since SIR
articles.summary: The Uttar Pradesh election office published a draft electoral roll containing 13.58 crore voters on November 17, 2026, marking an increase of 18 lakh since April. Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa reported the figures during a Lucknow press conference, noting the list excludes religion-based data. The revision precedes the 2027 Assembly election, with claims and objections accepted until December 16.
articles.description: Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa says Election Commission does not keep religion-wise data on voters; Akhilesh questions CM Yogi’s recent claim that 1.27 crore Hindu voters were removed

articles.headline: Southern Transitional Council gains prominence as Houthi forces advance toward Aden
articles.title: Houthi advance on Aden may spur resurgence of Yemen’s southern separatists
articles.summary: An advancing Houthi military threat toward Aden has elevated the importance of the Southern Transitional Council, a southern Yemeni secessionist movement supported by the United Arab Emirates. Following recent government force withdrawals, STC leaders are mobilizing defenses. Analysts warn the group remains politically divided and reliant on Saudi backing to effectively repel the ongoing offensive.
articles.description: Southern separatists try to regain power to defend Aden as Saudi Arabia reshuffles its military command against Houthis.

articles.headline: Mozambique opposition leader Venancio Mondlane faces trial over election unrest
articles.title: Mozambique opposition leader goes on trial for terrorism over deadly election protests
articles.summary: Prominent Mozambican opposition leader Venancio Mondlane appeared in the Supreme Court in Maputo to face trial on charges including incitement to terrorism and civil disobedience. The proceedings follow deadly post-election protests stemming from disputed presidential results in 2024 that declared Daniel Chapo the winner. Rights groups reported over three hundred deaths during the subsequent unrest, while police recorded ninety-six fatalities.
articles.description: Venâncio Mondlane faces several charges over 2024 post-election protests that left hundreds of people dead.

articles.headline: US government seeks 24-year prison term for Nikhil Gupta
articles.title: U.S. govt seeks 24-year prison term for Nikhil Gupta in Pannun murder-for-hire plot
articles.summary: United States authorities are pushing for a 24-year prison sentence for Indian national Nikhil Gupta over his involvement in a foiled plot to assassinate American citizen Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York. Gupta previously pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire charges and is scheduled to be sentenced on November 20 by United States District Judge Victor Marrero.
articles.description: Gupta will be sentenced on November 20. His lawyers have, however, argued for a "substantial downward" sentence of 12 years' imprisonment followed by three years of supervised release

articles.headline: Karnataka to move Supreme Court over rural development grants
articles.title: Karnataka to move Supreme Court over ₹2,186 crore rural development grants: Eshwar Khandre
articles.summary: The Karnataka government announced it will approach the Supreme Court within a week to seek the release of two thousand one hundred eighty-six crore rupees in grants under the fifteenth Finance Commission. Rural Development Minister Eshwar B. Khandre stated that technical portal discrepancies caused the Union government to withhold funds, while Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar prepares to launch new rural infrastructure schemes.

articles.headline: Democratic senators urge Federal Aviation Administration to pause router replacements following national ground stop
articles.title: US senators demand FAA pause upgrades linked to nationwide ground stop
articles.summary: Thirteen Democratic senators urged the Federal Aviation Administration to halt upcoming router replacements following an investigation into a nationwide ground stop on Friday that canceled over 10,000 flights. The FAA attributed the disruption to network upgrades involving L3Harris and Juniper Networks equipment. Meanwhile, the FBI and Department of Transportation are investigating the technical failure.
articles.description: Thousands of routers used in communications systems are slated to be replaced, raising the risk of more problems.

articles.headline: BJP criticises Telangana government over Bharat Summit expenditure
articles.title: BJP slams govt. over Bharat Summit spending, unmet promises
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party Legislature Party leader A. Maheshwar Reddy accused the Telangana government of misusing nearly one hundred crore rupees of public funds on the Bharat Summit instead of aiding drought-affected farmers. He also demanded an apology for controversial remarks made by an Italian politician at the event, while party spokesperson N.V. Subhash criticised the administration over unfulfilled election promises.

articles.headline: P.K. Mishra highlights coordination and citizen experience in governance
articles.title: Modi’s governance journey marked by coordination across govt departments, focus on citizen experience: P.K. Mishra
articles.summary: Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister P.K. Mishra emphasised the importance of seamless department coordination and citizen experience during an event organised by Niti Aayog in New Delhi. Marking twenty-five years of Narendra Modi as head of government, officials discussed milestones including disaster responses and the Lakhpati Didi initiative, aiming towards a developed nation by twenty forty-seven.
articles.description: The principal secretary to the Prime Minister said India’s governance journey has been marked by defining milestones that demonstrate the power of decisive leadership and the ability to translate vision into action

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh ranks fourth nationally in rooftop solar installations
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh ranks fourth in installation of rooftop solar systems nationally
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh secured fourth place in India for implementing the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, with 7,39,260 households equipped with rooftop solar systems as of November 15, 2026. Special Chief Secretary for Energy K. Vijayanand directed officials to upload installation data by December 15, 2026, warning that missing data would disqualify beneficiaries from receiving government subsidies.
articles.description: The State accounts for nearly 13% of the 56.97 lakh households covered across the country, behind Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra

articles.headline: Karnataka chief minister D.K. Shivakumar outlines tech expansion goals
articles.title: Karnataka charting next tech leap to push AI, deep-tech: CM D.K. Shivakumar
articles.summary: Karnataka aims to become a global hub for artificial intelligence and semiconductor manufacturing, according to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on November 17, 2026. Speaking in Bengaluru, he noted the State attracted $9.4 billion in foreign direct investment equity during the first half of fiscal year 2025-26. The government plans new initiatives, including a government-driven artificial intelligence university and semiconductor facility investments exceeding ₹23,000 crore.
articles.description: Inaugurating the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit, Shivakumar unveils major infrastructure, funding, and reskilling initiatives to lead global innovation beyond artificial intelligence

articles.headline: Om Birla urges women legislators to leverage AI for governance
articles.title: Women legislators must leverage AI for transparent, accountable governance: Om Birla
articles.summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla inaugurated the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians India Region Conference in Bengaluru, urging women representatives to utilise artificial intelligence for transparent governance. Leaders including Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara discussed the implementation of the Women Reservation Bill, digital safety, and mentorship pathways during the two-day event.

articles.headline: Prince William and Catherine honour young environmental winners in Mumbai
articles.title: Prince William, Catherine Honour Young Changemakers at First-Ever Children’s Earthshot Awards in Mumbai
articles.summary: Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, attended the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards in Mumbai on November 17, 2026. The event celebrated youth-led environmental projects across five categories, including climate and waste reduction. The initiative, which engaged nearly one million students, aims to foster local innovation to address urgent global environmental challenges and sustainability.
articles.description: Founded by Prince William and incubated in The Royal Foundation in 2020, the Earthshot Prize is the world’s most prestigious environmental award, designed to identify, back and celebrate groundbreaking leadership in environmental action

articles.headline: Nvidia must hire outside chief executive after Huang departure, Bessent says
articles.title: U.S. Treasury chief Scott Bessent wants answers soon from Nvidia
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that Nvidia must hire an outside chief executive following the resignation of Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down on November 12, 2026, amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. Bessent added that the board and outside counsel must answer questions regarding export compliance within 10 days.
articles.description: U.S. Treasury ‌Secretary Bessent said he wants to know if Nvidia used shell companies to dodge U.S. restrictions and sell its most powerful chips to China

articles.headline: Documentary explores environmental impact of conflict in Afghanistan
articles.title: Ghost Towns of Afghanistan: The Environmental Toll of Decades of War
articles.summary: The documentary film Ghost Towns of Afghanistan, directed by Matty Feurtado and Ibrahim Sulemen Khel, examines the long-term environmental degradation caused by decades of war. The film follows Ibrahim, a Kabul resident, as he returns to his home in Nangarhar province to witness the ruins and health crises facing families living in contaminated conflict zones.
articles.description: A father confronts the aftermath of environmental damage from years of war in Afghanistan.

articles.headline: Houthis advance in Yemen as government forces move to defend Aden
articles.title: Houthis advance in Yemen as government forces move to defend Aden
articles.description: An advance by the Houthi armed group in Yemen is threatening one of the government’s last strongholds.

articles.headline: Mahendra Singh Dhoni retires from IPL playing career with Chennai Super Kings
articles.title: Dhoni ends IPL playing career as CSK appoints him team mentor
articles.summary: Mahendra Singh Dhoni announced his retirement from active Indian Premier League play on November 17, 2026, concluding a career that began in 2008. The Chennai Super Kings owner N. Srinivasan appointed Dhoni as the team mentor for the five-time champions ahead of the 2027 season, following a period marked by injuries and the team failing to reach the playoffs.
articles.description: The announcement comes ahead of the IPL 2027 retention deadline

articles.headline: Megaspeed launches internal investigation into business and supply chain
articles.title: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
articles.summary: Singapore-based Megaspeed announced an internal investigation into its business operations after executive Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy linked to Nvidia's former chief executive Jensen Huang, left her role in August 2025. The company stated it complies with all regulatory regimes, while US treasury and commerce officials face mounting congressional scrutiny over high-end AI chip exports.
articles.description: The Nvidia scandal has raised questions over whether advanced AI chips ended up in China, despite US restrictions.

articles.headline: Rep. Thomas Massie Forces a New Fight for Epstein Survivors
articles.title: Rep. Thomas Massie Forces a New Fight for Epstein Survivors
articles.description: Kentucky Republican Rep. Thomas Massie is pushing for justice for victims of the Epstein files.

articles.headline: India prepares for opening Test match against New Zealand
articles.title: IND vs NZ Tests: India faces test of character as WTC hopes hang in balance
articles.summary: India faces New Zealand in the opening Test match of a two-match series at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on November 17, 2026. The series carries significant implications for India's qualification hopes for the World Test Championship final and its quest for a first series victory in New Zealand in 17 years. Captain Shubman Gill indicated the team may select four pace-bowling options for the match.
articles.description: After winning the T20I and ODI series, India turn their attention to the Tests. With conditions favouring pace, Gill and the team management must balance bowling firepower with batting depth

articles.headline: Lakshya Raichandani dedicates under-19 Asia Cup victory to coach
articles.title: Lakshya dedicates u-19 Asia Cup win to his late coach
articles.summary: Opening batter Lakshya Raichandani has dedicated his under-19 Asia Cup triumph to his late coach, Abhishek Kumar, following a victory over Pakistan in the final. The 18-year-old cricketer from Uttar Pradesh scored 80 runs in the summit clash and reflected on his long-standing journey training in Uttarakhand since the age of ten.

articles.headline: Indian stock markets extend rally driven by foreign fund inflows
articles.title: Stock markets rally second day on foreign fund inflows, moderate crude oil prices
articles.summary: Benchmark stock indices extended their rally for the second consecutive day, with the BSE Sensex climbing 427.40 points to settle at 82,532.19 and the NSE Nifty reaching 25,387.40. This upward movement was supported by steady foreign fund inflows, moderate crude oil prices, and strong buying in Reliance Industries and major banking stocks despite weak global trends.
articles.description: The 30-share BSE Sensex rallied 427.40 points, or 0.52%, to settle at 82,532.19; during the day, it surged 792.7 points, or 0.96%, to 82,897.49.

articles.headline: French students continue protests over poor school conditions
articles.title: At the origin of France’s education protests, students refuse to give up
articles.summary: Students across France are maintaining blockades at schools to protest deteriorating infrastructure and lack of resources. The movement, which began in September, saw hundreds of thousands of participants in October. While the government promised to address concerns, students report no significant improvements. Teachers have joined the protests, citing systemic neglect and insufficient educational funding.
articles.description: Blockades continue at some schools in the Parisian suburbs as students and teachers say little has improved.

articles.headline: Why do governments switch off the internet?
articles.title: Why do governments switch off the internet?
articles.description: The internet went dark somewhere every day in 2025. AJLabs explains why authorities switch it off.

articles.headline: Telangana debt servicing reached 26.8% of total receipts in 2024-25
articles.title: Telangana’s debt servicing accounted to 26.8% of 2024-25 total receipts, says CESS study
articles.summary: According to a study by the Centre for Economic and Social Studies, debt servicing in Telangana accounted for 26.8% of total receipts during 2024-25, totaling ₹62,953 crore against receipts of ₹2.36 lakh crore. The report highlighted that outstanding total liabilities reached ₹5,61,787 crore, exceeding the state's GSDP ceiling limit. Meanwhile, the Congress government noted a subsequent decline in average borrowing costs.
articles.description: No information on maturity dates and interest pertaining to OBBs, says the report

articles.headline: Prime Minister Andy Burnham delays unveiling options for UK-EU ties
articles.title: Burnham delays tabling of options for U.K.-EU ties
articles.summary: United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham delayed presenting long-term options for ties between the United Kingdom and the European Union until the next Parliament. Speaking at the City Hall banquet, Burnham stated he would seek to finalize a closer relationship agreement at a summit on Friday while ruling out rejoining the European Union, accepting freedom of movement, or joining the single market.
articles.description: At Friday’s Summit Mr. Burnham said he seek to finalise an agreement with Brussels for closer U.K.-EU ties, based on the groundwork laid by his predecessor Keir Starmer

articles.headline: Delhi police arrest owner and contractor after Paharganj building collapse injures eight workers
articles.title: Delhi’s construction boom, workers’ growing risks: Safety takes a back seat as violations go unchecked
articles.summary: Delhi police arrested property owner Raman and contractor Anwar on November 16, 2026, following a building collapse in Kaseruwalan, Paharganj, that injured eight workers. According to the Municipal Corporation of Delhi, workers were removing shuttering from a newly constructed ground-floor lintel under a valid building plan when the structure gave way, though officials maintained active construction was not underway during air pollution restrictions.
articles.description: Missing helmets and protective gear, unsafe structures, punishing work hours and rushed construction expose a deepening safety crisis at Delhi’s building sites, where basic safeguards are routinely ignored and accountability often comes only after tragedy strikes

articles.headline: US aviation authorities investigate nationwide ground stop caused by equipment failure
articles.title: After a nationwide ground stop, US faces aviation infrastructure questions
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration grounded United States flights for nearly four hours following a router malfunction during an upgrade performed by defence contractor L3Harris. Over 9,000 flights were cancelled and 1.5 million passengers stranded. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that investigations are ongoing into the incident, which has also renewed scrutiny regarding ageing infrastructure across the national aviation system.
articles.description: Trump has requested $50bn for upgrades, but Democratic lawmakers are asking for transparency before spending more.

articles.headline: India offers extended service terms to military recruits under Agnipath scheme
articles.title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?
articles.summary: India's Ministry of Defence announced on 4 November that soldiers finishing four-year terms under the Agnipath programme can serve two additional years at higher pay. Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani stated the decision followed internal reviews. More than 18,300 recruits will complete their initial tenure by the end of 2026, amid ongoing debates regarding training duration and military effectiveness.
articles.description: India has softened its recruitment scheme, giving young soldiers a longer military stint and another shot at permanent service.

articles.headline: US Senate Democrats face internal contest for majority leadership
articles.title: How is US Senate majority leader chosen?
articles.summary: Following midterm elections, United States Senate Democrats face an internal leadership contest between incumbent Chuck Schumer and challenger Chris Van Hollen. Schumer has led the caucus since 2017 but faces criticism from progressive members regarding his strategy against Donald Trump's agenda, while Van Hollen launched his bid to present a fresh direction for the party.
articles.description: Chris Van Hollen set to challenge Chuck Schumer for the post as the Democrats prepare to take control of Congress.

articles.headline: Cyclone Akvan approaches Andhra Pradesh coast as IMD issues warning
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan to make landfall between Nellore and Tuni in Andhra as very severe storm on November 20
articles.summary: According to the India Meteorological Department, Cyclone Akvan is projected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni as a very severe cyclonic storm by November 20 noon. Winds could reach 145 kmph. Officials have placed district administrations on high alert, suspended offshore operations, and instructed fishermen to remain ashore until November 20 due to dangerous conditions.
articles.description: Andhra fishermen, still awaiting compensation for Cyclone Arnab’s losses, are told to stay ashore till November 20

articles.headline: IN-SPACe selects three companies for urban settlement mapping
articles.title: Three space companies selected to develop high-resolution 3D reconstruction techniques for Indian cities
articles.summary: The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre has chosen three private entities under its Seed Fund Scheme to develop high-resolution human settlement layers for Indian cities. The chosen firms will receive seed funding of ₹1.46 crore to build satellite-based 3D reconstruction techniques, with initial pilot demonstrations scheduled to cover Bengaluru and Shimla.
articles.description: The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, and the deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh puts coastal districts on high alert for Cyclone Akvan
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: Andhra Home Minister Anitha puts coastal districts on high alert, warns fishermen
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha ordered all coastal districts into high alert as Cyclone Akvan approaches the Bay of Bengal. During a review meeting with disaster management officials, authorities warned that the storm is projected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm before crossing the coast on Friday, bringing heavy rainfall and strong winds.
articles.description: Andhra Pradesh Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha asks people to stay alert over the next four days and the Agriculture Department to help farmers protect crops ready for harvest

articles.headline: Adivasi youth dies after altercation with lodge staff in Bhadrachalam
articles.title: Adivasi youth dies following assault by private lodge staff in Bhadrachalam
articles.summary: A 23-year-old Adivasi man named Tellam Sharath died following a physical assault by lodge staff during an altercation over room charges in Bhadrachalam. Local Adivasi organizations have demanded stringent action against those responsible and requested a thorough investigation into the lodge management regarding alleged violations of land regulations.

articles.headline: Revanth Reddy asks Chhattisgarh for Sammakka Sagar barrage clearance
articles.title: Revanth seeks Chhattisgarh nod for Telangana’s Sammakka Sagar barrage; Vishnu Deo assures early completion of NOC process
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy met his Chhattisgarh counterpart Vishnu Deo Sai in Raipur on November 17, 2026, requesting a No Objection Certificate for the Sammakka Sagar barrage in Mulugu district. Mr. Revanth Reddy assured that Telangana will cover all land acquisition and rehabilitation expenses. Mr. Vishnu Deo responded positively, promising an early completion of the approval process to meet regional irrigation and drinking water demands.
articles.description: The Sammakka Sagar project is intended to utilise Godavari waters to meet irrigation and drinking water needs in drought-prone, backward and tribal areas of Telangana.

articles.headline: Mozambique opposition leader Venancio Mondlane stands trial over protests
articles.title: Mozambique’s opposition leader stands trial over deadly 2024 protests
articles.summary: Venancio Mondlane, opposition leader in Mozambique, appeared at the Supreme Court in Maputo on Tuesday to face five charges, including instigating terrorism related to deadly 2024 post-election protests. If convicted, he faces up to twenty-four years in prison. Mr. Mondlane denies all allegations, while rights groups report that hundreds died during a government crackdown following disputed national election results.
articles.description: Venancio Mondlane faces five charges, the most serious being instigating 'terrorism'.

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces withdraw from Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend Aden
articles.title: Yemeni government forces retreat from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces announced a strategic withdrawal from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait area to prioritize the defense of Aden. The retreat on November 15, 2026, marks the end of a six-week counteroffensive against the Iran-aligned Houthis, who previously seized the Red Sea coast. Meanwhile, the International Committee of the Red Cross reported that the Houthis released 600 prisoners on the same day amid ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February

articles.headline: Thousands of US flights face cancellations following technical failure
articles.title: Thousands of US flights still cancelled or delayed two days after grounding of planes nationwide
articles.summary: Thousands of US flights were cancelled or delayed after a technical failure in a communication router caused a national ground stop. Transport Secretary Sean Duffy stated normal operations may take time to recover as aircraft remain out of position. President Donald Trump urged Congress to approve funding to modernise the system.
articles.description: The US transport secretary says that normal air-traffic operations may not be restored until Monday.

articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot calls for Benjamin Netanyahu's removal amid alleged election meddling
articles.title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu can’t remain Israel PM amid alleged vote meddling
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot demanded the immediate departure of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following allegations of electoral interference reported by broadcaster Channel 12 on Sunday. The report claimed Netanyahu's chief of staff, Ido Norden, improperly prompted police raids against Ra'am party members before the October 27 election. Netanyahu's Likud party condemned the remarks as outrageous incitement.
articles.description: Arab party members were reportedly arrested before Israeli elections based on unfounded evidence from the PM's office.

articles.headline: Pakistan and Iran stress sustained coordination for regional stability in Rawalpindi
articles.title: Pakistan, Iran stress sustained engagement, coordination for regional stability
articles.summary: Pakistan Chief of Defence Forces Asim Munir met with an Iranian delegation led by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Rawalpindi on November 16, 2026, to discuss regional stability and security challenges. Mr. Araghchi also attended the Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers meeting and held talks with Pakistan Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar regarding diplomatic engagement.
articles.description: Field Marshal Munir made the remarks during a meeting with a high-level Iranian delegation led by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Rawalpindi

articles.headline: Gartner forecasts India IT spending to reach 16.9 trillion rupees
articles.title: AI, cloud investments to drive India’s IT spending to ₹16.9 trillion in 2027: Gartner
articles.summary: Information technology spending in India is projected to grow by 10.6 percent to reach 16.9 trillion rupees in 2027, according to a Gartner forecast released on Tuesday. D.D. Mishra stated that rising investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure, cloud services, and cybersecurity are driving the growth. Infrastructure as a service spending is expected to surge by 40.3 percent next year.
articles.description: India is entering a new phase of technology investment where AI infrastructure and digital sovereignty are becoming strategic priorities, says the analyst firm

articles.headline: Rebeca Grynspan emerges as frontrunner for UN leadership position
articles.title: Rebeca Grynspan could be the UN’s first woman boss, if she can sway Trump
articles.summary: Costa Rican diplomat Rebeca Grynspan is leading straw polls among United Nations Security Council members to succeed Antonio Guterres as secretary-general. Aged seventy, the current head of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development could become the first woman and first Jewish person to hold the post. However, she faces potential vetoes and must secure support from United States President Donald Trump.
articles.description: Swaying the US could test Grynspan but she likes taking risks - and wants UN to take more, she tells Al Jazeera.

articles.headline: Ukrainian breaks world record for deepest competitive freedive
articles.title: Ukrainian breaks world record for deepest competitive freedive
articles.description: Ukrainian freediver Nataliia Zharkova has broken the world record, reaching 124 metres in constant weight.

articles.headline: Pakistan defence minister suggests country could establish new provinces
articles.title: Is Pakistan about to carve out new provinces? Inside the controversial plan
articles.summary: Defence Minister Khwaja Asif stated that Pakistan could introduce a new administrative system featuring multiple new provinces as early as the New Year. The proposal, initially raised by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi at a July summit, aims to improve governance across the country's population of approximately 250 million. Implementing the plan requires a constitutional amendment and two-thirds parliamentary majority.
articles.description: Talk of new provinces has gathered pace, but there is no formal proposal or agreement among governing parties.

articles.headline: Bangladeshi police use tear gas against garment workers protesting low wages
articles.title: Bangladesh police clash with garment workers amid protests over wages
articles.summary: Police in Bangladesh fired tear gas and stun grenades on Tuesday after garment employees blocked highways and torched vehicles during demonstrations over pay. Workers are demanding a monthly minimum of thirty thousand taka to offset rising living costs. The unrest disrupted the thirty eight billion dollar industry, prompting the deployment of Border Guard Bangladesh forces as wage negotiations continue.
articles.description: Protesters hurl bricks, torch vehicles and block the main highway between Dhaka and Mymensingh.

articles.headline: Prince William and Princess Catherine arrive in Mumbai for Earthshot Prize
articles.title: Prince and Princess of Wales in Mumbai for Earthshot Prize 2026: All you need to know
articles.summary: Britain's Prince William and Princess Catherine arrived in Mumbai on November 17, 2026, for a three-day visit hosting the sixth edition of The Earthshot Prize. Marking the royal couple's first joint overseas trip since 2024, the event brings together five thousand guests to celebrate environmental innovators competing across five distinct categories.
articles.description: The sixth Earthshot Prize, founded by Britain’s Prince William to promote innovative climate change solutions, will be presented in Mumbai on November 17, 2026

articles.headline: Amaravati develops indigenous quantum technology stack to build local computers
articles.title: Amaravati builds indigenous quantum tech stack
articles.summary: An expanding network of companies, universities, and startups in Amaravati is developing domestic quantum technologies to foster local manufacturing. According to state officials, regional entities have created the NAADA resonator chip, the Q-SHIVA cryogenic platform, Q-CoRE control electronics, and Q-CODE software. These innovations aim to reduce import reliance and establish the region as a global quantum development hub.
articles.description: Amaravati-based companies, universities and startups develop the NAADA chip, Q-SHIVA cryogenic platform, Q-CoRE electronics and Q-CODE software, laying the foundation for building quantum computers locally

articles.headline: Investigation identifies Benjamin Tait as the operator behind anonymous X account
articles.title: Who is behind Habibi UK, an X account that targeted critics of Israel?
articles.summary: A six-month investigation by the Byline Times identified Benjamin Tait, a 61-year-old former United States Foreign Service officer, as the operator of the anonymous X account Habibi UK. The account targeted critics of Israel with online attacks and was amplified by various political figures. Tait previously directed a political campaign firm and operated an energy research company before its liquidation.
articles.description: A former US Foreign Service officer ran a company that funded election adverts attacking Jeremy Corbyn’s Labour.

articles.headline: Thiruvananthapuram court finds eleven CPI(M) workers guilty in RSS activist murder
articles.title: Keralam RSS activist Ranjith murder case: 11 CPI(M) workers found guilty
articles.summary: The Thiruvananthapuram Additional District and Sessions Court found eleven Communist Party of India Marxist workers guilty in the 2008 murder of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh activist Ranjith in Mannanthala. Prosecutors established that political hostility following the killing of another activist motivated the attack. The court cancelled the convicts' bails and scheduled their sentencing for the following day.
articles.description: Thiruvananthapuram court to pronounce sentences on November 18

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi questions EC’s ‘unanimous’ SIR decision ahead of Supreme Court hearing
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi questions EC’s ‘unanimous’ SIR decision ahead of Supreme Court hearing
articles.description: A day before the Supreme Court resumes hearing challenges to the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, Rahul Gandhi has questioned the poll body’s claim that the programme was approved unanimously by all three Election Commissioners.

articles.headline: Kulgam anti-terror operations continue as security forces retrieve body of accomplice
articles.title: Kulgam anti-terror ops continue; body of LeT terrorist Latteef Bhat’s ‘accomplice’ retrieved from encounter site
articles.summary: Security forces in Kulgam continued anti-terror operations for the seventh consecutive day while retrieving the body of an alleged accomplice of Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Lateef Bhat from an encounter site. Local political parties criticized the prolonged security restrictions and civilian hardships resulting from the operations following a recent checkpoint attack that injured three personnel.
articles.description: Security agencies released CCTV footage, which suggested Dar and Bhat were seen together on November 10 and 11 surveying multiple locations

articles.headline: Civil society questions Telangana police detention of SIO members over Israel event
articles.title: Civil society questions detention of SIO members over their stance on Telangana-Israel collaboration event
articles.summary: Civil society members in Hyderabad accused the Telangana police of curtailing democratic rights following the preventative detention of Students Islamic Organisation members on November 16, 2026. Activists including Padmaja Shaw and Khalida Parveen criticized the action as a human rights violation targeting Muslim youth who questioned a government collaboration with Israeli entities at T-Hub.
articles.description: Civil society members said that the detentions were contrary to India’s consistent foreign policy of supporting Palestine

articles.headline: Union Minister Santanu Thakur comments on political violence in West Bengal
articles.title: Feuds, factions and allegations of extortion: BJP’s problem of plenty in West Bengal | Explained
articles.summary: Union Minister of State Santanu Thakur remarked that party supporters are both perpetrators and victims of political violence in West Bengal. Speaking on November 15, 2026, the minister highlighted the shifting political dynamics six months after the Bharatiya Janata Party government came to power in the state, following earlier remarks by state party president Samik Bhattacharya during the assembly election campaign.
articles.description: The BJP leadership in West Bengal is not only facing the challenge of dealing with factionalism but also allegations of extortion by a section of its leaders

articles.headline: Alappuzha authorities to cull 26000 birds following bird flu confirmation
articles.title: Bird flu confirmed at two farms in Keralam’s Alappuzha; 26,000 birds to be culled
articles.summary: Authorities in Keralam will begin culling approximately 26,000 domestic birds on November 18, 2026, after bird flu was confirmed at two poultry farms in Alappuzha district. The National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal verified the infection in samples. District Collector Shaji V Nair convened an emergency meeting to coordinate six rapid response teams within the surveillance zone.
articles.description: Six rapid response teams of Animal Husbandry and Health departments set to carry out culling

articles.headline: Supreme Court to hear Rahul Gandhi application regarding election commission affidavit
articles.title: SIR row: Supreme Court agrees to hear INDIA bloc’s ‘interrogatories’ on ‘nationwide SIR’, CEC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to hear an application filed by Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders posing forty-eight interrogatories to Election Commission of India officials. A Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant scheduled the hearing for December 9, 2026, following challenges to an October 26 affidavit concerning the nationwide service information report exercise that excluded approximately thirteen crore voters.
articles.description: The affidavit asserted that the massive exercise (SIR), in which approximately 13 crore voters were excluded, was a unanimous decision of the ECI

articles.headline: Indian Oil Corporation secures government approval for commercial sustainable aviation fuel supply
articles.title: IOC gets government nod for commercial sustainable aviation fuel supply from Panipat refinery
articles.summary: State-owned Indian Oil Corporation obtained government approvals to commercially supply sustainable aviation fuel from its Panipat refinery, Chairman A.S. Sahney announced on November 17, 2026. The facility aims to meet India's 1 per cent blending target for international flights in 2027 by producing about 35,000 tonnes annually from used cooking oil sourced from large hospitality chains.
articles.description: The State-run refiner plans to enter into supply agreements with airlines before committing investments to additional SAF projects

articles.headline: Four nations urge Israel to allow immediate humanitarian aid into Gaza
articles.title: Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urge Israel to allow aid into Gaza
articles.summary: Australia, Canada, Italy and the United Kingdom urged Israel to permit immediate and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza following severe floods. The foreign ministers noted that 150,000 tents and vital supplies remain restricted at the border. More than 1.9 million people have been displaced in the territory during the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: The countries accuse Israel of preventing tents and other supplies from entering Gaza, despite the humanitarian crisis.

articles.headline: Denmark expands industrial biogas production using livestock manure to drive energy transition
articles.title: Powering towns on pig manure: How Denmark has transformed energy generation
articles.summary: Denmark has developed approximately 150 industrial-sized biogas plants utilizing livestock manure to supply about 40 percent of its national gas grid. While the sector aids energy independence and decarbonization initiatives such as Sonderborg's ProjectZero, critics argue the reliance on manure perpetuates factory farming, prompting ongoing debates over agricultural emissions and upcoming carbon taxes.
articles.description: Pigs are big business in Denmark. Now their waste is being turned into biogas, which powers the national grid.

articles.headline: Bessent calls for outsider leadership at Nvidia following executive scandal
articles.title: US Treasury chief calls for outsider to lead embattled tech firm Nvidia
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent advocated for external leadership at Nvidia during a television appearance on November 15, 2026. The technology firm faces scrutiny after former chief executive Jensen Huang resigned following reports of an affair with a woman linked to Chinese intelligence. Bessent also called for a 10-day deadline to verify export compliance.
articles.description: Scott Bessent gives Nvidia's board 10 days to show the company's compliance with US export controls.

articles.headline: Israeli opposition targets Knesset speaker role to advance legislative agenda
articles.title: As Knesset readies for new speaker, Israeli opposition holds powerful role
articles.summary: Following the November election, the Israeli political opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot seeks to elect Matan Kahana as Knesset speaker on Tuesday with the support of Arab-led parties. Securing this powerful legislative post would allow the anti-Netanyahu bloc to introduce key measures, including an inquiry into the October 7, 2023, attacks, restoring attorney general powers, and proposing a premiership term limit while coalition talks continue.
articles.description: The anti-Netanyahu bloc holds the keys to electing a new parliamentary speaker, setting the momentum for change.

articles.headline: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visits the oldest Philippine gurudwara
articles.title: PM Modi leads foundation stone-laying ceremony for Philippines’ oldest gurudwara’s redevelopment
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the century-old Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara in Manila and led the foundation stone-laying ceremony for its redevelopment project. Mr. Modi is currently on a three-day visit to the Philippines to attend regional summits including the ASEAN-India meeting, aiming to strengthen diplomatic ties and cultural connections across Southeast Asia.
