articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government plans to introduce the Investment Protection Act to prevent policy reversals that have previously harmed investor confidence. The legislation aims to shield businesses from arbitrary changes following past controversies, such as renewable energy contract reviews. Legal experts and industry leaders suggest the act will provide stability and attract new capital to the state.
articles.description: The proposed law aims to shield investments from policy reversals by successive governments, such as the ‘three capitals’ plan and the review of power purchase agreements

articles.headline: Central Bureau of Investigation assumes control of Nisha Kumari Bhagat death probe
articles.title: CBI takes over probe into Nisha Bhagat death case
articles.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation has taken over the investigation into the death of tribal activist Nisha Kumari Bhagat, who died in Ranchi on November 6. Following a state government referral, the agency re-registered a case against Ajay Tirky, Jyotsana Kerketta, and others. Bhagat had previously alleged harassment by state officials and land brokers on social media.
articles.description: The mortal remains of the tribal activist, who allegedly died by suicide, were consigned to flames at her ancestral village in Gumla district on November 7, amid protests in different parts of the State demanding a CBI probe into the case

articles.headline: Ahmad Tibi elected deputy speaker of the Israeli Knesset
articles.title: Who is Ahmad Tibi, the Arab MP elected deputy speaker of Israel’s Knesset?
articles.summary: Ahmad Tibi, chairman of the Arab Movement for Renewal party, has secured the position of deputy speaker in the Israeli Knesset. The appointment marks a significant milestone for the lawmaker representing Palestinian citizens of Israel. Tibi described the outcome as a victory against far-right factions that attempted to block his candidacy despite opposition from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party.
articles.description: A Palestinian citizen of Israel, Tibi was an aide to Yasser Arafat and has been a legislator for 27 years.

articles.headline: Autodesk says artificial intelligence will transform Indian job markets rather than eliminate positions
articles.title: AI to reshape, not replace, jobs in India’s design and manufacturing sectors: Autodesk
articles.summary: California-based technology company Autodesk reported that artificial intelligence will transform employment across India's design and manufacturing sectors rather than replace jobs. Citing a 147 percent increase in AI-related roles over two years, executives emphasized the need for collaboration between industry and educational institutions to bridge workforce skill gaps through training programs and software investments.
articles.description: San Francisco-based firm that creates 3D design, engineering, and entertainment technology has committed $350 million investment in India.

articles.headline: Germany manager Jurgen Klopp calls for FIFA president to step down
articles.title: Klopp says Infantino worse than Blatter
articles.summary: Germany manager Jurgen Klopp has stated that FIFA president Gianni Infantino should be replaced, comparing his tenure unfavourably to that of Sepp Blatter. Infantino faces ongoing pressure following scrapped proposals and opposition from UEFA, which has prepared criminal legal proceedings and pursued documents in United States courts. The deadline for candidates confirming their presidential challenge is Wednesday.
articles.description: Germany manager Jurgen Klopp says he "didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that" as he calls for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to be replaced.

articles.headline: Israeli settlers seize Palestinian homes in Jericho amid growing displacement
articles.title: As homes seized, Jericho’s Palestinian residents fear settler takeover
articles.summary: Israeli settlers seized eight Palestinian homes in the West Bank city of Jericho on November 4, following an operation supported by the Nachala movement and local settlement councils. Residents reported assaults by settlers and subsequent destruction of properties. The Palestinian Authority has launched an investigation into the takeovers, while local farmers express deep concern over the expansion of illegal settlement outposts.
articles.description: Palestinians are assaulted and their homes are levelled in pogrom in occupied West Bank.

articles.headline: United Nations delegates debate potential regulations for lethal autonomous weapons
articles.title: UN-backed talks consider possible rules on lethal autonomous weapons
articles.summary: Government envoys met in Geneva at a United Nations review conference on November 16, 2026, to consider launching negotiations for rules on killer robots. While seven nations proposed a legally binding agreement, Russian officials stated that discussions remain premature. The debate is critical as military powers and international leaders clash over artificial intelligence in warfare and the necessity of human accountability.
articles.description: Scary would-be scenarios, like armed drones flying amok and gunning down civilians with pinpoint precision, have peppered years of discussions about killer robots, but those talks haven't produced any international restrictions

articles.headline: China and Southeast Asian leaders commit to avoiding South China Sea disputes
articles.title: China, Southeast Asia pledge to avoid disputes during talks on South China Sea pact
articles.summary: China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations pledged on November 16, 2026, to avoid actions escalating South China Sea disputes during annual talks in Manila. Chinese Premier Li Qiang and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. discussed progress on a code of conduct. The talks matter because territorial standoffs in the vital trade route remain a major regional flashpoint.
articles.description: China, Taiwan and four ASEAN states — Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam — have been involved in the decades-long territorial standoffs in the busy waterway, a key global trade route

articles.headline: Seventeen people killed in two separate mass shootings across South Africa
articles.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 17 dead
articles.summary: South African police launched a manhunt after eight men were shot dead inside a minibus in KwaZulu-Nation province and nine people were killed in a shack in western Pretoria during Sunday night incidents. Police stated the shootings are unrelated as the nation continues to struggle with high rates of violent crime and illegal firearms.
articles.description: The shootings in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng highlight South Africa's struggle to curb violent crime.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh government proposes Investment Protection Act to shield business investments
articles.title: Andhra’s proposed Investment Protection Act seeks to shield investors from policy U-turns
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government is planning to enact the Investment Protection Act to prevent policy reversals and safeguard capital from political changes, following past controversies involving renewable energy power purchase agreements and capital shifts. Legal experts and industry leaders noted that the unprecedented legislation aims to restore investor confidence and protect economic planning across the State.
articles.description: The proposed law aims to shield investments from policy reversals by successive governments, such as the ‘three capitals’ plan and the review of power purchase agreements

articles.headline: Every Chhath, the same question returns: Why is the Yamuna still polluted?
articles.title: Every Chhath, the same question returns: Why is the Yamuna still polluted?
articles.description: Every year during Chhath Puja, images of devotees standing amid toxic foam bring the Yamuna’s pollution crisis back into focus. Despite decades of court interventions, government plans and cleanup projects, the river remains heavily polluted as it passes through Delhi. Experts say the key challenge is not just increasing river flow, but stopping untreated sewage and waste from entering the river in the first place.

articles.headline: India Meteorological Department forecasts heavy rainfall across Telangana due to Cyclone Akvan
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan may bring rains to Telangana between November 19 and 21
articles.summary: Cyclone Akvan is expected to bring heavy rain to parts of Telangana between November 19 and November 21, 2026, according to the India Meteorological Department. Authorities issued orange alerts for four districts on November 20 and November 21. The weather system matters because severe cyclonic conditions threaten widespread thunderstorms, lightning, and gusty winds across multiple regional districts.
articles.description: The impact may be observed from Thursday (November 19, 2026). Four district were placed under orange alert, indicating heavy to very heavy rainfall, on Friday (November 20, 2026)

articles.headline: India Meteorological Department issues heavy rain warning for south Bengal districts
articles.title: IMD warns of heavy rain in four south Bengal districts from November 19
articles.summary: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm, bringing heavy rain to south Bengal districts between November 19 and November 21, 2026. The India Meteorological Department advised fishermen to avoid the sea. This severe weather threatens South 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, Paschim Medinipur, and Jhargram with thunderstorms and gusty winds.
articles.description: The weather system, which lies over the southeast Bay of Bengal as a deep depression, is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by November 16 evening and subsequently into a severe cyclonic storm as it moves in a north-northwestward direction, says IMD

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu pastoralists demand representation in state wildlife conservation
articles.title: Why Tamil Nadu’s pastoralists are demanding a voice in wildlife conservation?
articles.summary: Traditional pastoral communities in Tamil Nadu are demanding representation in the State Board for Wildlife following its reconstitution by the government on October 28, 2026. The Tamil Nadu Federation of Pastoral Peoples Sangams argues that excluding indigenous herders who possess vital traditional ecological knowledge threatens livelihoods and contravenes existing legal frameworks protecting historical grazing rights.
articles.description: Tamil Nadu government issued a Government Order on October 28, 2026, to reconstitute its State Board for Wildlife—headed by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. Missing from the move was representation for traditional pastoral communities.

articles.headline: Congress and INDIA bloc plan strong alternative in Uttar Pradesh
articles.title: Congress, INDIA bloc will provide strong alternative in Uttar Pradesh, says Kharge
articles.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge stated on November 16, 2026, that his party and the INDIA bloc will provide a strong alternative for Uttar Pradesh in the upcoming assembly polls. Following a strategic meeting in Delhi, leaders emphasized social justice and defeating the Bharatiya Janata Party, amid discussions regarding seat-sharing arrangements with Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav.
articles.description: The upcoming elections in Uttar Pradesh will give a new direction to the country's politics, Mallikarjun Kharge said.

articles.headline: Fishing trawler capsizes in Andaman Sea with many feared dead
articles.title: The tragedy of recurring Rohingya refugee deaths
articles.summary: A fishing trawler carrying between 250 and 280 Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi nationals capsized in the Andaman Sea in mid-April 2026 while attempting to reach Malaysia from Cox’s Bazar. According to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and the International Organization for Migration, approximately 250 people are feared dead or missing, with only nine to ten survivors rescued.
articles.description: The capsizing of a fishing trawler carrying refugees draws attention to the cost of protracted displacement

articles.headline: Rohingya crisis overview and regional displacement issues
articles.title: For Rohingya, there is no place called home
articles.summary: Rohingya Muslims originating from Rakhine state in Myanmar face systemic statelessness under the 1982 Burmese citizenship law and have experienced recurring sectarian violence and military crackdowns. Over recent years, tens of thousands have fled across borders into Bangladesh and India, prompting major humanitarian concerns, security challenges, and ongoing legal and political debates regarding deportation and refugee status.
articles.description: Rejected by the country they were born in and shunned by the neighbouring states, the Rohingya are among the the most vulnerable amongst forcibly displaced groups.

articles.headline: Supreme Court issues warning over Aadhaar face authentication accessibility issues
articles.title: Supreme Court warns contempt if authorities fail to give detailed reply to plea on visually impaired unable to do Aadhaar face authentication
articles.summary: The Supreme Court warned of contempt action if authorities fail to provide a detailed response to an application by advocate Amar Jain concerning visually impaired individuals unable to complete Aadhaar face authentication. The plea highlights e-KYC failures and challenges a mandatory biometric LPG refill order issued by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas in October 2026.
articles.description: The Supreme Court issued notice on application pointing out that the inability to complete Aadhaar face authentication was affecting e-KYC, which only relies on face authentication

articles.headline: Belur residents protest following two fatal elephant attacks within three days
articles.title: Elephant attack: Protesters want Forest Minister visit Belur after two deaths in three days
articles.summary: Protesters in Belur blocked a road on November 16, 2026, demanding a permanent solution to human-elephant conflicts after two fatal attacks occurred within three days in Karnataka. Local resident Jayamma was killed on November 14, followed by Hafees Ur Rahman on November 16. Former minister B. Shivaramu criticized the district administration, while Hassan district authorities planned a visit to address safety concerns.
articles.description: The Minister in charge of Hassan district, K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, was expected to visit the spot later in the day along with senior officers

articles.headline: Bahrain court sentences sixty-four Shia individuals to life in prison
articles.title: Bahrain sentences 64 Shias, mostly clerics, to life on terror charges: rights group
articles.summary: A Bahraini criminal court sentenced 64 Shia Muslims, including 57 clerics, to life imprisonment on November 16, 2026, amid an ongoing crackdown on suspected Iran-linked networks. The Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy reported the sentences, while rights groups raised serious concerns regarding alleged torture, forced confessions, and the widespread persecution of religious clerics.
articles.description: Bahrain, a Sunni Muslim kingdom, has a large Shia population that has long complained of marginalisation

articles.headline: Jordanian authorities ban Telegram messaging application over national security concerns
articles.title: Jordan and Iraq block Telegram over national security concerns
articles.summary: Jordanian authorities banned the Telegram messaging application on November 16, 2026, citing efforts to curb illegal content and extremist material following a church shooting in Karak. The Public Security Directorate announced the security measure as part of a broader crackdown. Telegram was founded in 2013 by Pavel Durov, who currently faces international investigations and legal scrutiny.
articles.description: Jordan says wants to stop 'attempts to ‌spread extremism' as Iraq says ⁠app failed to 'address non-compliant ⁠content'.

articles.headline: Sadiq Khan: Global North must take responsibility for climate change
articles.title: Sadiq Khan: Global North must take responsibility for climate change
articles.description: At COP31, Sadiq Khan urges wealthy nations to support the Global South, which bears the brunt of climate change.

articles.headline: HRCP warns of escalating threats to democracy and constitutional rights in Pakistan
articles.title: Pakistan human rights body warns of escalating threats to democracy and fundamental freedoms
articles.summary: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan raised concerns on November 16, 2026, regarding an escalating assault on constitutional democracy, judicial independence, and freedom of expression. Following its annual general meeting, the commission highlighted the sentencing of lawyers Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Chattha, criticized recent constitutional amendments, and demanded the protection of minorities and fundamental freedoms nationwide.
articles.description: According to a press release issued by HRCP, the commission's General Body expressed alarm over the systematic erosion of freedom of expression through censorship, surveillance, restrictive regulations and the misuse of criminal laws

articles.headline: Prince Harry visits Ukraine to support injured war veterans and Invictus athletes
articles.title: 'You're going to win the war': Harry praises war veterans on surprise Ukraine visit
articles.summary: The Duke of Sussex undertook a two-day surprise visit to Lviv, Ukraine, to meet injured service personnel and Ukrainian competitors participating in the Invictus Games. Prince Harry visited rehabilitation facilities including the Superhumans Center, where he observed advanced medical treatments and praised the resilience of wounded veterans facing ongoing missile attacks from Russian forces.
articles.description: He has been showing support for injured veterans in Ukraine and praising the country's resilience.

articles.headline: Supreme Court upholds Maharashtra reservation rotation policy for local bodies
articles.title: Supreme Court rejects plea against Maharashtra's rotation policy for reserved SC/ST seats in local bodies
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed an appeal challenging Maharashtra government rules that treat general elections following their enforcement as the first for rotating reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in local bodies. Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana ruled that voters do not possess a vested right to specific seat reservations, concluding that the policy falls entirely within government domain.
articles.description: A Bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana dismissed an appeal filed by Sau. Rupali Indrabhushan Sonde against the September 19, 2025, judgment of the Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court, saying, "No voter or a candidate can have a vested right to have a constituency declared as a reserved seat for SCs or STs”

articles.headline: Sudanese army drone strike kills fifteen civilians in West Kordofan
articles.title: Sudan Army strike kills 15, including children says rights group, survivor
articles.summary: A double-tap drone strike conducted by the Sudanese Army in the village of Abu Qalb killed fifteen people, including four children playing football, according to a survivor and a local rights monitor. The attack occurred during a military counter-offensive against the Rapid Support Forces, escalating a conflict that has triggered severe humanitarian crises across the region.
articles.description: The double-tap strike on November 15 in the village of Abu Qalb also “injured others and burned a number of homes”, reported local rights monitor the Kordofan Observatory

articles.headline: Kachin: where Myanmar’s rare earth minerals are in tight grip
articles.title: Kachin: where Myanmar’s rare earth minerals are in tight grip
articles.description: In Myanmar’s northern state of Kachin lies millions of dollars worth of rare earth minerals.

articles.headline: Ahmad Tibi elected deputy speaker of Israel parliament following electoral gains
articles.title: Ahmad Tibi elected deputy speaker of Israel’s Knesset
articles.summary: Joint List alliance chairman Ahmad Tibi was elected deputy speaker of the Israeli Knesset on November 16, 2026, following historic electoral gains by parties representing Palestinian citizens. Tibi called for a criminal investigation into Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding alleged interference in the parliamentary elections, emphasizing that no individual is above the law.
articles.description: Leader of alliance representing Palestinian citizens of Israel says election is 'rightful achievement' for Joint List.

articles.headline: Odisha miners leave 40% of iron ore capacity underutilised amid rising demand
articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.summary: Miners in Odisha left nearly forty percent of approved iron ore capacity unutilised, prompting judicial concern regarding resource waste and potential state revenue losses. While courts highlighted delays and financial impacts, industry sources attributed the low operational rates to lengthy forest clearance procedures affecting production across major mineral-producing states.
articles.description: The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, which is among the highest-grade varieties of iron ore

articles.headline: Over 2,000 people cross over from Senegal into Spain’s Canary Islands
articles.title: Over 2,000 people cross over from Senegal into Spain’s Canary Islands
articles.description: Around 2,000 migrants have crossed into Spain’s Canary Islands from Senegal in two days.

articles.headline: European militaries seek domestic alternatives to reduce defense technology dependence
articles.title: Europe hunts for Palantir alternatives as Militaries seek to limit U.S. dependence
articles.summary: European defense ministries are actively pursuing domestic software solutions to reduce reliance on American technology provider Palantir Technologies for critical military functions. Countries including France, Germany, and the Netherlands are exploring alternative suppliers to ensure national data sovereignty, balancing strategic autonomy against the operational capabilities provided by established U.S. platforms.
articles.description: Last week, Germany’s Helsing unveiled ​military intelligence software called Clarity, which is a part of a broader market for AI-powered systems designed to accelerate military decision-making

articles.headline: Ecuadoran president denies United States military presence following reported aircraft deployment
articles.title: Ecuador’s president denies existence of US military base
articles.summary: Ecuadoran President Daniel Noboa denied the existence of a United States military base near Guayaquil, stating that American personnel at Taura Air Base were participating solely in temporary cooperative activities. The denial followed journalistic investigations documenting unusual aircraft deployments and military flights, which raised domestic legal questions regarding bilateral anti-narcotics efforts.
articles.description: Daniel Noboa says US personnel in the country for 'temporary activities'.

articles.headline: Pakistan nominates climate minister to represent government at New Delhi forum
articles.title: Pakistan’s participation in SCO Civilisational Forum | Explained
articles.summary: Pakistan designated Climate Change and Coordination Minister Musadik Masud Malik to represent its government at the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue in New Delhi. The event aims to connect ancient civilizations among member countries, bringing attention to Pakistani representation despite ongoing regional diplomatic tensions involving bilateral water treaties and security disputes.
articles.description: The Ministry of Culture, in collaboration with the Ministry of External Affairs, will organise the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum from November 20-22 at the Purana Qila (Old Fort) in New Delhi

articles.headline: Italy fines Meta record €805 million over unauthorised gallery access
articles.title: Why Italy hit Meta with record €805 million fine | Explained
articles.summary: Italy’s data protection authority penalized Meta €805 million on November 14, 2026, for collecting user photos and videos from Android galleries without explicit consent. The platform feature allowed browsing suggestions using device media. This represents the largest monetary penalty ever levied by Italian authorities against a major technology corporation, highlighting growing regulatory scrutiny over digital privacy practices.
articles.description: Italy’s data protection authority conducted a technical analysis after it received a complaint from a consumer protection forum, which said that the platform accessed “unpublished files stored on users’ smartphones”

articles.headline: Phuket commercial shophouse fire kills 11 people and injures 16
articles.title: 11 killed, 17 injured in fire at Phuket shophouse
articles.summary: An early morning blaze on November 16, 2026, destroyed a commercial shophouse in a resort town on Thailand's Phuket island, resulting in eleven fatalities and sixteen injuries. Local law enforcement reported that the fire erupted in a vehicle rental establishment before spreading to adjacent structures near Patong beach. Thai authorities extinguished the flames within two hours, while investigators continue determining the precise origin of the disaster.
articles.description: Police said officers are still investigating the cause of the fire, but initial investigations found an electrical transformer near the building had exploded shortly before the fire started

articles.headline: Kerala Police link arrest to synagogue arson case investigation
articles.title: Kerala Police find similarities between Gurumurthy, Kochi synagogue arson cases; yet to find evidence of Lawrence Bishnoi links
articles.summary: State Police Chief Ravada A. Chandrasekhar stated on November 16, 2026, that investigators identified modus operandi similarities between suspect Gurumurthy and Ebin P. Paul, who is in custody for an October 12 arson attack on the Kadavumbhagam synagogue in Ernakulam. Although both suspects allegedly maintained criminal network ties, authorities have confirmed no direct connection to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.
articles.description: Thrissur police are investigating case against Tamil Nadu native Gurumurthy who was arrested recently from Palakkad for alleged links with criminal networks, while NIA has taken over probe into arson case

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs status reports on special NDPS courts
articles.title: Supreme Court asks Centre, States to file status reports on setting up of special courts to hear NDPS Act cases
articles.summary: The Supreme Court instructed the Centre, states, and union territories on November 16, 2026, to submit fresh progress reports regarding the creation of 449 designated courts to handle Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act cases. A Bench consisting of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana reviewed the backlog and emphasized establishing adequate infrastructure for expeditious trials.
articles.description: Supreme Court took note of the submissions of Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that not much progress has been made in pursuance of the orders passed by the apex court recently on setting up of special courts

articles.headline: Commercial building fire in Phuket kills at least eleven people
articles.title: At least 11 killed in blaze on Thailand’s Phuket island
articles.summary: A fierce blaze in Patong on November 16, 2026, resulted in eleven deaths and sixteen injuries following an apparent electrical transformer explosion. Phuket Governor Chodnarin Koedsom reported that stored motorbikes, gas, and tyres inside a rental shop accelerated the flames. Fifteen Thai nationals and one Myanmar citizen received hospital treatment, while authorities confirmed no tourists were harmed.
articles.description: Authorities are investigating the cause of the fire, which also injured 16, but have ruled out arson.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh survey reveals millions of hypertension and diabetes cases
articles.title: Andhra NCD survey finds 59.63 lakh hypertension, 48.95 lakh diabetes cases
articles.summary: Officials submitted the Non-Communicable Diseases 4.0 survey findings to Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav on November 15, 2026, covering 4.2 crore tested individuals. The assessment identified 59.63 lakh hypertension cases and 48.95 lakh diabetes cases across the state. Additionally, screenings confirmed thousands of oral, breast, and cervical cancer diagnoses, with older demographics recording the highest prevalence of lifestyle diseases.
articles.description: Andhra Pradesh has 59.63 lakh hypertension and 48.95 lakh diabetes cases; 34 lakh people have both hypertension and diabetes

articles.headline: Depression over Bay of Bengal expected to become severe cyclonic storm
articles.title: No rainfall alerts for Andhra as depression to turn severe cyclonic storm over Bay of Bengal by November 17
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department reported that a low-pressure area over the Southeast Bay of Bengal intensified into a depression on November 15, 2026. Currently located hundreds of kilometres from Port Blair and Chennai, the system is projected to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17. Authorities in Andhra Pradesh have not yet issued rainfall alerts for the system.
articles.description: At 5.30 a.m., the system lay centred over southeast and southwest Bay of Bengal, about 700 km west-southwest of Port Blair

articles.headline: India Meteorological Department forecasts heavy rain for coastal Andhra Pradesh from upcoming cyclone
articles.title: Cyclone may bring isolated heavy rain to Andhra Pradesh from November 18 to 20
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department forecasted heavy rainfall and gusty winds reaching up to fifty kilometers per hour for coastal Andhra Pradesh from November 18 to 20. A low-pressure system over the southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by November 16, prompting authorities to advise fishermen to return to the coasts by November 15 due to rough sea conditions.
articles.description: According to the IMD’s afternoon bulletin, heavy rain is likely at one or two places in coastal Andhra Pradesh and gusty winds, with speed reaching 40-50 kmph, on November 18, 19 and 20.

articles.headline: Bay of Bengal depression projected to intensify into severe cyclonic storm
articles.title: Depression likely to become cyclone, move towards A.P.; Tamil Nadu, Odisha to get rain: IMD
articles.summary: The meteorological department announced on November 15, 2026, that a depression over the Bay of Bengal will likely intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17. Rain is expected in northern Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal, following rainfall recorded in districts including Chengalpattu, Chennai, Kancheepuram, and Kanyakumari over the preceding 24 hours.
articles.description: If Cyclone Akvan, as the storm is being called, makes landfall in Andhra Pradesh, it will be the third cyclone within a month to hit the State

articles.headline: Low-pressure area forms over southeast Bay of Bengal
articles.title: Low-pressure area forms over Bay of Bengal, likely to intensify into depression by November 15
articles.summary: A low-pressure area has formed over the southeast Bay of Bengal and is expected to intensify into a depression by November 15, 2026, according to the India Meteorological Department. The system developed under the influence of an upper-air cyclonic circulation and is predicted to bring squally weather and strong winds to the Andaman Sea and surrounding regions.
articles.description: The system formed at 5:30 a.m. under the influence of an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the central Andaman Sea and adjoining Andaman and Nicobar Islands, according to the latest weather update

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu government withdraws six hundred cases against farmers and teachers
articles.title: Tamil Nadu government withdraws 600 cases against farmers and teachers
articles.summary: Authorities in Tamil Nadu issued orders on November 16, 2026, to drop six hundred protest-related cases filed against ninety-two thousand farmers and teachers between May 2021 and April 2026. According to an official release, the move follows a suo motu announcement made by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in the Assembly on September 2, 2026.
articles.description: The orders follow Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s suo motu announcement in the Assembly on September 2, 2026

articles.headline: PDP criticises six-day security restrictions in south Kashmir's Kulgam
articles.title: Six days of restrictions in Kulgam reminiscent of 1990s, people facing collective hardships: PDP's Sartaj Madani
articles.summary: Opposition Peoples Democratic Party leader Sartaj Madani condemned a six-day anti-terror operation in Kulgam on November 16, 2026, stating that movement restrictions in Akhran created fear and hardship. Restrictions were imposed after a November 11 attack on a Central Reserve Police Force checkpoint. Madani also criticised the ruling National Conference for remaining silent on civilian difficulties.
articles.description: Parts of south Kashmir’s Kulgam were placed under restrictions following a terrorist attack on a CRPF checkpoint at Akhran

articles.headline: Rising job cuts and tech layoffs spark debate over employee reskilling responsibilities
articles.title: Layoffs and retrenchment: why 15 days’ wages is not enough for employee reskilling
articles.summary: Following significant workforce reductions by companies such as Tata Consultancy Services, which cut approximately 23,000 net jobs by March 2026, technology professionals face growing job insecurity. As global tech layoffs reached about 1.22 lakh and India's attrition rate climbed to 18% in 2026, desk-job employees are increasingly funding their own reskilling certifications amidst a broader economic downturn.
articles.description: Reskilling has become the default answer to a layoff. Amid prevalent instability, few ask the lawyer’s question: is reskilling the individual’s responsibility or a collective one?

articles.headline: United States reverses cuts to fund United Nations military support in Somalia
articles.title: In reversal, U.S. to fund UN military support in Somalia for another year
articles.summary: The United States State Department announced on November 15, 2026, that it will renew funding for United Nations and African Union military support missions in Somalia for another year. The reversal cancels planned shutdowns and aims to prevent regional security crises, following Washington cuts driven by frustration with local political instability and Al-Shabaab insurgents.
articles.description: The Al-Qaeda-linked Al-Shabaab has been fighting the Somali government for two decades and continues to control large swathes of central Somalia despite the African Union military campaign, which was unlikely to be able to continue without UNSOS support.

articles.headline: Congress demands independent SIT reporting to Supreme Court over temple donations
articles.title: Ram temple donation theft: Congress seeks new SIT reporting exclusively to Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Indian National Congress party demanded a new, independent Special Investigation Team reporting directly to the Supreme Court of India to investigate the Ram temple donation theft in Ayodhya. Speaking on November 16, 2026, party officials criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi and alleged that government authorities attempted to shield individuals associated with the ruling political establishment by misleading both the public and the judiciary regarding the ongoing inquiries.
articles.description: Congress said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s “silence” on the issue is “deeply troubling” to the nation and asserted that those who have betrayed people’s faith must be held accountable

articles.headline: Rajasthan holds final phase of panchayat polls across 25 districts
articles.title: Voting underway for final phase of panchayat polls in Rajasthan
articles.summary: Elections for the fourth and final phase of panch and sarpanch posts commenced across 3,747 gram panchayats in 25 districts of Rajasthan on November 16, 2026. Over 1.05 crore eligible voters participated at 11,905 polling stations starting at 7 a.m. Voting concluded at 6 p.m., with ballot counting for ward panch seats and sarpanch positions scheduled to begin immediately afterward.
articles.description: More than 1.05 crore voters are eligible to exercise their franchise at 11,905 polling stations. Long queues of voters were seen at several polling stations since morning

articles.headline: Police detain activists before Israel technology event in Hyderabad
articles.title: SIO activists detained in pre-dawn swoop before Israel-T-Hub event in Hyderabad
articles.summary: Mir Chowk police detained members of the Students Islamic Organisation of India during a pre-dawn operation following opposition to a delegation of Israeli companies visiting T-Hub in Hyderabad. The technology incubator event aims to foster business collaborations, though local activists and rights organisations have raised serious concerns regarding military links.
articles.description: Incidentally, the Israeli delegation’s visit and the collaboration does not show up on the schedule of T-Hub, while the schedule is reported in tech-websites.

articles.headline: Martine Moise registers as candidate for Haiti presidential election
articles.title: Widow of Haiti’s slain leader Moise to contest presidential vote
articles.summary: Martine Moise, widow of assassinated Haitian President Jovenel Moise, registered as a candidate for the presidential election scheduled for July 2027. Her candidacy follows years of repeated delays driven by severe gang violence and political instability that have displaced 1.5 million people and caused over 22,000 deaths. She joins thirty-two other registered candidates, including former presidents and prime ministers, as international forces assist local authorities in combating armed groups.
articles.description: Martine Moise is one of ​33 registered candidates running in Haiti's first presidential election in a decade.

articles.headline: Karnataka government notifies amended BMLTA Act to protect infrastructure projects
articles.title: BMLTA Amendment notified: Tunnel Roads, Elevated Corridors to evade institutional scrutiny
articles.summary: The Karnataka government notified the Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority Amendment Act on October 9, 2026, retrospectively shielding urban transport projects initiated between 2022 and mid-2026 from institutional scrutiny. Passed during the August monsoon session without debate, the legislation incorporates a controversial savings clause that exempts initiatives like tunnel roads and elevated corridors from the transport planning authority, drawing sharp criticism and pending legal challenges from civic groups.
articles.description: The provision of the Section retrospectively validates decisions and actions relating to projects initiated between the adoption of the BMLTA Act in 2022 and the notification of the 2026 Rules, deeming them to have been undertaken under the Act

articles.headline: Mumbai youth linked to Lawrence Bishnoi gang arrested for reconnaissance
articles.title: Youth held for recce of Jewish establishments was recruited by suspected Bishnoi gang associate arrested in Keralam: police
articles.summary: Mumbai resident Yash Singh was arrested by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad for conducting reconnaissance of Jewish establishments, including the Chabad House. Transferred to Kerala police custody on November 15, 2026, Singh was allegedly recruited by Gurumoorthi, a suspected associate of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang previously arrested in Ottapalam. Investigators are also probing potential connections between this case and a recent synagogue-adjacent arson incident investigated by the National Investigation Agency.
articles.description: Yash Singh (20), a native of Navi Mumbai, was arrested by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) for allegedly conducting reconnaissance of Jewish establishments, including Chabad House in Mumbai

articles.headline: India faces sustainability challenges amid massive global rice exports
articles.title: Rebalancing India’s Rice economy: exports, virtual water, emissions and the groundwater challenge
articles.summary: India produced 154.02 million tonnes of rice in the 2025-26 period, maintaining its position as the world's largest exporter with shipments totaling 21.57 million tonnes worth $11.54 billion. Experts from the Institute for Social and Economic Change and the International Rice Research Institute argue that policymakers must address heavy groundwater depletion, virtual water trade, and greenhouse gas emissions.
articles.description: India has proved its competitiveness in global rice markets and the next challenge is to make that competitiveness sustainable; the country’s rice policy needs a more differentiated production strategy that moves from volume to value: more crop per drop, more income per tonne, and less energy use per unit exported

articles.headline: Stock markets rebound in early trade driven by foreign fund inflows
articles.title: Stock markets rally in early trade led by foreign fund inflows, lower crude oil
articles.summary: Indian equity benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty rebounded in early trade on November 16, 2026, driven by sustained foreign fund inflows and lower crude oil prices. The BSE Sensex climbed 414.36 points, while the NSE Nifty rallied 102.10 points. According to experts, strong capital inflows and better-than-expected corporate earnings growth support this market outperformance.
articles.description: The 30-share BSE Sensex climbed 414.36 points to 82,010.15 in early trade and the 50-share NSE Nifty rallied 102.10 points to 25,252.50

articles.headline: Martine Moise registers as a presidential candidate in Haiti
articles.title: Wife of assassinated ex-Haitian leader registers for presidential election
articles.summary: Martine Moise, the widow of assassinated former Haitian president Jovenel Moise, registered as a presidential candidate for upcoming elections in the Caribbean nation. She was injured in the 2021 attack that killed her husband. Haiti has faced chronic gang violence and instability, with elections postponed until July due to insecurity according to officials.
articles.description: There has not been an election in Haiti since before the death of Jovenel Moise in 2021.

articles.headline: Kataib Hezbollah denies involvement in oil smuggling in Iraq
articles.title: Iraqi armed group denies involvement in oil smuggling, calls probe a ‘lie’
articles.summary: The Iran-aligned armed faction Kataib Hezbollah denied involvement in an oil smuggling operation in Iraq's Jurf al-Nasr area. The denial followed an anticorruption crackdown where Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior officials. The group accused the prime minister's office of fabricating lies under pressure from Washington, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates.
articles.description: Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah says the group is subjected to 'blackmail' to force disarmament amid US pressure on Iraq.

articles.headline: Megaspeed confirms Alice Huang left executive role last year
articles.title: Megaspeed, firm at centre of Nvidia scandal, says Alice Huang left in 2025
articles.summary: Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed confirmed that tech executive Alice Huang departed her executive role on August 30, 2025. The company faces scrutiny over United States export controls concerning Nvidia graphics processing units. Singaporean authorities are investigating Megaspeed for suspected false declarations, and the Ministry of Home Affairs barred Huang from re-entering the country.
articles.description: Chinese tech executive romantically linked to ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left in August 2025, Singapore-based firm says.

articles.headline: Indonesian president apologises to Singapore and Malaysia for wildfire haze
articles.title: Indonesian president apologises to Singapore, Malaysia for wildfire haze
articles.summary: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto issued a formal apology during the ASEAN summit in Manila regarding severe transboundary haze originating from prolonged domestic wildfires. According to a presidential statement, Jakarta maintains a strict enforcement approach against responsible commercial entities, having revoked seventeen permits and initiated numerous formal investigations. Meanwhile, regional meteorological services recently reported temporary relief from the smoke across affected Southeast Asian territories.
articles.description: Prabowo says his government has a 'zero-tolerance policy' for firms that contribute to blazes and pledges strict action.

articles.headline: Indian grandmaster Arjun Erigaisi eliminated from Total Chess World Championship Tour
articles.title: Tata Chess Pilot: Vaishali defeats Arjun Erigaisi; all three Indians are out of championship race
articles.summary: Indian Grandmaster Arjun Erigaisi missed qualification for the championship knockout stage following a defeat against compatriot R Vaishali during the final group matches in Budapest. Despite early success, Erigaisi placed third in Group D as Maxime Vachier-Lagrave advanced instead. All three Indian competitors failed to reach the main bracket, directing their focus toward upcoming classification encounters against international opponents in their respective playoff brackets.
articles.description: Magnus Carlsen ended the group stage without a win. Carlsen is now down to 2801.2 and in danger of dropping below 2800 for the first time in more than 15 years

articles.headline: Shophouse fire kills at least 11 in Phuket
articles.title: Shophouse fire kills at least 11 in Phuket
articles.description: Fire engulfed buildings in Thailand’s popular tourist town of Patong, killing several people and injuring many others.

articles.headline: New book examines Jawaharlal Nehru through intelligence chief Bhola Nath Mullik
articles.title: Jawaharlal Nehru through an intelligence prism
articles.summary: A recently published analysis explores the professional relationship between India's inaugural Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and his longtime intelligence leader, Bhola Nath Mullik. Mullik directed the Intelligence Bureau from 1950 until shortly following Nehru's passing, operating as the principal authority on national security matters before the establishment of modern external intelligence agencies. The publication highlights a rarely examined operational dimension of the administration.
articles.description: Critics of Jawaharlal Nehru have spared no effort to portray him as being rosy-eyed and naive about China; yet, memoirs of Bhola Nath Mullik, the intelligence chief who served under Nehru for almost the entire duration his Prime Ministership make it clear this was far from the truth

articles.headline: Indian Army troops open fire following suspicious border movement in Poonch
articles.title: Army opens fire after suspicious movement near LoC in J&K’s Poonch
articles.summary: Military personnel deployed along the Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir discharged roughly two dozen small arms rounds after detecting suspicious activity within a forest zone. Defense representatives stated that vigilant border guards in the Sawjian sector initiated the tactical response to prevent potential militant infiltration from across the international boundary. A comprehensive search operation commenced at dawn and remains actively underway across the cordoned territory.
articles.description: A search operation was launched with the first light of the day and it was underway when last reports were received, the officials said

articles.headline: Notorious Mexican drug lord Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies in hospital at age 80
articles.title: Mexican drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo dies age 80
articles.summary: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, founder of the Guadalajara Cartel and a pioneer of international drug smuggling alliances, died in a Guadalajara hospital at age 80. Known as The Godfather, he orchestrated partnerships with Colombian cartels during the 1980s cocaine boom. He had remained in state custody since his arrest in 1989 following the murder of Drug Enforcement Administration agent Enrique Camarena.
articles.description: Known as the 'Boss of Bosses', he was the head of all-powerful Guadalajara Cartel in the 1980s before his arrest broke up his drug organisation.

articles.headline: Australian MP Helen Haines discharged from hospital after car attack
articles.title: Australian MP 'full of gratitude' upon leaving hospital after alleged car attack
articles.summary: Independent Australian politician Helen Haines has left the Alfred Hospital following four weeks of treatment and multiple surgeries after she was allegedly struck by a vehicle outside her Wangaratta office on October 19. Brendan Nugent faces multiple charges regarding the incident, while Victoria Police continue their ongoing investigation into the attack.
articles.description: The MP lost both of her legs after the alleged attack outside her electorate office four weeks ago.

articles.headline: Six-year-old girl goes missing from school in Panchkula district
articles.title: Panchkula school attack: Ringing the school bell, raising a safety alarm
articles.summary: A six-year-old girl went missing from her school in Haryana’s Panchkula district on October 28, 2026. Her school bag was found at the reception area when the auto-rickshaw driver arrived to pick her up. Family members and teachers searched the building before a boy directed her father to a first-floor classroom, where he was told someone had beaten her up, according to the report.
articles.description: A six-year-old girl was allegedly assaulted by an eight-year-old classmate in a classroom in Panchkula, with CCTV footage capturing the attack. The incident raises concerns about school safety, supervision, and the influence of violent video games on children

articles.headline: Odisha signs tripartite agreement for desalination project in Gopalpur
articles.title: Tripartite agreement signed for ₹1,000-crore desalination project in Odisha
articles.summary: The Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation, the International Finance Corporation, and the Odisha government have signed a tripartite agreement for a ₹1,000-crore desalination project in Gopalpur. The public-private partnership initiative will produce 100 million litres of water daily for industries, supporting regional economic development and infrastructure investment goals across the state.
articles.description: Eleven projects worth around ₹15,498 crore, identified as part of the collaboration with IFC, were granted in-principle were approval by State’s Empowered Committee on Infrastructure

articles.headline: ASEAN and China fail to conclude South China Sea code of conduct
articles.title: ASEAN, China fall short of agreeing on South China Sea code
articles.summary: During meetings in Manila, China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations failed to finalize a long-negotiated code of conduct for the South China Sea. Philippine Foreign Minister Theresa Lazaro stated that key issues remain unresolved, including whether the agreement will be legally binding. Separately, the bloc extended its ban on Myanmar leaders attending annual summits.
articles.description: Southeast Asian leaders also denounce violence in Myanmar and extend ban on country's leader attending bloc's summits.

articles.headline: Pope Leo XIV condemns Amazon deforestation and murders of Indigenous leaders
articles.title: Pope condemns murders of Peru’s Indigenous leaders, deforestation of Amazon
articles.summary: During his tour of South America, Pope Leo XIV met with Indigenous communities in the Peruvian city of Pucallpa to denounce the environmental destruction of the Amazon rainforest. The pontiff demanded justice for the dozens of Indigenous leaders killed while defending their territories from illegal mining and logging, while noting that the Peruvian Amazon lost approximately 200,000 hectares of natural forest in 2025.
articles.description: Pontiff says he supports Indigenous efforts to protect their lands, demands justice for slain environmental defenders.

articles.headline: Pope urges end to Amazon deforestation
articles.title: Pope urges end to Amazon deforestation
articles.description: Pope Leo XIV warns deforestation and illegal mining are threatening the Amazon rainforest and the local communities.

articles.headline: Apple launches health research study to evaluate conversational artificial intelligence tools
articles.title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
articles.summary: Apple announced the Apple HealthAI Usage Study in collaboration with clinical platform OpenEvidence to evaluate how users interact with conversational medical tools. Seeking up to 200,000 United States participants aged 21 and older using an iPhone 15 Pro, the research aims to improve tool design and ensure responses remain accurate and understandable while protecting user confidentiality.
articles.description: Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are. The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical […]

articles.headline: West Bengal police kill shooting suspect during an arrest attempt
articles.title: In latest ‘encounter’, West Bengal police kill a man accused of shooting at a constable two days ago
articles.summary: A man accused of shooting a police constable in West Bengal was killed in a gunfight with law enforcement on November 15, 2026. The suspect, Ratan Sheikh, was cornered at a brick kiln in Nanoor while evading arrest for allegedly injuring constable Biswajit Das two days prior. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari defended the police action, asserting that criminals have no place in the state.
articles.description: This is the fifth instance of an accused killed in police firing in West Bengal, within six months of the BJP coming to power in the State; this was an “extrajudicial execution”, says civil society group

articles.headline: Bangladesh clothing factories shut down as workers strike over minimum wage
articles.title: Clothing factories shut in Bangladesh as workers strike over pay
articles.summary: Nearly one hundred fifty garment production sites across industrial hubs in Savar, Ashulia, and Gazipur suspended operations after employees walked off the job demanding an increase to thirty thousand taka monthly. Protesters blocked the Dhaka-Tangail highway before police intervention. Industry leaders warn that continued unrest threatens international supply chains for global brands like H&M and Zara.
articles.description: Workers are striking over demands for a minimum wage of 30,000 taka (£182) a month.

articles.headline: Guadalajara cartel founder Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies in hospital at age 80
articles.title: Founder of Guadalajara cartel dies in hospital after decades in prison
articles.summary: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, who founded the Guadalajara cartel and was imprisoned since 1989 for crimes including the 1985 killing of a United States drug enforcement agent, has died at age 80 from multiple organ failure at a hospital in Guadalajara. Local security authorities confirmed his death after he was transferred from a maximum-security prison due to declining health.
articles.description: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo was convicted of the 1985 murder of a US drug enforcement agent and a Mexican pilot.

articles.headline: Czechs rally against gov’t threat to media independence
articles.title: Czechs rally against gov’t threat to media independence
articles.description: Czechs rallied in Prague over plans to shift public media funding to the state, raising fears of government influence.

articles.headline: Russian billionaires quietly contemplate political future after Vladimir Putin's departure
articles.title: Russia's mega-rich are already imagining a future after Putin
articles.summary: Some members of Russia's ultra-rich business elite are privately considering a post-Putin political landscape following decades of strict Kremlin control. According to analyst Arkady Ostrovsky, Western sanctions and domestic limitations have left tycoons with minimal political influence. Although President Vladimir Putin has served for twenty-five years, uncertainty remains over potential leadership succession and future economic conditions.
articles.description: Some Russian tycoons are pining after a return to a 1990s system of oligarchy, when businessmen enjoyed power.

articles.headline: Libyan city of Derna undergoes rapid two billion dollar reconstruction
articles.title: Town rebuilt after devastating floods becomes showcase for Libyan strongman's rule
articles.summary: Eastern Libya is utilizing a two billion dollar state-allocated fund to rapidly rebuild Derna following catastrophic floods in September 2023 that killed thousands. While many survivors have received free new housing in developments commissioned by Belkacem Haftar, international critics and rights groups have raised serious concerns regarding financial transparency, public accountability, and the absolute lack of published spending records.
articles.description: The remarkable reconstruction of Derna is being used as a showcase for the rest of Libya by Khalifa Haftar and his sons.

articles.headline: Astronomers discover unusual pair of distant quasars in the early universe
articles.title: Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified a strange pair of quasars located just 18,100 light-years apart when the universe was only 900 million years old. Officially designated as J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, the discovery was studied using the James Webb Space Telescope and the Gemini North telescope in Hawaii, leaving scientists investigating how such massive black holes could have formed so early.
articles.description: Two celestial bodies—Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua—are a close pair of ancient quasars challenging ideas about early black hole growth

articles.headline: Zambia attracts billions in mining investments while local workers question benefits
articles.title: Zambia’s copper boom attracts billions in investment, but who benefits?
articles.summary: President Hakainde Hichilema announced that Zambia has secured over 12 billion dollars in mining investments since 2022 to expand copper production for the global energy transition. Major firms like First Quantum Minerals and International Resources Holding are driving the sector. However, trade unions report that local mineworkers have experienced no improvements in employment conditions amid rising operational costs.
articles.description: Workers' rights, environmental concerns and local businesses remain at the centre of the debate.

articles.headline: Mirra Andreeva wins WTA Finals title after defeating Elina Svitolina in Indian Wells
articles.title: Teenager Andreeva caps stunning week with WTA Finals title
articles.summary: Nineteen-year-old tennis player Mirra Andreeva defeated Elina Svitolina in straight sets to capture the WTA Finals singles championship in California. The Russian competitor did not drop a single set throughout the tournament, securing two million five hundred fifty thousand pounds in prize money alongside a custom vehicle. Following this victory, Andreeva rose to second place in the world rankings.
articles.description: French Open champion Mirra Andreeva caps her stellar season with a hard-fought victory over Elina Svitolina to win the WTA Finals.

articles.headline: Thirteen-year-old boy confirmed as fourth Indian fatality in UAE crash
articles.title: 13-year-old boy identified as fourth Indian killed in UAE road accident
articles.summary: A 13-year-old boy from Gujarat named Aatif Mohmmed Imran Mansur was identified by authorities as the fourth Indian killed in a massive 23-vehicle road accident in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, on November 12, 2026. According to the UAE Ministry of Interior, the disaster left 14 people dead and 30 injured, including the boy's parents and sister who received hospital treatment.
articles.description: The accident involved 23 vehicles, including trucks, and left 30 people injured

articles.headline: Steering failure preceded New Orleans cruise ship collision
articles.title: Steering failure preceded New Orleans cruise ship collision, says NTSB
articles.summary: An asphalt cargo vessel experienced a steering casualty before striking a docked riverboat on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday, according to National Transportation Safety Board findings released on Sunday. The collision injured 32 people from the American Heritage riverboat, which carried 129 passengers and listed before tipping onto its side.
articles.description: Preliminary findings by National Transportation Safety Board investigators suggest the tanker suffered a "steering casualty" before colliding with the cruise ship on Friday.

articles.headline: England defeat Spain to claim top spot in UEFA Nations League
articles.title: England stun Spain to end La Roja’s 43-game unbeaten run
articles.summary: England secured a dramatic victory against Spain in Madrid on November 16, 2026, finishing first in Group A3 on goal difference despite playing with ten men following Elliott Anderson's red card. Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa, and Ben White scored for the visitors before Nico Williams and Mikel Oyarzabal responded for the hosts in a tense finish.
articles.description: Spain suffer first defeat since March 2024 after losing 3-2 to England in Madrid despite grandstand finish.

articles.headline: Paris police ban demonstrations near educational institutions amid ongoing protests
articles.title: Police ban protests near 10 schools and five universities in Paris
articles.summary: Paris police issued a five-day ban on protests near 10 secondary schools and five universities from November 16 to 20, 2026. Paris police chief Patrice Faure cited persistent violence and blockades that damaged public property and injured educational staff. Authorities reported that 1,548 people have been arrested in Paris since demonstrations began in September.
articles.description: The order will be in place from 16 to 20 November, Paris police chief Patrice Faure says.

articles.headline: Yemen’s Houthis unilaterally release 600 war detainees
articles.title: Yemen’s Houthis unilaterally release 600 war detainees
articles.description: Yemen’s Houthis have released 600 people imprisoned during the country’s civil war.

articles.headline: Thousands of Czech protesters rally against public media funding changes
articles.title: Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media
articles.summary: Thousands of Czech citizens gathered in Prague on Sunday to protest government plans to replace public media license fees with state budget funding. Organisers from the Million Moments for Democracy association estimated attendance at roughly 400,000 people. Critics argue the legislation threatens media freedom, while the coalition government led by Prime Minister Andrej Babis insists editorial independence will remain unaffected.
articles.description: Protesters say the move will stifle media freedom, while the government insists broadcasters need to cut costs.

articles.headline: Estonia to close border crossings with Russia after alleged arson attack
articles.title: Estonia to close border crossings with Russia after alleged arson attack
articles.description: Estonia is closing its border crossings with Russia following an alleged arson attempt at a drone factory.

articles.headline: Jordan sentences three men to death over deadly church attack in Karak
articles.title: Jordan sentences three men to death over deadly church attack in Karak
articles.description: Jordan sentences three men to death over deadly church attack in Karak

articles.headline: Bilkis Bano reflects on her life struggle at Kochi women conference
articles.title: My entire life has been a struggle, says Bilkis Bano at GIO conference in Kochi
articles.summary: Gujarat riots survivor Bilkis Bano stated that her entire existence has been a struggle while inaugurating the International Conference on Women in Kochi on November 15, 2026. Speaking at the event organized by the Girls Islamic Organisation, she reflected on her prolonged legal battle for justice following the 2002 riots where she was gang-raped and lost seven family members, highlighting an ongoing journey that her husband Patel Yakub Rasool noted involved multiple relocations and denied rights.
articles.description: Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage.

articles.headline: West Bengal BJP chief warns Christian missionary schools over conversions
articles.title: West Bengal BJP president alleges conversions at missionary schools; draws flak
articles.summary: West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party chief Samik Bhattacharya warned Christian missionary schools on November 15, 2026, alleging religious conversions and anti-India activities. The Bangiya Christiya Pariseba urged him to publicly name the institutions. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari accused the previous government of exclusively recognizing Muslims as a minority, asserting that Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains also qualify.
articles.description: This is the first time a senior State BJP leader has made remarks about the community, even as Christian groups have protested against attacks on churches

articles.headline: Traditional Kashmiri wazwan feasts linked to rising diabetes cases
articles.title: As diabetes spikes in Kashmir, the health lens turns to the fabled wazwan
articles.summary: High-calorie Kashmiri wazwan feasts are a key cultural factor driving a sharp rise in diabetes across Jammu and Kashmir, according to experts and a new book released on November 14, 2026. Ministry data indicates millions were screened, adding over two lakh new patients in three years. Authors attributed the surge to sedentary winters, rice-centric meals, and rapid urbanization.
articles.description: Subsistence agriculture and labour-intensive living has been replaced by urbanisation and declining physical activity, while traditional dietary patterns persist largely unchanged, the doctor-authors of Diabetes Simplified for Kashmir say
